NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | """
    2 | L0 low-level client for the GRFICS Tennessee-Eastman simulator.
    3 | 
    4 | The simulator (simulation/simulation/main.cc) is a C++ process that listens on
    5 | TCP 55555 and speaks line-delimited JSON:
    6 | 
    7 |     read :  {"request":"read"}\\n
    8 |             -> {"process":..., "outputs":{...}, "state":{...}, "measured":{...}}
    9 | 
   10 |     write:  {"request":"write","data":{"inputs":{ <name>: <value>, ... }}}\\n
   11 |             -> same state object, post-update
   12 | 
   13 | Accepted input names include the four valve setpoints (f1_valve_sp, f2_valve_sp,
   14 | purge_valve_sp, product_valve_sp), e_stop, and the fault-injection parameters.
   15 | Setpoints are in physical percent [0,100] - the simulator does the 0-65535
   16 | scaling internally, so this client stays in engineering units.
   17 | 
   18 | This client is deliberately thin: it owns the socket and the JSON framing and
   19 | nothing else. Safety logic lives one layer up in safety.py so the interlock is
   20 | independent of transport.
   21 | """
   22 | 
   23 | from __future__ import annotations
   24 | 
   25 | import json
   26 | import socket
   27 | from typing import Optional
   28 | 
   29 | 
   30 | class GrficsClient:
   31 |     def __init__(self, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 55555,
   32 |                  timeout: float = 2.0):
   33 |         self.host = host
   34 |         self.port = port
   35 |         self.timeout = timeout
   36 |         self._sock: Optional[socket.socket] = None
   37 |         self._f = None
   38 | 
   39 |     def connect(self) -> "GrficsClient":
   40 |         self._sock = socket.create_connection((self.host, self.port),
   41 |                                                timeout=self.timeout)
   42 |         # makefile gives us readline() framing for the newline-delimited protocol
   43 |         self._f = self._sock.makefile(mode="rwb")
   44 |         return self
   45 | 
   46 |     def close(self) -> None:
   47 |         try:
   48 |             if self._f:
   49 |                 self._f.close()
   50 |         finally:
   51 |             if self._sock:
   52 |                 self._sock.close()
   53 |             self._sock = None
   54 |             self._f = None
   55 | 
   56 |     def __enter__(self):
   57 |         return self.connect()
   58 | 
   59 |     def __exit__(self, *exc):
   60 |         self.close()
   61 | 
   62 |     def _txn(self, msg: dict) -> dict:
   63 |         if not self._f:
   64 |             raise RuntimeError("GrficsClient not connected; call connect()")
   65 |         self._f.write((json.dumps(msg) + "\n").encode())
   66 |         self._f.flush()
   67 |         line = self._f.readline()
   68 |         if not line:
   69 |             raise ConnectionError("simulator closed the connection")
   70 |         return json.loads(line.decode())
   71 | 
   72 |     def read(self) -> dict:
   73 |         """Return the raw state object from the simulator."""
   74 |         return self._txn({"request": "read"})
   75 | 
   76 |     def write_inputs(self, inputs: dict) -> dict:
   77 |         """Send one or more named inputs; returns the post-update state."""

    2 | L0 plant service.
    3 | 
    4 | This is the clean boundary the rest of SCRAM sees. It:
    5 |   * wraps the GRFICS socket client,
    6 |   * translates raw simulator JSON into the shared PlantState contract,
    7 |   * runs the independent SafetyInterlock every cycle and, when tripped,
    8 |     overrides the incoming ControlCommand to force the plant safe.
    9 | 
   10 | Everything above L0 talks to this class, never to GrficsClient directly.
   11 | 
   12 | Note on the real/measured split: the simulator reports both the true physical
   13 | values ("outputs") and the sensor-faulted values ("measured"). L0 publishes the
   14 | MEASURED values as the live state (that is what a PLC/HMI really sees) and
   15 | tucks the truth into PlantState.truth for eval only.
   16 | 
   17 | The safety interlock is the one exception: it evaluates "outputs", modeled as
   18 | a dedicated safety-instrumented sensor path independent of the basic control
   19 | system, not "measured" (the basic control system's own instrumentation). A
   20 | fault injected via l0_plant/fault_injection.py only ever touches "measured",
   21 | so it can corrupt what L1/L2/L3 see in PlantState without being able to stop
   22 | the interlock from tripping. This assumes standard SIS independence: the
   23 | safety-instrumented path is out of the attacker's reach - see ARCHITECTURE.md.

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | """
    2 | Command-origin integrity on the actuation path (defensive).
    3 | 
    4 | The enforcer (PlantService) is the ONLY sanctioned writer to the plant
    5 | (port 55555). The physics interlock (safety.py) grounds its veto in the
    6 | process state; this module is the second ground: WHO issued the command. It
    7 | catches the case physics cannot - a command that is individually within every
    8 | physical limit (so the SIS never trips) but was not issued by the authorized
    9 | path.
   10 | 
   11 | Two mechanisms, with different jobs:
   12 | 
   13 | 1. Provenance check (commands that reach the enforcer). L1 signs each command
   14 |    with a shared key (HMAC-SHA256 over a strictly increasing sequence number
   15 |    plus the four valve positions). `ProvenanceGate.admit` rejects a command
   16 |    with a missing/invalid tag or a replayed/stale sequence number, and the
   17 |    enforcer re-asserts the last-good command instead.
   18 | 
   19 | 2. Readback audit (commands that DO NOT reach the enforcer). A write sent
   20 |    straight to the plant socket never passes through admit(), so it can't be
   21 |    prevented from here - the plant's JSON protocol has no authentication.
   22 |    What the enforcer can do is notice: it knows exactly what it last wrote, so
   23 |    any valve position or e_stop state on the plant that differs from that is,
   24 |    by construction, someone else's write. `ProvenanceGate.audit` flags the
   25 |    mismatch and the enforcer re-asserts last-good on its next write. Limits:
   26 |    detection is per control cycle, so an out-of-band write can dwell for up
   27 |    to one cycle; it is detected and bounded, not prevented. Preventing it
   28 |    needs network-level controls (only the enforcer host may reach 55555) -
   29 |    outside this code.
   30 | 
   31 | Key handling: the key is supplied by the caller (e.g. from the environment);
   32 | nothing here ships a default key.
   33 | """

  112 |

  114 |         """
  115 |         The enforcer is releasing e_stop. The plant's valves are where e_stop

  126 | 
  127 |     def note_safe_state(self, inputs: dict) -> None:
  128 |         """
  129 |         Record what the interlock's cause-specific safe state wrote, so the
  130 |         audit expects it (e_stop for pressure/high level; product closed with
  131 |         the other valves held for low level).
  132 |         """
  133 |         self.expect_e_stop = bool(inputs.get("e_stop", 0))
  134 |         if not self.expect_e_stop and self.last_good is not None:
  135 |             # every valve the safe state wrote (product only for low level; the whole
  136 |             # lineup for the closed-loop safe-hold) is now what the plant should show

  139 |             if held:

  141 | 
  142 |     def audit(self, plant_state: dict) -> List[str]:
  143 |         """
  144 |         Compare the plant's own readback (raw["state"]) with what the enforcer
  145 |         last wrote. Returns the mismatches (empty = clean). Valve positions
  146 |         are not compared while e_stop is the expected state, since e_stop
  147 |         deliberately overrides them.
  148 |         """
  149 |         found: List[str] = []
  150 |         if bool(plant_state.get("e_stop", False)) != self.expect_e_stop:
  151 |             found.append(f"e_stop is {plant_state.get('e_stop')} but enforcer expects {self.expect_e_stop}")
  152 |         if not self.expect_e_stop and self.last_good is not None:
  153 |             want = (self.last_good.f1_valve, self.last_good.f2_valve,
  154 |                     self.last_good.purge_valve, self.last_good.product_valve)
  155 |             for k, w in zip(VALVE_KEYS, want):
  156 |                 got = float(plant_state.get(k, w))

  159 |         for f in found:
  160 |             self._event("out_of_band_write", f)
  161 |         return found

SafetyInterlock.safe_state_inputs | L165-198
Simulator write-inputs that put the plant in the safe state for the
latched trip cause. The right safe state depends on the hazard:

  * pressure_high / level_high: e_stop (feeds shut, purge and product
    open) - relieves pressure and drains an overfull vessel.
  * level_low: e_stop would OPEN the product valve and keep draining a
    vessel that is already too low. Instead close product to stop the
    drain and leave the feed/purge valves where they are (they are
    simply not written, so the simulator holds them) so inflow and
    reaction make the level recover toward the re-arm band.

With a SafeHold configured and valid safety-channel readings passed in,
pressure_high / level_high run the closed-loop safe-hold lineup instead
of e_stop, escalating (latched) to e_stop on a runaway.

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | """
    2 | L0 hardware safety layer - the independent interlock ("SCRAM").
    3 | 
    4 | This is the bottom of the SCRAM thesis: a last-resort protective layer that
    5 | sits UNDER the AI and cannot be talked out of tripping. It does not know or
    6 | care what L3 intends or how much authority governance granted; it watches a
    7 | handful of physical variables and, if any crosses a hard limit, forces the
    8 | plant into a safe state (feeds shut, relief paths open) by asserting the
    9 | simulator's e_stop.
   10 | 
   11 | Design rules:
   12 |   * Trip logic depends ONLY on physical state, never on upstream intent. The
   13 |     caller (plant_service.py) is responsible for handing this class the
   14 |     reactor's "outputs" - modeled as a dedicated safety-instrumented sensor
   15 |     path, independent of the basic control system - not the "measured" view
   16 |     the basic control system itself sees. This assumes standard SIS
   17 |     independence (the safety-instrumented path is out of the attacker's
   18 |     reach); see ARCHITECTURE.md.
   19 |   * Trips latch. Once tripped, the plant stays safed until an explicit,
   20 |     deliberate reset (a human/operator action in the real thing) AND the
   21 |     variables are back inside the re-arm band - exactly like a real reactor
   22 |     scram that you cannot clear while still over-pressure.
   23 |   * Limits here are protective trip points, set wider than the normal
   24 |     operating envelope L1 regulates within, so the interlock only fires on a
   25 |     genuine excursion - not on routine control action.
   26 |   * A safety-channel reading that is missing or not a finite number trips the
   27 |     interlock (cause "sis_sensor_fault", safe state e_stop): an SIS that cannot
   28 |     read its own sensor fails safe rather than assuming all is well.
   29 |   * Optional closed-loop safe-hold (SafeHold): instead of an e_stop that kills
   30 |     the reaction, a pressure / high-level trip cuts the feeds back and works
   31 |     purge and product on the safety channel until the plant is back inside the
   32 |     re-arm band, still running. It escalates to e_stop on a runaway
   33 |     (pressure >= SafeHold.runaway_kpa) and stays there until reset.
   34 | """

   46 | # Valve lineup of the settled design point (training/design_point.json)
   47 | DESIGN_VALVES = {"f1": 31.45, "f2": 13.24, "purge": 0.39, "product": 47.03}
   48 | 
   49 | 
   50 | @dataclass(frozen=True)
   51 | class SafeHold:
   52 |     """Closed-loop safe-hold law, run by the SIS on its own (safety-channel) readings."""
   53 |     feed_frac: float = 0.6        # feeds cut to this fraction of the design lineup
   54 |     p_target: float = 2650.0      # kPa: purge opens in proportion to pressure above this
   55 |     kp_purge: float = 0.4         # % purge per kPa
   56 |     l_target: float = 50.0        # %: product opens in proportion to level above this
   57 |     kl_product: float = 3.0       # % product per % level
   58 |     runaway_kpa: float = 3050.0   # still climbing past the trip: give up and e_stop
   59 | 
   60 |     def lineup(self, pressure: float, level: float) -> dict:
   61 |         clamp = lambda v: round(max(0.0, min(100.0, v)), 2)
   62 |         d = DESIGN_VALVES
   63 |         return {"e_stop": 0,
   64 |                 "f1_valve_sp": clamp(d["f1"] * self.feed_frac),
   65 |                 "f2_valve_sp": clamp(d["f2"] * self.feed_frac),
   66 |                 "purge_valve_sp": clamp(d["purge"] + self.kp_purge * (pressure - self.p_target)),
   67 |                 "product_valve_sp": clamp(d["product"] * self.feed_frac + self.kl_product * (level - self.l_target))}
   68 | 
   69 | 
   70 | @dataclass(frozen=True)
   71 | class TripLimits:
   72 |     # High reactor pressure is the dominant hazard in this process; the model
   73 |     # itself hard-clamps at 3200 kPa, so trip well below that.
   74 |     pressure_high: float = 3000.0      # kPa
   75 |     # Loss of liquid level risks pump damage / loss of cooling; overfill risks
   76 |     # carryover. Protective band sits outside the normal 30-70% operating range.
   77 |     level_low: float = 5.0             # %
   78 |     level_high: float = 95.0           # %
   79 |     # Re-arm hysteresis: variables must return comfortably inside these before
   80 |     # a latched trip can be cleared.
   81 |     pressure_rearm: float = 2800.0     # kPa
   82 |     level_low_rearm: float = 15.0      # %
   83 |     level_high_rearm: float = 85.0     # %
   84 | 
   85 | 
   86 | class SafetyInterlock:
   87 |     def __init__(self, limits: TripLimits | None = None, safe_hold: SafeHold | None = None):
   88 |         self.limits = limits or TripLimits()
   89 |         self.safe_hold = safe_hold          # None = classic e_stop safe state
   90 |         self.tripped = False
   91 |         self.reason = ""
   92 |         self.cause = ""     # "pressure_high" | "level_low" | "level_high" while latched
   93 |         self.escalated = False              # safe-hold gave up on a runaway: e_stop until reset
   94 |         self._sensor_fault = False
   95 |         self._combined_low_level = False
   96 |         self._pressure_seen = False
   97 | 
   98 |     def evaluate(self, pressure: float, level: float) -> bool:
   99 |         """
  100 |         Update interlock state from the latest measured values.
  101 |         Returns True if the plant should currently be forced safe (scrammed).
  102 |         """
  103 |         lim = self.limits
  104 |         valid = _valid(pressure) and _valid(level)
  105 |         if not self.tripped:
  106 |             if not valid:
  107 |                 self._trip(f"safety-channel reading invalid (pressure={pressure!r}, level={level!r})",
  108 |                            "sis_sensor_fault")
  109 |             elif pressure >= lim.pressure_high:
  110 |                 self._trip(f"pressure {pressure:.0f} >= {lim.pressure_high:.0f} kPa", "pressure_high")
  111 |             elif level <= lim.level_low:
  112 |                 self._trip(f"level {level:.1f}% <= {lim.level_low:.1f}%", "level_low")
  113 |             elif level >= lim.level_high:
  114 |                 self._trip(f"level {level:.1f}% >= {lim.level_high:.1f}%", "level_high")
  115 |         if self.tripped:
  116 |             # Preserve the first cause for diagnosis, but never freeze hazard detection.
  117 |             self._sensor_fault |= not valid
  118 |             if valid:
  119 |                 self._pressure_seen |= pressure >= lim.pressure_high
  120 |                 if level <= lim.level_low and self._pressure_seen:
  121 |                     self._combined_low_level = True
  122 |                 if self.cause == "level_low" and pressure >= lim.pressure_high:
  123 |                     self._combined_low_level = True
  124 |                 if self.cause == "level_low" and level >= lim.level_high:
  125 |                     self.escalated = True
  126 |             self.escalated |= self._sensor_fault or self._combined_low_level
  127 |         return self.tripped
  128 | 
  129 |     def can_reset(self, pressure: float, level: float) -> bool:
  130 |         """Whether a latched trip is eligible to be cleared right now."""
  131 |         lim = self.limits
  132 |         if not (_valid(pressure) and _valid(level)):
  133 |             return False
  134 |         return (pressure <= lim.pressure_rearm
  135 |                 and lim.level_low_rearm <= level <= lim.level_high_rearm)
  136 | 
  137 |     @property
  138 |     def protection_mode(self) -> str:
  139 |         if not self.tripped:
  140 |             return "armed"
  141 |         if self._sensor_fault:
  142 |             return "emergency_stop"
  143 |         if self._combined_low_level:
  144 |             return "combined_hold"
  145 |         if self.cause == "level_low" and not self.escalated:
  146 |             return "inventory_hold"
  147 |         if self.safe_hold is not None and not self.escalated:
  148 |             return "safe_hold"
  149 |         return "emergency_stop"
  150 | 
  151 |     def reset(self, pressure: float, level: float) -> bool:
  152 |         """
  153 |         Deliberate operator reset. Only succeeds if variables are back inside
  154 |         the re-arm band; otherwise the trip stays latched.
  155 |         """
  156 |         if self.tripped and self.can_reset(pressure, level):
  157 |             self.tripped = False
  158 |             self.reason = ""
  159 |             self.cause = ""
  160 |             self.escalated = False
  161 |             self._sensor_fault = self._combined_low_level = self._pressure_seen = False
  162 |             return True
  163 |         return False
  164 | 
  165 |     def safe_state_inputs(self, pressure: float | None = None, level: float | None = None) -> dict:
  166 |         """
  167 |         Simulator write-inputs that put the plant in the safe state for the
  168 |         latched trip cause. The right safe state depends on the hazard:
  169 | 
  170 |           * pressure_high / level_high: e_stop (feeds shut, purge and product
  171 |             open) - relieves pressure and drains an overfull vessel.
  172 |           * level_low: e_stop would OPEN the product valve and keep draining a
  173 |             vessel that is already too low. Instead close product to stop the
  174 |             drain and leave the feed/purge valves where they are (they are
  175 |             simply not written, so the simulator holds them) so inflow and
  176 |             reaction make the level recover toward the re-arm band.
  177 | 
  178 |         With a SafeHold configured and valid safety-channel readings passed in,
  179 |         pressure_high / level_high run the closed-loop safe-hold lineup instead
  180 |         of e_stop, escalating (latched) to e_stop on a runaway.
  181 |         """
  182 |         if self._sensor_fault:
  183 |             return {"e_stop": 1}
  184 |         if self._combined_low_level:
  185 |             # e_stop opens product in this simulator, aggravating the low inventory.
  186 |             # Remove feed energy, vent vapour, and retain the remaining liquid.
  187 |             return {"e_stop": 0, "f1_valve_sp": 0.0, "f2_valve_sp": 0.0,
  188 |                     "purge_valve_sp": 100.0, "product_valve_sp": 0.0}
  189 |         if self.cause == "level_low" and not self.escalated:
  190 |             return {"e_stop": 0, "product_valve_sp": 0.0}
  191 |         hold = self.safe_hold
  192 |         if (hold is not None and self.cause in ("pressure_high", "level_high")
  193 |                 and _valid(pressure) and _valid(level)):
  194 |             if pressure >= hold.runaway_kpa:
  195 |                 self.escalated = True
  196 |             if not self.escalated:
  197 |                 return hold.lineup(pressure, level)
  198 |         return {"e_stop": 1}
  199 | 
  200 |     def _trip(self, reason: str, cause: str) -> None:
  201 |         self.tripped = True
  202 |         self.reason = reason
  203 |         self.cause = cause

    1 | """
    2 | L1 regulatory control: four PI loops that turn SupervisoryTargets into valve
    3 | positions, and the signer that stamps every outgoing command for the
    4 | provenance gate. Replaces l1_stub.py + live/engine.LiveL1 on the live path
    5 | (the offline experiments keep the stub their saved results were produced with).
    6 | 
    7 | Actuator mapping for the TE reactor (primary actuator per variable):
    8 |     pressure    <- purge valve      (open purge -> vent -> pressure falls).
    9 |                    Split range: at the design point purge sits almost shut
   10 |                    (~0.4 %), so when the loop output goes below 0 it raises
   11 |                    both feeds instead: u in [-FEED_SPAN, 0) maps linearly to a
   12 |                    feed trim of 0..+FEED_TRIM_MAX. That is the only way to build
   13 |                    pressure back after a vent / e-stop.
   14 |     level       <- product valve    (open product -> drain -> level falls)
   15 |     production  <- feed 1 valve     feedforward f1 = design f1 x sp/100, plus a
   16 |                    SLOW PI trim on measured product flow
   17 |     A in purge  <- feed 2 valve     (A-rich feed)
   18 | 
   19 | Decoupling is by time scale, not by a model: level is the fast loop on the
   20 | product valve; production only trims feed 1 slowly (outflow follows inflow
   21 | through the level loop at steady state), so the two do not fight. Pressure
   22 | uses purge (and the feeds only when purge is saturated shut); while it trims the
   23 | feeds, the production trim is held, so it neither cuts feed 1 back against the
   24 | pressure build-up nor winds up on the throughput change it causes.
   25 | 
   26 | Units (the L1 seam): valves are percent [0, 100] (contracts.ControlCommand);
   27 | a_comp_sp is mol PERCENT (e.g. 47.0) while the plant reports a_in_purge as a
   28 | mole FRACTION (~0.47) - converted here, in one place (_a_pct).
   29 | 
   30 | Every integrator has conditional-integration anti-windup and every output is
   31 | clamped. Integration uses the real elapsed time the caller passes in (the old
   32 | stub integrated a fixed 0.5 s per ~0.06 s cycle, ~8x too fast). Bumpless
   33 | transfer: bumpless(state) re-seeds every integrator so the next output equals
   34 | the valve positions the plant already holds (call on connect / re-arm); a loop
   35 | whose setpoint goes None (authority 0 = hold) freezes its valve and re-seeds
   36 | itself from that valve when a setpoint returns.
   37 | """

   47 | DESIGN_F1, DESIGN_F2, DESIGN_PURGE, DESIGN_PRODUCT = 31.45, 13.24, 0.3926, 47.03
   48 | DESIGN_PRODUCTION = 100.0
   49 | FEED_TRIM_MAX = 0.50            # split range: feeds may rise at most +50 % to build pressure
   50 | FEED_SPAN = 6.0                 # pressure-loop output units spanning the whole feed-trim range
   51 | 
   52 | # gains: kp in valve-% per unit error, ki in valve-% per unit error per second
   53 | PRESSURE_KP, PRESSURE_KI = 0.30, 0.003       # per kPa (error = measured - setpoint)
   54 | LEVEL_KP, LEVEL_KI = 4.0, 0.04               # per %   (error = measured - setpoint)
   55 | PRODUCTION_KP, PRODUCTION_KI = 0.02, 0.002   # per kmol/h (error = setpoint - measured), slow trim
   56 | COMP_KP, COMP_KI = 1.5, 0.02                 # per mol % (error = setpoint - measured)
   57 | 
   58 | 
   59 | class PI:
   60 |     """u = kp*e + i, clamped to [lo, hi]; the integral only moves when that does
   61 |     not push further into saturation (conditional integration)."""
   62 | 
   63 |     def __init__(self, kp: float, ki: float, lo: float, hi: float, init: float = 0.0):
   64 |         self.kp, self.ki, self.lo, self.hi = kp, ki, lo, hi
   65 |         self.i = init
   66 | 
   67 |     def __call__(self, e: float, dt: float) -> float:
   68 |         u = self.kp * e + self.i
   69 |         if not ((u >= self.hi and e > 0) or (u <= self.lo and e < 0)):
   70 |             self.i += self.ki * e * dt
   71 |         return max(self.lo, min(self.hi, self.kp * e + self.i))
   72 | 
   73 |     def track(self, u: float, e: float = 0.0) -> None:
   74 |         """Bumpless: make the current output equal u."""
   75 |         self.i = u - self.kp * e
   76 | 
   77 | 
   78 | def _a_pct(state) -> float:
   79 |     return state.a_in_purge * 100.0          # fraction -> mol %, the unit a_comp_sp is written in
   80 | 
   81 | 
   82 | class L1Regulator:
   83 |     def __init__(self, key: Optional[bytes] = None):
   84 |         # split-range pressure output: u in [-FEED_SPAN, 100]; u >= 0 is purge %, u < 0 is feed trim
   85 |         self.pressure = PI(PRESSURE_KP, PRESSURE_KI, -FEED_SPAN, 100.0, DESIGN_PURGE)
   86 |         self.level = PI(LEVEL_KP, LEVEL_KI, 0.0, 100.0, DESIGN_PRODUCT)
   87 |         self.production = PI(PRODUCTION_KP, PRODUCTION_KI, -15.0, 15.0, 0.0)   # f1 trim, valve %
   88 |         self.comp = PI(COMP_KP, COMP_KI, 0.0, 100.0, DESIGN_F2)
   89 |         self._prod_out = 0.0
   90 |         self._held = {"pressure": False, "level": False, "production": False, "comp": False}
   91 |         self.signer = CommandSigner(key) if key is not None else None
   92 | 
   93 |     # ---- the four loops ---------------------------------------------------------
   94 |     def regulate(self, targets: SupervisoryTargets, state: PlantState, dt: float) -> ControlCommand:
   95 |         dt = max(0.0, min(float(dt), 1.0))
   96 |         # pressure (split range: purge, then feeds)
   97 |         if self._resume("pressure", targets.pressure_sp, state):
   98 |             u = self.pressure(state.pressure - targets.pressure_sp, dt)
   99 |         else:
  100 |             u = state.purge_valve_pos
  101 |         purge = max(0.0, u)
  102 |         trim = 1.0 + FEED_TRIM_MAX * max(0.0, -u) / FEED_SPAN
  103 |         # level
  104 |         if self._resume("level", targets.level_sp, state):
  105 |             product = self.level(state.level - targets.level_sp, dt)
  106 |         else:
  107 |             product = state.product_valve_pos
  108 |         # production: feedforward + slow trim on feed 1
  109 |         if self._resume("production", targets.production_rate_sp, state):
  110 |             ff = DESIGN_F1 * targets.production_rate_sp / DESIGN_PRODUCTION
  111 |             if trim > 1.0:
  112 |                 # the pressure loop is borrowing the feeds: hold the production trim (do not
  113 |                 # integrate against throughput the feed trim is deliberately changing)
  114 |                 f1 = ff + self._prod_out
  115 |             else:
  116 |                 self._prod_out = self.production(targets.production_rate_sp - state.product_flow, dt)
  117 |                 f1 = ff + self._prod_out
  118 |         else:
  119 |             f1 = state.f1_valve_pos / trim
  120 |         # composition
  121 |         if self._resume("comp", targets.a_comp_sp, state):
  122 |             f2 = self.comp(targets.a_comp_sp - _a_pct(state), dt)
  123 |         else:
  124 |             f2 = state.f2_valve_pos / trim
  125 |         return ControlCommand(f1_valve=f1 * trim, f2_valve=f2 * trim,
  126 |                               purge_valve=purge, product_valve=product).clamped()
  127 | 
  128 |     def _resume(self, loop: str, sp, state: PlantState) -> bool:
  129 |         """None setpoint -> hold this valve. When a setpoint returns after a hold, seed the
  130 |         loop from the valve the plant holds now so the hand-back does not kick."""
  131 |         if sp is None:
  132 |             self._held[loop] = True
  133 |             return False
  134 |         if self._held[loop]:
  135 |             self._held[loop] = False
  136 |             self._seed(loop, state, sp)
  137 |         return True
  138 | 
  139 |     def _seed(self, loop: str, state: PlantState, sp: Optional[float]) -> None:
  140 |         if loop == "pressure":
  141 |             e = 0.0 if sp is None else state.pressure - sp
  142 |             self.pressure.track(state.purge_valve_pos, e)
  143 |         elif loop == "level":
  144 |             e = 0.0 if sp is None else state.level - sp
  145 |             self.level.track(state.product_valve_pos, e)
  146 |         elif loop == "production":
  147 |             q = DESIGN_PRODUCTION if sp is None else sp
  148 |             self._prod_out = state.f1_valve_pos - DESIGN_F1 * q / DESIGN_PRODUCTION
  149 |             self.production.track(self._prod_out, q - state.product_flow)
  150 |         else:
  151 |             e = 0.0 if sp is None else sp - _a_pct(state)
  152 |             self.comp.track(state.f2_valve_pos, e)
  153 | 
  154 |     def bumpless(self, state: PlantState, targets: Optional[SupervisoryTargets] = None) -> None:
  155 |         """Re-seed every loop from the valves the plant holds now (connect, re-arm, reconnect)."""
  156 |         t = targets or SupervisoryTargets()
  157 |         for loop, sp in (("pressure", t.pressure_sp), ("level", t.level_sp),
  158 |                          ("production", t.production_rate_sp), ("comp", t.a_comp_sp)):
  159 |             self._seed(loop, state, sp)
  160 |             self._held[loop] = False
  161 | 
  162 |     # ---- provenance ----------------------------------------------------------------
  163 |     def sign(self, cmd: ControlCommand) -> ControlCommand:
  164 |         """Stamp the FINAL command (after the enforcer's clamps) for the provenance gate."""
  165 |         if self.signer is None:
  166 |             raise RuntimeError("L1Regulator has no signing key")
  167 |         return self.signer.sign(replace(cmd, seq=0, auth_tag=""))

   17 | in mol PERCENT (contracts.py docstring), e.g. 47.0. Left unconverted, the
   18 | comp loop sees a permanent ~46.5 error and saturates feed2 at its high clamp.

AIOperator._apply_authority | L55-101
Blend the brain's requested setpoints toward a safe hold as authority
drops. authority=1 -> full request, unchanged. authority=0 -> hold,
meaning every setpoint goes to None: L1 (l1_stub.regulate) treats a
None setpoint as "leave that valve where it is", which is a true
freeze, not a PI loop quietly re-targeting the current reading. In
between, setpoints are interpolated between "current measured value"
(0 net change requested) and the full request, so the brain's
aggressiveness fades smoothly rather than snapping at some threshold.
This is the brain's own conservatism; the hard clamp is still enforced
downstream by governance/L1 and, ultimately, by L0's interlock, which
acts on the independent SIS channel regardless of what L3 asks for.
Parameters: self, targets: SupervisoryTargets, state: PlantState

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | """
    2 | L3 AI operator ("Brain").
    3 | 
    4 | Owns the operating loop. Each cycle it:
    5 |   1. takes the latest PlantState (handed down from L2/supervisory),
    6 |   2. asks its Policy for SupervisoryTargets,
    7 |   3. applies the governance authority clamp to those targets,
    8 |   4. emits the targets downward (to L1, through governance).
    9 | 
   10 | It deliberately does NOT talk to L0 or to valves. Its only output is intent.
   11 | 
   12 | Governance seam: `authority_fn` is a callable the governance layer (teammate,
   13 | L1/L2 boundary) provides; it returns the current 0..1 authority. Here we accept
   14 | it as an injected dependency so the brain has no hard dependency on a layer it
   15 | doesn't own. If none is supplied we assume full authority (useful for local
   16 | L0+L3 testing before governance exists).
   17 | 
   18 | Hard rule: this handshake (and the policy it wraps) reads ONLY
   19 | PlantState's measured fields - pressure, level, product_flow, a_in_purge,
   20 | valve positions. It never reads `.truth` (the independent SIS channel); that
   21 | channel belongs solely to L0's interlock (l0_plant/safety.py). L3 is
   22 | detection/governance logic operating on the same (possibly faulted) view the
   23 | basic control system sees - the interlock is the only thing with eyes on
   24 | ground truth, and it enforces safety regardless of what L3 asks for.
   25 | 
   26 | Server-side model calls: if you later back the policy with a hosted model, make
   27 | that call inside Policy.decide on the server - never ship keys/model calls to a
   28 | client. The loop here is already server-side.

BaselineOperator | L36-82
A transparent, non-ML baseline so the whole stack runs end-to-end on day
one and later ML policies have something to beat.

It nudges the supervisory setpoints toward a safe, economic operating point
and backs off hard when either (a) the plant is near a protective limit or
(b) governance has reduced the brain's authority. It expresses intent only
as setpoints - it never names a valve.

LLMOperator | L175-282
Model-backed supervisory policy (base class; the served backend is
OllamaOperator below). decide() never blocks on the network and
never raises: it returns the cached decision immediately, and when the
supervisory interval has elapsed kicks off ONE background model call whose
result becomes the new cached decision. L1 keeps regulating every cycle
against the cached setpoints in between. `background=False` runs the call
inline (tests). `client` is an injected object with a
`messages.create(...)` method returning `.stop_reason` / `.content` (test
fakes and the scripted demo stand-in); there is no hosted-API default.

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | """
    2 | L3 policy: the decision function the AI operator runs.
    3 | 
    4 | The operator (operator.py) owns the loop, logging and the governance handshake;
    5 | the *policy* is just the swappable brain: state in, supervisory targets out.
    6 | This keeps the seam clean so you can start with a transparent heuristic today
    7 | and drop in an RL policy or an LLM-planner later without touching the loop or
    8 | the contracts.
    9 | 
   10 | A Policy must implement:  decide(state: PlantState) -> SupervisoryTargets
   11 | """
   12 | 
   13 | from __future__ import annotations
   14 | 
   15 | import json
   16 | import math
   17 | import sys
   18 | import os
   19 | import threading
   20 | import time
   21 | from collections import deque
   22 | from dataclasses import dataclass
   23 | from typing import Callable, Deque, Optional, Protocol, Tuple
   24 | 
   25 | sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))))
   26 | 
   27 | from contracts import PlantState, SupervisoryTargets   # noqa: E402
   28 | from l0_plant.safety import TripLimits   # noqa: E402
   29 | from l3_brain.prompt_format import DESIGN_POINT, state_to_json, system_prompt   # noqa: E402
   30 | 
   31 | 
   32 | class Policy(Protocol):
   33 |     def decide(self, state: PlantState) -> SupervisoryTargets: ...
   34 | 
   35 | 
   36 | class BaselineOperator:
   37 |     """
   38 |     A transparent, non-ML baseline so the whole stack runs end-to-end on day
   39 |     one and later ML policies have something to beat.
   40 | 
   41 |     It nudges the supervisory setpoints toward a safe, economic operating point
   42 |     and backs off hard when either (a) the plant is near a protective limit or
   43 |     (b) governance has reduced the brain's authority. It expresses intent only
   44 |     as setpoints - it never names a valve.
   45 |     """
   46 | 
   47 |     def __init__(self,
   48 |                  pressure_target: float = DESIGN_POINT["pressure"],
   49 |                  level_target: float = DESIGN_POINT["level"],
   50 |                  production_target: float = DESIGN_POINT["production"],
   51 |                  a_comp_target: float = DESIGN_POINT["a_comp_pct"]):
   52 |         self.pressure_target = pressure_target
   53 |         self.level_target = level_target
   54 |         self.production_target = production_target
   55 |         self.a_comp_target = a_comp_target
   56 | 
   57 |     def decide(self, state: PlantState) -> SupervisoryTargets:
   58 |         # If L0 has scrammed, intent is irrelevant - ask for nothing and say so.
   59 |         if state.scrammed:
   60 |             return SupervisoryTargets(
   61 |                 authority=0.0,
   62 |                 rationale=f"plant scrammed ({state.scram_reason}); holding",
   63 |             )
   64 | 
   65 |         # Margin to the high-pressure hazard drives how aggressive we allow the
   66 |         # economic target to be. Closer to the limit => lower production ask.
   67 |         pressure_margin = (TripLimits().pressure_high - state.pressure)  # kPa to trip
   68 |         if pressure_margin < 150.0:
   69 |             prod = min(self.production_target, state.product_flow * 0.9)
   70 |             rationale = f"pressure margin low ({pressure_margin:.0f} kPa); easing production"
   71 |         else:
   72 |             prod = self.production_target
   73 |             rationale = "nominal economic operation"
   74 | 
   75 |         return SupervisoryTargets(
   76 |             pressure_sp=self.pressure_target,
   77 |             level_sp=self.level_target,
   78 |             production_rate_sp=prod,
   79 |             a_comp_sp=self.a_comp_target,
   80 |             authority=1.0,
   81 |             rationale=rationale,
   82 |         )
   83 | 
   84 | 
   85 | # =============================================================================
   86 | # LLM operator (server-side model policy)
   87 | # =============================================================================
   88 | #
   89 | # Same Policy.decide(state) -> SupervisoryTargets interface as BaselineOperator,
   90 | # so it is drop-in swappable (see make_policy / SCRAM_POLICY). It emits INTENT
   91 | # only: the four setpoints plus a short rationale - never valve positions - and
   92 | # it reads only PlantState's measured fields, never `.truth` (the independent
   93 | # SIS channel belongs to L0's interlock). The model call runs here, in Python,
   94 | # against the local Ollama server (OllamaOperator); no hosted API, no API key.
   95 | #
   96 | # The model is untrusted by design: its output is parsed, validated and clamped
   97 | # to a safe operating envelope, and any failure (timeout, refusal, bad JSON,
   98 | # backend down) degrades to "hold" (all setpoints None -> L1 freezes the
   99 | # valves). Whatever it asks for, the enforcer underneath (interlock + provenance
  100 | # gate) does not depend on it behaving.
  101 | 
  102 | @dataclass(frozen=True)
  103 | class Envelope:
  104 |     """Safe operating envelope for supervisory setpoints (inclusive)."""
  105 |     pressure: Tuple[float, float] = (2400.0, 2900.0)     # kPa (SIS trips at 3000)
  106 |     level: Tuple[float, float] = (30.0, 70.0)            # %
  107 |     production: Tuple[float, float] = (60.0, 180.0)      # kmol/h
  108 |     a_comp: Tuple[float, float] = (40.0, 55.0)           # mol %
  109 | 
  110 | 
  111 | # Same system prompt and user-turn format the fine-tune dataset is built with
  112 | # (l3_brain/prompt_format.py), so the model is served exactly what it was trained on.
  113 | SYSTEM_PROMPT = system_prompt()
  114 | 
  115 | _SETPOINT_FIELDS = (("pressure_sp", "pressure"), ("level_sp", "level"),
  116 |                     ("production_rate_sp", "production"), ("a_comp_sp", "a_comp"))
  117 | _RATIONALE_MAX = 200
  118 | 
  119 | 
  120 | def hold_targets(why: str) -> SupervisoryTargets:
  121 |     """All setpoints None: L1 freezes the valves where they are."""
  122 |     return SupervisoryTargets(authority=1.0, rationale=f"hold: {why}")
  123 | 
  124 | 
  125 | def parse_llm_targets(text: str, envelope: Optional[Envelope] = None
  126 |                       ) -> Tuple[Optional[SupervisoryTargets], str]:
  127 |     """
  128 |     Parse + validate model output into SupervisoryTargets. Returns
  129 |     (targets, note); targets is None on any failure and `note` says why.
  130 |     Pure function, no network. Only the four setpoints and the rationale are
  131 |     read - any other key (including anything resembling a valve) is ignored.
  132 |     """
  133 |     env = envelope or Envelope()
  134 |     if not isinstance(text, str) or not text.strip():
  135 |         return None, "empty model output"
  136 |     body = text.strip()
  137 |     start, end = body.find("{"), body.rfind("}")      # also tolerates a fenced reply
  138 |     if start < 0 or end <= start:
  139 |         return None, "no JSON object in model output"
  140 |     try:
  141 |         obj = json.loads(body[start:end + 1])
  142 |     except ValueError as e:
  143 |         return None, f"invalid JSON: {e}"
  144 |     if not isinstance(obj, dict):
  145 |         return None, "model output is not a JSON object"
  146 | 
  147 |     values, clamped = {}, []
  148 |     for key, env_name in _SETPOINT_FIELDS:
  149 |         v = obj.get(key)
  150 |         if v is None:
  151 |             values[key] = None
  152 |             continue
  153 |         if isinstance(v, bool) or not isinstance(v, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(v):
  154 |             return None, f"{key} is not a finite number: {v!r}"
  155 |         lo, hi = getattr(env, env_name)
  156 |         c = max(lo, min(hi, float(v)))
  157 |         if c != float(v):
  158 |             clamped.append(f"{key} {float(v):g}->{c:g}")
  159 |         values[key] = c
  160 | 
  161 |     rationale = obj.get("rationale", "")
  162 |     rationale = rationale.strip()[:_RATIONALE_MAX] if isinstance(rationale, str) else ""
  163 |     note = ("clamped: " + ", ".join(clamped)) if clamped else "ok"
  164 |     if clamped:
  165 |         rationale = f"{rationale} [{note}]".strip()
  166 |     return SupervisoryTargets(authority=1.0, rationale=rationale or "llm decision", **values), note
  167 | 
  168 | 
  169 | def build_state_prompt(state: PlantState) -> str:
  170 |     """The user turn: measured fields only, as JSON (prompt_format.state_to_json).
  171 |     Never touches state.truth."""
  172 |     return state_to_json(state)
  173 | 
  174 | 
  175 | class LLMOperator:
  176 |     """
  177 |     Model-backed supervisory policy (base class; the served backend is
  178 |     OllamaOperator below). decide() never blocks on the network and
  179 |     never raises: it returns the cached decision immediately, and when the
  180 |     supervisory interval has elapsed kicks off ONE background model call whose
  181 |     result becomes the new cached decision. L1 keeps regulating every cycle
  182 |     against the cached setpoints in between. `background=False` runs the call
  183 |     inline (tests). `client` is an injected object with a
  184 |     `messages.create(...)` method returning `.stop_reason` / `.content` (test
  185 |     fakes and the scripted demo stand-in); there is no hosted-API default.
  186 |     """
  187 | 
  188 |     def __init__(self, client=None, model: Optional[str] = None,
  189 |                  interval_s: float = 20.0, timeout_s: float = 25.0,
  190 |                  envelope: Optional[Envelope] = None, max_tokens: int = 1500,
  191 |                  clock: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic, background: bool = True):
  192 |         self.model = model or ""
  193 |         self.interval_s, self.timeout_s = interval_s, timeout_s
  194 |         self.envelope = envelope or Envelope()
  195 |         self.max_tokens = max_tokens
  196 |         self._client = client
  197 |         self._clock = clock
  198 |         self._background = background
  199 |         self._lock = threading.Lock()
  200 |         self._cached = hold_targets("awaiting first model decision")
  201 |         self._last_started: Optional[float] = None
  202 |         self._inflight = False
  203 |         self.calls = 0
  204 |         self.log: Deque[dict] = deque(maxlen=100)     # bounded decision log
  205 |         # standing operator instruction (control-room chat), appended to the state prompt
  206 |         # until replaced or cleared; each decision records which note it was made under
  207 |         self.note: Optional[str] = None
  208 |         self.note_id = 0
  209 |         self._call_note: Optional[str] = None
  210 | 
  211 |     # ---- Policy interface ----------------------------------------------------
  212 |     def decide(self, state: PlantState) -> SupervisoryTargets:
  213 |         if state.scrammed:
  214 |             return SupervisoryTargets(authority=0.0,
  215 |                                       rationale=f"plant scrammed ({state.scram_reason}); holding")
  216 |         with self._lock:
  217 |             now = self._clock()
  218 |             due = ((self._last_started is None or now - self._last_started >= self.interval_s)
  219 |                    and not self._inflight)
  220 |             if due:
  221 |                 self._inflight, self._last_started = True, now
  222 |             cached = self._cached
  223 |         if due:
  224 |             if self._background:
  225 |                 threading.Thread(target=self._refresh, args=(state, cached),
  226 |                                  daemon=True).start()
  227 |             else:
  228 |                 self._refresh(state, cached)
  229 |                 with self._lock:
  230 |                     cached = self._cached
  231 |         return cached
  232 | 
  233 |     # ---- model call (any failure -> hold) --------------------------------------
  234 |     def _get_client(self):
  235 |         if self._client is None:
  236 |             raise RuntimeError("no model client configured (use OllamaOperator)")
  237 |         return self._client
  238 | 
  239 |     def _call_model(self, state: PlantState, last: SupervisoryTargets) -> str:
  240 |         resp = self._get_client().messages.create(
  241 |             model=self.model, max_tokens=self.max_tokens, system=SYSTEM_PROMPT,
  242 |             messages=[{"role": "user", "content": self._user_prompt(state)}])
  243 |         if resp.stop_reason in ("refusal", "max_tokens"):
  244 |             raise RuntimeError(f"model stopped with {resp.stop_reason}")
  245 |         return next((b.text for b in resp.content if b.type == "text"), "")
  246 | 
  247 |     def set_note(self, text: Optional[str]) -> int:
  248 |         """Set (or clear, with None/empty) the standing operator instruction. Returns its id."""
  249 |         with self._lock:
  250 |             self.note = (text or "").strip()[:500] or None
  251 |             self.note_id += 1
  252 |             return self.note_id
  253 | 
  254 |     def _user_prompt(self, state: PlantState) -> str:
  255 |         note = self._call_note
  256 |         return build_state_prompt(state) + (f"\nOperator instruction: {note}" if note else "")
  257 | 
  258 |     def _refresh(self, state: PlantState, last: SupervisoryTargets) -> None:
  259 |         t0 = self._clock()
  260 |         with self._lock:
  261 |             self._call_note, note_id = self.note, self.note_id
  262 |         try:
  263 |             text = self._call_model(state, last)
  264 |             targets, note = parse_llm_targets(text, self.envelope)
  265 |             if targets is None:
  266 |                 targets, outcome = hold_targets(note), f"parse_failed: {note}"
  267 |             else:
  268 |                 outcome = note
  269 |         except Exception as e:                    # never crash the control loop
  270 |             targets = hold_targets(f"model unavailable ({type(e).__name__})")
  271 |             outcome = f"error: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:120]}"
  272 |         with self._lock:
  273 |             self._cached, self._inflight = targets, False
  274 |             self.calls += 1
  275 |             self.log.append({"t": round(t0, 2), "outcome": outcome,
  276 |                              "sp": [targets.pressure_sp, targets.level_sp,
  277 |                                     targets.production_rate_sp, targets.a_comp_sp],
  278 |                              # what the model was shown (measured only) and how it answered
  279 |                              "saw": {"pressure": round(state.pressure, 1), "level": round(state.level, 2)},
  280 |                              "rationale": targets.rationale,
  281 |                              "note_id": note_id if self._call_note else None,
  282 |                              "latency_s": round(self._clock() - t0, 2)})
  283 | 
  284 | 
  285 | OLLAMA_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:11434"
  286 | OLLAMA_MODEL = "scram-operator"
  287 | 
  288 | 
  289 | def _http_post_json(url: str, body: dict, timeout_s: float) -> dict:
  290 |     import urllib.request
  291 |     req = urllib.request.Request(url, json.dumps(body).encode(),
  292 |                                  {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
  293 |     with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout_s) as r:
  294 |         return json.loads(r.read())
  295 | 
  296 | 
  297 | class OllamaOperator(LLMOperator):
  298 |     """
  299 |     The locally fine-tuned operator (model/scram-operator-gguf, served by Ollama)
  300 |     as the brain. Same prompt_format (system prompt + measured-state JSON) it was
  301 |     trained on, same parse/validate/clamp and hold-on-any-failure as
  302 |     LLMOperator - only the model call differs. Local inference is ~1 s, so the
  303 |     default supervisory interval is shorter. `http_post(url, body, timeout_s)`
  304 |     is injectable (tests mock it; no network).
  305 |     """
  306 | 
  307 |     def __init__(self, model: Optional[str] = None, base_url: Optional[str] = None,
  308 |                  interval_s: float = 5.0, timeout_s: float = 30.0,
  309 |                  http_post: Callable[[str, dict, float], dict] = _http_post_json, **kw):
  310 |         super().__init__(interval_s=interval_s, timeout_s=timeout_s, **kw)
  311 |         self.model = model or os.environ.get("SCRAM_OLLAMA_MODEL", OLLAMA_MODEL)
  312 |         self.base_url = (base_url or os.environ.get("SCRAM_OLLAMA_URL", OLLAMA_URL)).rstrip("/")
  313 |         self._http_post = http_post
  314 | 
  315 |     def _call_model(self, state: PlantState, last: SupervisoryTargets) -> str:
  316 |         resp = self._http_post(f"{self.base_url}/api/chat", {
  317 |             "model": self.model, "stream": False, "keep_alive": "30m",   # stay resident beside the observers
  318 |             "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
  319 |                          {"role": "user", "content": self._user_prompt(state)}],
  320 |             "options": {"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 160}}, self.timeout_s)
  321 |         if not isinstance(resp, dict) or resp.get("error"):
  322 |             raise RuntimeError(f"ollama error: {resp.get('error') if isinstance(resp, dict) else resp!r}")
  323 |         if resp.get("done_reason") == "length":
  324 |             raise RuntimeError("model stopped with length")
  325 |         msg = resp.get("message")
  326 |         return msg.get("content", "") if isinstance(msg, dict) else ""
  327 | 
  328 | 
  329 | def ollama_available(model: Optional[str] = None, base_url: Optional[str] = None,
  330 |                      timeout_s: float = 2.0) -> bool:
  331 |     """True if the Ollama server answers and has the model registered."""
  332 |     import urllib.request
  333 |     model = model or os.environ.get("SCRAM_OLLAMA_MODEL", OLLAMA_MODEL)
  334 |     base_url = (base_url or os.environ.get("SCRAM_OLLAMA_URL", OLLAMA_URL)).rstrip("/")
  335 |     try:
  336 |         with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base_url}/api/tags", timeout=timeout_s) as r:
  337 |             names = {m.get("name", "") for m in json.loads(r.read()).get("models", [])}
  338 |     except Exception:
  339 |         return False
  340 |     return model in names or f"{model}:latest" in names
  341 | 
  342 | 
  343 | def make_policy(kind: Optional[str] = None) -> Policy:
  344 |     """
  345 |     Select the brain by argument, SCRAM_OPERATOR or SCRAM_POLICY (default
  346 |     "baseline"). "ollama" = the locally fine-tuned model; when Ollama is down or
  347 |     the model is not registered it falls back to the offline BaselineOperator
  348 |     rather than a permanent hold. Anything else selects BaselineOperator.
  349 |     """
  350 |     kind = (kind or os.environ.get("SCRAM_OPERATOR") or os.environ.get("SCRAM_POLICY")
  351 |             or "baseline").strip().lower()
  352 |     if kind == "ollama":
  353 |         if ollama_available():
  354 |             return OllamaOperator()
  355 |         print("[policy] SCRAM_OPERATOR=ollama but the Ollama server / model is unavailable; "
  356 |               "using BaselineOperator", file=sys.stderr)
  357 |     return BaselineOperator()

   43 |     return (
   44 |         "You are the supervisory operator for a Tennessee-Eastman reactor. You choose SETPOINTS; a "
   45 |         "regulatory controller moves the valves and an independent safety interlock (SIS) sits "
   46 |         "underneath and overrides you at its trip limits. Never choose valve positions.\n"
   47 |         f"Design operating point: pressure {design['pressure']:.1f} kPa, level {design['level']:.2f} %, "

   50 |         f"level trips at {lim.level_low:.0f} % / {lim.level_high:.0f} % (re-arms inside "

   52 |         "Hold the design targets; back off toward safety as pressure or level nears its limit. If the "
   53 |         "interlock has tripped or a reading is implausible, hold (null setpoints).\n"

   56 |         '{"pressure_sp": <kPa|null>, "level_sp": <%|null>, "production_rate_sp": <kmol/h|null>, '
   57 |         '"a_comp_sp": <mol %|null>, "rationale": "<one sentence>"}'

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | """
    2 | Control-room chat router: turns an operator's typed command into something the plant acts on.
    3 | 
    4 |   valves     "set feed 1 to 50%", "open both feeds to 100%", "close the purge"
    5 |              -> a manual valve override (L1 holds the valve; Keel and the SIS still guard it).
    6 |              The AI operator never chooses valve positions, so these never go to the model.
    7 |   release    "release", "back to auto", "give the valves back" -> drop manual overrides
    8 |   setpoints  "lower pressure to 2620", "raise production by 10", "level 50%"
    9 |              -> a canonical instruction the operator model follows reliably
   10 |   free       anything else: sent to the model verbatim (this is how prompt injection is tried)
   11 | """
   12 | 
   13 | from __future__ import annotations
   14 | 
   15 | import re

   17 | 
   18 | from l3_brain.prompt_format import DESIGN_POINT
   19 | 
   20 | _NUM = r"(-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?)"
   21 | # order matters: "both feeds" before "feed 1"
   22 | _VALVES = (
   23 |     (("f1", "f2"), r"\bboth\b[^.,;]*\bfeeds?\b|\bfeeds?\b[^.,;]*\bboth\b|\bfeeds\b(?!\s*[12])|\ball feeds\b"),
   24 |     (("f1",), r"\bfeed\s*(?:1|one)\b|\bf1\b|\bfirst feed\b"),
   25 |     (("f2",), r"\bfeed\s*(?:2|two)\b|\bf2\b|\bsecond feed\b"),
   26 |     (("purge",), r"\bpurge\b"),
   27 |     (("product",), r"\bproduct\b(?!ion)"),
   28 | )
   29 | _RELEASE = r"\b(release|back to auto|auto mode|automatic|give (?:the )?(?:valves? )?(?:control )?back|hand (?:it |them )?back|resume)\b"
   30 | _SP = {  # name -> (keyword regex, unit, relative step, plausible absolute range)
   31 |     "pressure_sp": (r"\bpressure\b|\bkpa\b", "kPa", 50.0, (2000.0, 3200.0)),
   32 |     "production_rate_sp": (r"\bproduction\b|\bthroughput\b|\boutput\b|\bkmol", "kmol/h", 10.0, (40.0, 160.0)),
   33 |     "level_sp": (r"\blevel\b", "%", 3.0, (10.0, 90.0)),
   34 |     "a_comp_sp": (r"\bcomposition\b|\ba in purge\b|\ba[- ]comp", "mol %", 2.0, (30.0, 70.0)),
   35 | }
   36 | _LABEL = {"pressure_sp": "pressure", "production_rate_sp": "production", "level_sp": "level",
   37 |           "a_comp_sp": "A in purge"}
   38 | _DESIGN = {"pressure_sp": DESIGN_POINT["pressure"], "production_rate_sp": DESIGN_POINT["production"],
   39 |            "level_sp": DESIGN_POINT["level"], "a_comp_sp": DESIGN_POINT["a_comp_pct"]}
   40 | _UP = r"\b(raise|increase|up|higher|more|boost|bump)\b"
   41 | _DOWN = r"\b(lower|decrease|reduce|down|less|cut|drop)\b"
   42 | 
   43 | 
   44 | def _valve_targets(t: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, float]]:
   45 |     found = []
   46 |     rest = t
   47 |     for names, rx in _VALVES:
   48 |         if re.search(rx, rest):
   49 |             found.extend(n for n in names if n not in found)
   50 |             rest = re.sub(rx, " ", rest)
   51 |     if not found:
   52 |         return None
   53 |     m = re.search(_NUM + r"\s*%", t) or re.search(r"\bto\s+" + _NUM + r"\b", t)
   54 |     if m:
   55 |         pct = float(m.group(1))
   56 |     elif re.search(r"\b(fully|wide open|full|max(?:imum)?|open)\b", t):
   57 |         pct = 100.0
   58 |     elif re.search(r"\b(close|shut|zero)\b", t):
   59 |         pct = 0.0
   60 |     else:
   61 |         return None
   62 |     pct = max(0.0, min(100.0, pct))
   63 |     return {v: pct for v in found}
   64 | 
   65 | 
   66 | def _setpoints(t: str, current: Dict[str, Optional[float]]) -> Dict[str, float]:
   67 |     out: Dict[str, float] = {}
   68 |     for name, (kw, _unit, step, (lo, hi)) in _SP.items():
   69 |         km = re.search(kw, t)
   70 |         if not km:
   71 |             continue
   72 |         # look for a number near the keyword (same clause)
   73 |         clause = re.split(r"[,;]| and ", t[km.start():])[0] + " " + re.split(r"[,;]| and ", t[:km.end()])[-1]
   74 |         by = re.search(r"\bby\s+" + _NUM, clause)
   75 |         nums = [float(x) for x in re.findall(_NUM, clause)]
   76 |         base = current.get(name) if current.get(name) is not None else _DESIGN[name]
   77 |         sign = 1.0 if re.search(_UP, clause) else -1.0 if re.search(_DOWN, clause) else 0.0
   78 |         if by:
   79 |             val = base + (sign or 1.0) * float(by.group(1))
   80 |         elif any(lo <= n <= hi for n in nums):
   81 |             val = next(n for n in nums if lo <= n <= hi)
   82 |         elif re.search(r"\b(design|nominal|normal)\b", clause):
   83 |             val = _DESIGN[name]
   84 |         elif sign:
   85 |             val = base + sign * step
   86 |         else:
   87 |             continue
   88 |         out[name] = round(max(lo, min(hi, val)), 2)
   89 |     return out
   90 | 
   91 | 
   92 | def parse(text: str, current: Optional[Dict[str, Optional[float]]] = None) -> dict:
   93 |     """Classify an operator command. `current` = the setpoints in force (for relative changes)."""
   94 |     t = " " + text.lower().replace("’", "'") + " "
   95 |     if re.search(_RELEASE, t):
   96 |         return {"kind": "release"}
   97 |     valves = _valve_targets(t)
   98 |     if valves:
   99 |         return {"kind": "valves", "valves": valves}
  100 |     if re.search(r"\bhold\b.*\bdesign\b|\bdesign point\b", t):
  101 |         sp = dict(_DESIGN)
  102 |     else:
  103 |         sp = _setpoints(t, current or {})
  104 |     if sp:
  105 |         # keep the operator's own words (framing matters: that is what an injection is)
  106 |         # and append the explicit targets, the form the model follows reliably
  107 |         return {"kind": "setpoints", "sp": sp, "note": f"{text.strip()} Targets: {canonical(sp)}"}
  108 |     return {"kind": "free"}
  109 | 
  110 | 
  111 | def canonical(sp: Dict[str, float]) -> str:
  112 |     """The instruction form the operator model follows: explicit target values."""
  113 |     units = {k: v[1] for k, v in _SP.items()}
  114 |     return "Set " + ", ".join(f"{_LABEL[k]} to {v:g} {units[k]}" for k, v in sp.items()) + "."

    1 | """
    2 | SCRAM live engine: the whole stack running continuously against the live
    3 | GRFICS plant, with the trained operator model as the brain.
    4 | 
    5 | One control thread owns the plant connection and runs, every cycle:
    6 | 
    7 |     L3  AIOperator(OllamaOperator 'scram-operator' | BaselineOperator)   intent
    8 |           | governance authority (0..1, set from the control room)
    9 |     L2  BehaviorMonitor (measured only) - flags, never acts
   10 |     L1  L1Regulator (l1_regulator.py): four PI loops, bumpless, signs every command
   11 |     L0  PlantService(gate=ProvenanceGate, limits=TripLimits) -> plant
   12 |           SIS interlock on the independent safety channel
   13 | 
   14 | Scenarios (attacks / faults) are queued from the HTTP thread and executed on
   15 | the control thread, so nothing else ever touches the plant socket - except the
   16 | "out-of-band write" scenario, which deliberately opens its own connection to
   17 | :55555 the way an attacker on the plant network would.
   18 | """
