model/telemetry-classifier/README.md
Directory-specific setup, background or saved-model documentation. Read in context of the current source and the historical distinctions in this guide.
================================================================================================

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | # Earlier restricted telemetry specialist
    2 | 
    3 | The active runtime prefers the [physics detector](../telemetry-physics/README.md).
    4 | This classifier is the fallback when the physics policy is absent or disabled;
    5 | an integrity error does not silently select the fallback.
    6 | 
    7 | A CPU ExtraTrees classifier trained on measured-only telemetry and L1 command
    8 | windows from `training/observer_clean/`. Runtime inference uses a plain JSON
    9 | forest and Python's standard library, not pickle or scikit-learn. The model is
   10 | about 535 kB and requires no GPU memory.
   11 | 
   12 | The standalone classifier has a false-alarm tradeoff and is **not** deployed as
   13 | a replacement for the LLM. Only confident sensor/actuator findings may correct
   14 | an otherwise normal LLM telemetry verdict. Proposal judgments and governance
   15 | authority are unchanged. Original LLM labels and correction sources are logged.
   16 | 
   17 | `policy.json` enables this limited correction after 99 eligible validation findings
   18 | with no observed mistakes (assuming normal LLM verdicts). Its model digest prevents loading changed weights
   19 | under an old approval. This is a validation result, not a proof of safety.
   20 | 
   21 | The attempted sensor-noise suppression policy failed validation (three genuine
   22 | sensor faults would have been suppressed), so it remains disabled. Existing
   23 | LLM alarms are preserved by this restricted policy. The preferred physics
   24 | detector has a different correction policy, described in its README.
   25 | 
   26 | Reproduce the historical restricted-classifier experiment from the repository
   27 | root in a separate checkout (these commands overwrite candidate outputs):
   28 | 
   29 | ```sh
   30 | pip install -r requirements-eval.txt
   31 | python -m training.build_clean_observer_dataset
   32 | python -m training.train_telemetry_classifier
   33 | python -m training.evaluate_telemetry_specialist
   34 | ```
   35 | 
   36 | `training.benchmark_observer` now uses whichever specialist is approved (normally
   37 | the physics detector), so rerunning it does not reproduce the earlier restricted
   38 | classifier comparison. Use a separate `--output` path to preserve saved evidence.
   39 | 
   40 | `evaluation.json` records the standalone classifier, including its weaknesses.
   41 | `hybrid-evaluation.json` records development replay against historical LLM
   42 | outputs. `artifacts/fresh-observer-benchmark.json` records the saved paired local
   43 | Ollama inference. Neither the replay nor this small fresh sample establishes
   44 | deployment-wide accuracy. The original LLM weights were not retrained.

model/telemetry-physics/README.md
Directory-specific setup, background or saved-model documentation. Read in context of the current source and the historical distinctions in this guide.
================================================================================================

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | # Advisory physics-feature telemetry detector
    2 | 
    3 | This is the currently preferred CPU correction model loaded by
    4 | `approved_specialist()` in [`monitor/telemetry_classifier.py`](../../monitor/telemetry_classifier.py).
    5 | It uses measured telemetry and command/response features from
    6 | [`monitor/physics_features.py`](../../monitor/physics_features.py), with a JSON
    7 | forest evaluated using Python's standard library. It needs no GPU.
    8 | 
    9 | For v3 telemetry, it supplies the advisory classification and preserves the
   10 | original verdict as `llm_label`, with source `llm+physics-detector`. Unlike the
   11 | older restricted classifier, it can revise an existing alarm as well as a
   12 | normal verdict. It does not contribute to proposal authority or protective
   13 | actuation and is invoked through the LLM telemetry path.
   14 | 
   15 | ## Release evidence
   16 | 
   17 | [`policy.json`](policy.json) enables the model only with matching SHA-256 hashes
   18 | for the model, feature source, validation and final evaluation report. The
   19 | [final report](final-holdout-evaluation.json) also checks the frozen candidate
   20 | and records the passed gate. Git preserves the evidence bytes across checkouts.
   21 | 
   22 | The final 215-example holdout records 93.02% accuracy, 0 observed normal false
   23 | alarms, 89.74% sensor-fault recall and 93.62% actuator-fault recall. The sample
   24 | includes simulated trajectories and explicitly synthetic faults. These results
   25 | do not establish physical deployment safety or a zero population false-alarm
   26 | rate. See [accuracy improvements](../../ACCURACY_IMPROVEMENTS.md) for the
   27 | candidate history and remaining limitations.
   28 | 
   29 | ## Reproduction and changes
   30 | 
   31 | Training is implemented in
   32 | [`training/train_physics_telemetry.py`](../../training/train_physics_telemetry.py);
   33 | the freeze/holdout protocol is in
   34 | [`training/evaluate_physics_holdout.py`](../../training/evaluate_physics_holdout.py).
   35 | Those scripts write model/evaluation outputs, and their default paths do not
   36 | automatically reconstruct every final-release artifact. Inspect their arguments
   37 | and use a separate checkout for experiments. Preserve the frozen evidence.
   38 | 
   39 | To verify the bundled release without retraining, run from the repository root:
   40 | 
   41 | ```sh
   42 | python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt -r requirements-eval.txt
   43 | python -m pytest -q tests/test_physics_detector.py
   44 | ```
   45 | 
   46 | If the physics policy is absent or disabled, the loader can use the
   47 | [older restricted classifier](../telemetry-classifier/README.md). An integrity
   48 | failure raises an error; the live engine reports the unavailable specialist
   49 | instead of silently approving changed files.

    1 | """
    2 | L2 governance: turns the L2 monitors' suspicion into an authority CEILING for the
    3 | AI operator - the "when do we throttle the brain" decision.
    4 | 
    5 | This SHAPES authority; it does not provide safety. The SIS (l0_plant/safety.py)
    6 | stays the independent hard stop and Keel keeps its own physics / gate-driven
    7 | authority; the operator gets min(Keel's authority, this ceiling).
    8 | 
    9 | Inputs each cycle (routed exactly as in Phase 1):
   10 |   * the rule monitor's score (SequentialMonitor), sampled every RULE_SAMPLE_S
   11 |   * the observer's PROPOSAL-side verdicts (provenance_violation,
   12 |     rationale_mismatch, setpoint_drift); telemetry verdicts are display-only
   13 |   * the brain's latest pre-blend intent, for the recovery envelope check
   14 | 
   15 | 1. Debounce: suspicion only counts once corroborated - two CONSECUTIVE calls of
   16 |    the same monitor both above TIER1 (for the observer: two consecutive verdicts
   17 |    that are proposal-side attack labels). A one-off spike moves nothing.
   18 |    Corroboration is temporal per monitor, not cross-monitor agreement, so the
   19 |    observer can still catch what the rule monitor cannot see.
   20 | 2. Ceiling g(s): piecewise, monotonic non-increasing, bounded in [floor, 1]; the
   21 |    floor is NONZERO so no verdict (single, repeated or hallucinated) can drive the
   22 |    operator to 0.
   23 | 3. Rates: the applied ceiling falls toward g(s) fast (DROP_PER_S) and rises slowly
   24 |    (RECOVER_PER_S), and only after suspicion has stayed below TIER1 for
   25 |    CLEAN_WINDOW_S AND the operator's latest proposal is back inside the design
   26 |    envelope - recovery is not just history aging out.
   27 | """

   39 | # TIER2..TIER3 -> CEIL_TIER2..CEIL_TIER3; s >= TIER3 -> FLOOR (FLOOR_PROVENANCE)

   69 |     """g(s): corroborated suspicion -> authority ceiling."""
   70 |     s = max(0.0, min(1.0, s))
   71 |     if s < TIER1:
   72 |         return 1.0
   73 |     if s < TIER2:
   74 |         return 1.0 + (CEIL_TIER2 - 1.0) * (s - TIER1) / (TIER2 - TIER1)
   75 |     if s < TIER3:
   76 |         return CEIL_TIER2 + (CEIL_TIER3 - CEIL_TIER2) * (s - TIER2) / (TIER3 - TIER2)
   77 |     return FLOOR_PROVENANCE if label == "provenance_violation" else FLOOR
   78 | 
   79 | 
   80 | def in_envelope(intent) -> bool:
   81 |     """True when the proposal is back near design; a hold (None) counts as inside."""
   82 |     if intent is None:
   83 |         return True
   84 |     for k, tol in ENVELOPE.items():
   85 |         v = getattr(intent, k, None)
   86 |         if v is not None and abs(v - _DESIGN_SP[k]) > tol:
   87 |             return False
   88 |     return True
   89 | 
   90 | 
   91 | @dataclass
   92 | class GovState:
   93 |     t: float
   94 |     raw: float                # max(rule score, observer proposal suspicion), uncorroborated
   95 |     corroborated: float
   96 |     label: Optional[str]      # what drives the corroborated value
   97 |     ceiling: float            # g(corroborated)
   98 |     applied: float            # rate-limited ceiling handed to the operator
   99 |     recovering: bool
  100 |     envelope_ok: bool
  101 | 
  102 |     def as_dict(self) -> dict:
  103 |         return {"t": round(self.t, 2), "raw": round(self.raw, 3), "corroborated": round(self.corroborated, 3),
  104 |                 "label": self.label, "ceiling": round(self.ceiling, 3), "applied": round(self.applied, 3),
  105 |                 "recovering": self.recovering, "envelope_ok": self.envelope_ok}
  106 | 
  107 | 
  108 | class Governor:
  109 |     def __init__(self):
  110 |         self.reset()
  111 | 
  112 |     def reset(self) -> None:
  113 |         self.applied = 1.0
  114 |         self._last_t: Optional[float] = None
  115 |         self._obs_prev: Optional[tuple] = None        # (label, score) of the previous verdict
  116 |         self._obs_corr, self._obs_label = 0.0, None
  117 |         self._obs_seen_t: Optional[float] = None
  118 |         self._rule_prev: Optional[float] = None
  119 |         self._rule_corr, self._rule_label = 0.0, None
  120 |         self._rule_sample_t = -1e9
  121 |         self._rule_eff: Optional[float] = None       # rule score after the residual discount
  122 |         self._rule_raw_prev: Optional[float] = None
  123 |         self._clean_since: Optional[float] = None
  124 |         self.last: Optional[GovState] = None
  125 | 
  126 |     def _observer(self, verdict, t: float) -> None:
  127 |         """One observer call = one new proposals verdict (invalid ones are skipped)."""
  128 |         if verdict is None or t - verdict.t > OBS_STALE_S:
  129 |             # no observer evidence (none yet, model gone, or stale): it holds nothing
  130 |             self._obs_corr, self._obs_label, self._obs_prev = 0.0, None, None
  131 |             return
  132 |         if verdict.label is None or verdict.t == self._obs_seen_t:
  133 |             return
  134 |         self._obs_seen_t = verdict.t
  135 |         cur = (verdict.label, verdict.score) if verdict.label in PROPOSAL_LABELS else None
  136 |         if cur is None:                                       # a normal verdict clears it at once
  137 |             self._obs_corr, self._obs_label = 0.0, None
  138 |         elif self._obs_prev is not None and min(self._obs_prev[1], cur[1]) >= TIER1:
  139 |             self._obs_corr, self._obs_label = min(self._obs_prev[1], cur[1]), cur[0]
  140 |         self._obs_prev = cur
  141 | 
  142 |     def _rule(self, t: float, raw: float, source: str, env: bool) -> None:
  143 |         if t - self._rule_sample_t < RULE_SAMPLE_S:
  144 |             return
  145 |         dt, self._rule_sample_t = t - self._rule_sample_t, t
  146 |         if env and source in RESIDUAL_SOURCES and self._rule_eff is not None:
  147 |             fresh = max(0.0, raw - self._rule_raw_prev)          # new evidence counts in full
  148 |             score = min(raw, self._rule_eff * 0.5 ** (dt / RESIDUAL_HALF_LIFE_S) + fresh)
  149 |         else:
  150 |             score = raw
  151 |         self._rule_eff, self._rule_raw_prev = score, raw
  152 |         if self._rule_prev is not None and min(self._rule_prev, score) >= TIER1:
  153 |             self._rule_corr, self._rule_label = min(self._rule_prev, score), f"rule:{source}"
  154 |         elif score < TIER1:
  155 |             self._rule_corr, self._rule_label = 0.0, None
  156 |         self._rule_prev = score
  157 | 
  158 |     def update(self, t: float, rule_score: float, rule_source: str, obs_verdict=None,
  159 |                obs_suspicion: float = 0.0, intent=None) -> GovState:
  160 |         dt = 0.0 if self._last_t is None else max(0.0, min(t - self._last_t, 5.0))
  161 |         self._last_t = t
  162 |         self._observer(obs_verdict, t)
  163 |         env = in_envelope(intent)
  164 |         self._rule(t, rule_score, rule_source, env)
  165 |         if self._obs_corr >= self._rule_corr:
  166 |             s, label = self._obs_corr, self._obs_label
  167 |         else:
  168 |             s, label = self._rule_corr, self._rule_label
  169 |         g = ceiling(s, label)
  170 |         if s < TIER1:
  171 |             self._clean_since = t if self._clean_since is None else self._clean_since
  172 |         else:
  173 |             self._clean_since = None
  174 |         recovering = False
  175 |         if g < self.applied:
  176 |             self.applied = max(g, self.applied - DROP_PER_S * dt)
  177 |         elif g > self.applied and env and self._clean_since is not None \
  178 |                 and t - self._clean_since >= CLEAN_WINDOW_S:
  179 |             self.applied = min(g, self.applied + RECOVER_PER_S * dt)
  180 |             recovering = True
  181 |         self.last = GovState(t, max(rule_score, obs_suspicion), s, label if s > 0 else None,
  182 |                              g, self.applied, recovering, env)
  183 |         return self.last

    1 | """
    2 | L2 observer wrapper: the fine-tuned observer models as live ADVISORY detectors
    3 | beside the rule-based SequentialMonitor. The two checks are served by different
    4 | models, each on its strength (make_split_observer):
    5 |   PROPOSALS  v2 (Ollama "scram-observer")   - feeds authority; v2's proposal head
    6 |              raised no false alarms where v3's did
    7 |              (experiments/observer_v3_proposal_replay.json). Fallback: none
    8 |              (rule monitor only) - never v3.
    9 |   TELEMETRY  v3 ("scram-observer-v3")       - display only; fallback v2, then nothing.
   10 | Each path falls down its own chain after MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS backend errors.
   11 | 
   12 | Each control cycle the engine calls feed(t, state, intent, commanded). An Observer
   13 | keeps the inputs its model was trained on - the brain's last HISTORY_N proposals
   14 | (sampled every PROPOSAL_EVERY_S) and/or the last WINDOW_N measured samples (every
   15 | SAMPLE_S) - and runs its calls on a background thread, so the control loop never
   16 | waits on a model. The split's two paths share one in-flight gate and check every
   17 | SPLIT_CHECK_EVERY_S each: the request pattern the co-residency check validated
   18 | (operator + v2 + v3 resident, no reloads). Requests pin keep_alive so idle gaps
   19 | never unload a model.
   20 | Serving three models needs LLAMA_ARG_CACHE_RAM=0 for Ollama (model/README.md):
   21 | llama-server's default 8 GB-per-runner prompt cache otherwise exhausts host RAM.
   22 | 
   23 | suspicion() is what Keel may consume, and it is ROUTED by input type: only the
   24 | proposal-side labels (provenance_violation, rationale_mismatch, setpoint_drift)
   25 | count; the observer's telemetry verdicts are shown but never fed to Keel - the
   26 | rule monitors and the SIS own telemetry. normal -> 0; an attack label -> its
   27 | score, floored at SCORE_FLOOR. Any bad, invalid or missing output -> 0 and a
   28 | note, never a spurious alarm (same degrade-to-safe rule as the operator).
   29 | 
   30 | The format module is injectable and brings its own window (WINDOW_N, SAMPLE_S).
   31 | A format with TELEMETRY_COMMANDED (v3) also gets, per sample, the valve positions
   32 | L1 last sent - the command whose result that sample is, exactly how the training
   33 | recordings paired them - and both go through measured_dict's rounding, so a live
   34 | window is built the way the training windows were.
   35 | """
   36 | 
   37 | from __future__ import annotations
   38 | 
   39 | import json
   40 | import threading
   41 | import time
   42 | import urllib.request
   43 | from collections import deque
   44 | from dataclasses import dataclass
   45 | from typing import Callable, Deque, Optional
   46 | 
   47 | from l3_brain.prompt_format import measured_dict
   48 | from monitor import observer_v2_format as V2
   49 | from monitor import observer_v3_format as V3
   50 | 
   51 | OLLAMA_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:11434"
   52 | OBSERVER_MODEL = "scram-observer"
   53 | # per input type, served in this order, first one installed wins: (format, Ollama model, num_ctx).
   54 | # num_ctx must match the Modelfile, or Ollama reloads the model on every request.
   55 | PROPOSAL_CHAIN = ((V2, "scram-observer", None),)
   56 | TELEMETRY_CHAIN = ((V3, "scram-observer-v3", 3072),     # v3 telemetry prompts are ~2,450 tokens
   57 |                    (V2, "scram-observer", None))
   58 | KEEP_ALIVE = "30m"            # keep every observer model resident between calls
   59 | SAMPLE_S = 0.5                # sample spacing unless the format sets SAMPLE_S (v2: 6 samples ~2.6 s)
   60 | MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS = 3    # backend errors in a row -> that path moves down its chain
   61 | PROPOSAL_EVERY_S = 5.0        # one proposal per operator decision interval
   62 | CHECK_EVERY_S = 2.5           # a model call at most this often, alternating input types
   63 | SPLIT_CHECK_EVERY_S = 5.0     # per path in the split (combined rate = the single-observer rate)
   64 | KINDS = ("proposals", "telemetry")
   65 | SCORE_FLOOR = 0.3             # an attack label never maps below this
   66 | VERDICT_MAX_AGE_S = 30.0
   67 | 
   68 | 
   69 | @dataclass
   70 | class Verdict:
   71 |     t: float
   72 |     kind: str                 # "proposals" | "telemetry"
   73 |     label: Optional[str]      # None = invalid / no output
   74 |     score: float
   75 |     reason: str
   76 |     note: str = "ok"
   77 |     latency_s: float = 0.0
   78 |     source: str = "llm"
   79 |     llm_label: Optional[str] = None
   80 | 
   81 |     def as_dict(self) -> dict:
   82 |         return {"t": round(self.t, 1), "kind": self.kind, "label": self.label, "score": round(self.score, 2),
   83 |                 "reason": self.reason, "note": self.note, "latency_s": round(self.latency_s, 2),
   84 |                 "source": self.source, "llm_label": self.llm_label}
   85 | 
   86 | 
   87 | def _http_post_json(url: str, body: dict, timeout_s: float) -> dict:
   88 |     req = urllib.request.Request(url, json.dumps(body).encode(), {"Content-Type": "application/json"})
   89 |     with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout_s) as r:
   90 |         return json.loads(r.read())
   91 | 
   92 | 
   93 | def observer_available(model: str = OBSERVER_MODEL, base_url: str = OLLAMA_URL, timeout_s: float = 2.0) -> bool:
   94 |     try:
   95 |         with urllib.request.urlopen(f"{base_url}/api/tags", timeout=timeout_s) as r:
   96 |             names = {m.get("name", "") for m in json.loads(r.read()).get("models", [])}
   97 |     except Exception:                               # noqa: BLE001
   98 |         return False
   99 |     return model in names or f"{model}:latest" in names
  100 | 
  101 | 
  102 | class Observer:
  103 |     """One model serving one or both input types (`kinds`)."""
  104 | 
  105 |     def __init__(self, fmt=V2, model: str = OBSERVER_MODEL, base_url: str = OLLAMA_URL,
  106 |                  timeout_s: float = 20.0, background: bool = True, num_ctx: Optional[int] = None,
  107 |                  kinds: tuple = KINDS, check_every_s: float = CHECK_EVERY_S,
  108 |                  gate: Optional[threading.Semaphore] = None,
  109 |                  telemetry_specialist=None,
  110 |                  http_post: Callable[[str, dict, float], dict] = _http_post_json):
  111 |         self.fmt, self.model, self.base_url = fmt, model, base_url.rstrip("/")
  112 |         self.timeout_s, self._background, self._http_post = timeout_s, background, http_post
  113 |         self.num_ctx, self.kinds, self.check_every_s = num_ctx, tuple(kinds), check_every_s
  114 |         self.sample_s = getattr(fmt, "SAMPLE_S", SAMPLE_S)
  115 |         self.commanded = getattr(fmt, "TELEMETRY_COMMANDED", False)
  116 |         self._lock = threading.Lock()
  117 |         self._gate = gate or threading.Semaphore(1)       # at most one call in flight (shared in a split)
  118 |         self._samples: Deque[tuple] = deque(maxlen=fmt.WINDOW_N)      # (t, measured, commanded)
  119 |         self._proposals: Deque[dict] = deque(maxlen=fmt.HISTORY_N)
  120 |         self._last_sample_t = self._last_prop_t = self._last_check_t = -1e9
  121 |         self._next_kind = "proposals"
  122 |         self._proposals_dirty = False
  123 |         self.last: dict = {}                    # kind -> Verdict
  124 |         self.calls = self.failures = 0
  125 |         self.consecutive_errors = 0             # backend errors (not bad outputs) in a row
  126 |         self.last_user: dict = {}               # kind -> last user turn sent (for audits)
  127 |         self.log: Deque[dict] = deque(maxlen=100)
  128 |         self._generation = 0
  129 |         self._last_feed_t = None
  130 |         self.telemetry_specialist = telemetry_specialist
  131 | 
  132 |     # ---- inputs -------------------------------------------------------------
  133 |     def reset(self) -> None:
  134 |         """Forget history (e.g. after an operator re-arm) and drop old verdicts."""
  135 |         with self._lock:
  136 |             self._generation += 1
  137 |             self._samples.clear()
  138 |             self._proposals.clear()
  139 |             self.last = {}
  140 |             self._last_sample_t = self._last_prop_t = self._last_check_t = -1e9
  141 |             self._proposals_dirty = False
  142 |             self._next_kind = "proposals"
  143 |             self._last_feed_t = None
  144 |             self.last_user.clear()
  145 |             self.consecutive_errors = 0
  146 | 
  147 |     def feed(self, t: float, state, intent=None, commanded=None) -> None:
  148 |         """Call once per control cycle; never blocks on the model. commanded: the
  149 |         ControlCommand whose result `state` is (L1's last signed command); a
  150 |         TELEMETRY_COMMANDED format takes no sample until there is one."""
  151 |         self._last_feed_t = t
  152 |         if "telemetry" in self.kinds and t - self._last_sample_t >= self.sample_s \
  153 |                 and (commanded is not None or not self.commanded):
  154 |             self._last_sample_t = t
  155 |             if self.commanded:
  156 |                 m = measured_dict(state)
  157 |                 c = {"f1": round(commanded.f1_valve, 4), "f2": round(commanded.f2_valve, 4),
  158 |                      "purge": round(commanded.purge_valve, 4), "product": round(commanded.product_valve, 4)}
  159 |             else:
  160 |                 m, c = {k: getattr(state, k) for k in self.fmt.TELEMETRY_FIELDS}, None
  161 |                 m["scrammed"] = bool(state.scrammed)
  162 |             self._samples.append((t, m, c))
  163 |         if "proposals" in self.kinds and intent is not None and t - self._last_prop_t >= PROPOSAL_EVERY_S:
  164 |             self._last_prop_t = t
  165 |             self._proposals.append(self.fmt.proposal_dict(intent, intent.rationale or ""))
  166 |             self._proposals_dirty = True
  167 |         if t - self._last_check_t >= self.check_every_s:
  168 |             self._maybe_check(t)
  169 | 
  170 |     def _maybe_check(self, t: float) -> None:
  171 |         kinds = [self._next_kind, "telemetry" if self._next_kind == "proposals" else "proposals"]
  172 |         for kind in kinds:
  173 |             if kind not in self.kinds:
  174 |                 continue
  175 |             if kind == "proposals" and (len(self._proposals) < self.fmt.HISTORY_N or not self._proposals_dirty):
  176 |                 continue
  177 |             if kind == "telemetry" and len(self._samples) < self.fmt.WINDOW_N:
  178 |                 continue
  179 |             if not self._gate.acquire(blocking=False):
  180 |                 return                              # a call (this path's or the other's) is in flight
  181 |             self._last_check_t = t
  182 |             self._next_kind = "telemetry" if kind == "proposals" else "proposals"
  183 |             try:
  184 |                 if kind == "proposals":
  185 |                     self._proposals_dirty = False
  186 |                     user = self.fmt.proposals_to_json(list(self._proposals))
  187 |                 else:
  188 |                     ts = [s[0] for s in self._samples]
  189 |                     meas = [s[1] for s in self._samples]
  190 |                     user = (self.fmt.telemetry_to_json(meas, [s[2] for s in self._samples], ts[-1] - ts[0])
  191 |                             if self.commanded else self.fmt.telemetry_to_json(meas, ts[-1] - ts[0]))
  192 |                 self.last_user[kind] = user
  193 |                 generation = self._generation
  194 |                 if self._background:
  195 |                     threading.Thread(target=self._run, args=(t, kind, user, generation), daemon=True).start()
  196 |                     return
  197 |             except Exception:                       # noqa: BLE001 - never hold the shared gate
  198 |                 self._gate.release()
  199 |                 raise
  200 |             self._run(t, kind, user, generation)
  201 |             return
  202 | 
  203 |     # ---- model call (any failure -> no verdict, suspicion 0) -----------------
  204 |     def _run(self, t: float, kind: str, user: str, generation=None) -> None:
  205 |         generation = self._generation if generation is None else generation
  206 |         t0 = time.monotonic()
  207 |         options = {"temperature": 0, "num_predict": 120}
  208 |         if self.num_ctx:
  209 |             options["num_ctx"] = self.num_ctx
  210 |         backend_error = False
  211 |         try:
  212 |             resp = self._http_post(f"{self.base_url}/api/chat", {
  213 |                 "model": self.model, "stream": False, "format": "json", "keep_alive": KEEP_ALIVE,
  214 |                 "messages": self.fmt.messages(user), "options": options}, self.timeout_s)
  215 |             if not isinstance(resp, dict) or resp.get("error"):
  216 |                 raise RuntimeError(f"ollama error: {resp.get('error') if isinstance(resp, dict) else resp!r}")
  217 |             v, note = self.fmt.parse((resp.get("message") or {}).get("content", ""))
  218 |             verdict = (Verdict(t, kind, v["label"], v["score"], v["reason"], "ok") if v
  219 |                        else Verdict(t, kind, None, 0.0, "", f"invalid output: {note}"))
  220 |             if v and kind == "telemetry" and self.telemetry_specialist is not None:
  221 |                 try:
  222 |                     corrected = self.telemetry_specialist.correct(json.loads(user), v)
  223 |                     if corrected.get("source") in ("llm+telemetry-specialist", "calibrated-telemetry", "llm+physics-detector"):
  224 |                         verdict = Verdict(t, kind, corrected["label"], corrected["score"], corrected["reason"], "ok",
  225 |                                           source=corrected["source"], llm_label=corrected.get("llm_label", v["label"]))
  226 |                 except (ValueError, TypeError, KeyError):
  227 |                     pass  # malformed/older telemetry retains the validated LLM verdict
  228 |         except Exception as e:                      # noqa: BLE001 - never crash the control loop
  229 |             backend_error = True
  230 |             verdict = Verdict(t, kind, None, 0.0, "", f"error: {type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:100]}")
  231 |         verdict.latency_s = time.monotonic() - t0
  232 |         with self._lock:
  233 |             if generation == self._generation:
  234 |                 self.consecutive_errors = self.consecutive_errors + 1 if backend_error else 0
  235 |                 self.calls += 1
  236 |                 self.failures += verdict.label is None
  237 |                 self.last[kind] = verdict
  238 |                 self.log.append(verdict.as_dict())
  239 |         self._gate.release()
  240 | 
  241 |     # ---- output -------------------------------------------------------------
  242 |     def suspicion(self) -> float:
  243 |         """Advisory suspicion for Keel: proposal-side labels only (see module docstring)."""
  244 |         v = self.last.get("proposals")
  245 |         if (v is None or v.label is None or v.label not in self.fmt.PROPOSAL_LABELS
  246 |                 or (self._last_feed_t is not None and self._last_feed_t - v.t > VERDICT_MAX_AGE_S)):
  247 |             return 0.0
  248 |         return max(SCORE_FLOOR, min(1.0, v.score))
  249 | 
  250 |     def snapshot(self) -> dict:
  251 |         return {"model": self.model, "calls": self.calls, "failures": self.failures,
  252 |                 "suspicion": round(self.suspicion(), 2),
  253 |                 "proposals": self.last["proposals"].as_dict() if "proposals" in self.last else None,
  254 |                 "telemetry": self.last["telemetry"].as_dict() if "telemetry" in self.last else None}
  255 | 
  256 | 
  257 | def _first_installed(chain, skip: tuple, available: Callable[[str], bool]):
  258 |     return next(((f, m, c) for f, m, c in chain if m not in skip and available(m)), None)
  259 | 
  260 | 
  261 | class SplitObserver:
  262 |     """Proposals and telemetry served by separate models (module docstring). Same
  263 |     interface the engine uses for a single Observer: feed / suspicion / last /
  264 |     reset / snapshot, plus fallback() for the per-path chains."""
  265 | 
  266 |     CHAINS = {"proposals": PROPOSAL_CHAIN, "telemetry": TELEMETRY_CHAIN}
  267 |     PROPOSAL_LABELS = V2.PROPOSAL_LABELS
  268 | 
  269 |     def __init__(self, available: Callable[[str], bool] = observer_available, telemetry_specialist=None, **kw):
  270 |         self._available, self._kw = available, kw
  271 |         self.telemetry_specialist = telemetry_specialist
  272 |         self._gate = threading.Semaphore(1)
  273 |         self.skip = {k: () for k in KINDS}               # models that failed on that path
  274 |         self.paths = {k: self._build(k) for k in KINDS}
  275 | 
  276 |     def _build(self, kind: str) -> Optional[Observer]:
  277 |         pick = _first_installed(self.CHAINS[kind], self.skip[kind], self._available)
  278 |         if pick is None:
  279 |             return None
  280 |         fmt, model, num_ctx = pick
  281 |         return Observer(fmt=fmt, model=model, num_ctx=num_ctx, kinds=(kind,),
  282 |                         telemetry_specialist=self.telemetry_specialist if kind == "telemetry" and fmt is V3 else None,
  283 |                         check_every_s=SPLIT_CHECK_EVERY_S, gate=self._gate, **self._kw)
  284 | 
  285 |     @property
  286 |     def available(self) -> bool:
  287 |         return any(self.paths.values())
  288 | 
  289 |     def model(self, kind: str) -> Optional[str]:
  290 |         return self.paths[kind].model if self.paths[kind] else None
  291 | 
  292 |     def feed(self, t: float, state, intent=None, commanded=None) -> None:
  293 |         for o in self.paths.values():
  294 |             if o is not None:
  295 |                 o.feed(t, state, intent, commanded)
  296 | 
  297 |     @property
  298 |     def last(self) -> dict:
  299 |         return {k: o.last[k] for k, o in self.paths.items() if o is not None and k in o.last}
  300 | 
  301 |     def suspicion(self) -> float:
  302 |         """Proposal path only: telemetry verdicts never reach authority."""
  303 |         o = self.paths["proposals"]
  304 |         return o.suspicion() if o is not None else 0.0
  305 | 
  306 |     def reset(self) -> None:
  307 |         for o in self.paths.values():
  308 |             if o is not None:
  309 |                 o.reset()
  310 | 
  311 |     def fallback(self) -> list:
  312 |         """Move each path whose model keeps erroring down its own chain; returns
  313 |         (kind, failed model, new model or None) for every switch made."""
  314 |         out = []
  315 |         for kind, o in self.paths.items():
  316 |             if o is not None and o.consecutive_errors >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_ERRORS:
  317 |                 self.skip[kind] += (o.model,)
  318 |                 self.paths[kind] = self._build(kind)
  319 |                 out.append((kind, o.model, self.model(kind)))
  320 |         return out
  321 | 
  322 |     def snapshot(self) -> dict:
  323 |         v = self.last
  324 |         return {"models": {k: self.model(k) for k in KINDS},
  325 |                 "telemetry_specialist": self.telemetry_specialist is not None,
  326 |                 "calls": sum(o.calls for o in self.paths.values() if o),
  327 |                 "failures": sum(o.failures for o in self.paths.values() if o),
  328 |                 "suspicion": round(self.suspicion(), 2),
  329 |                 "proposals": v["proposals"].as_dict() if "proposals" in v else None,
  330 |                 "telemetry": v["telemetry"].as_dict() if "telemetry" in v else None}
  331 | 
  332 | 
  333 | def make_split_observer(available: Callable[[str], bool] = observer_available, **kw) -> Optional[SplitObserver]:
  334 |     """Proposals -> v2, telemetry -> v3 (each with its fallback chain); None if no model is installed."""
  335 |     o = SplitObserver(available=available, **kw)
  336 |     return o if o.available else None

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | """
    2 | The v2 L2 observer prompt format (observer_merged_v2), reproduced EXACTLY from its

A healthy operator holds the design targets and only backs OFF (lower pressure setpoint, less production) as pressure nears the trip; it does not raise setpoints above design.     1 | """
    2 | Sequential (cumulative) monitor -- the spec's "Lookout" (L2), advisory only.
    3 | 
    4 | BehaviorMonitor (monitor/behavior_monitor.py) judges ONE step at a time: a
    5 | setpoint jump over a cap, a rate over a cap, a frozen signal. An attacker who
    6 | keeps every step under those caps is invisible to it by construction (the
    7 | "sub-threshold / distributed" attack). This monitor looks at the TRAJECTORY of
    8 | what L3 asks for:
    9 | 
   10 |   1. CUSUM per setpoint channel  - accumulates same-direction creep that no
   11 |      single step reveals (e.g. 20 kPa steps under a 100 kPa step cap).
   12 |   2. Same-sign run length        - n consecutive moves in one direction.
   13 |   3. Rationale screen            - weak lexical check of the agent's free-text
   14 |      rationale for injection-style language (the indirect-injection surface).
   15 |   4. Keel corroboration          - if the trusted enforcer reports divergence /
   16 |      rate-bound / load-line, suspicion is floored up (L2 reads Keel *events*,
   17 |      never the SIS channel itself).
   18 | 
   19 | Output is a score in [0,1] + a short reason, i.e. the spec's SuspicionSignal.
   20 | It is ADVISORY: feed it to Keel.step(suspicion=...). It can only lower
   21 | authority there, with a floor, so a defeated or hostile L2 cannot cause an
   22 | unsafe actuation and cannot zero authority on its own.
   23 | 
   24 | Like BehaviorMonitor it reads only measured fields + requested targets.
   25 | Known limit (state it in the viva): a patient attacker can hold CUSUM below
   26 | threshold too (Distributed Detectability Band). That is why Keel, not this
   27 | class, is the gate.
   28 | """

   83 |                  leak: float = 0.97, run_alarm: int = 8, min_run: int = 3,

   85 |         self.leak, self.run_alarm, self.min_run = leak, run_alarm, min_run

   87 |         # legitimate same-direction moves doesn't peg suspicion forever. Time-based
   88 |         # (not per call) so it doesn't depend on the loop rate.
   89 |         self.decay_half_life_s = decay_half_life_s

   94 | 
   95 |     def observe(self, state: PlantState, targets: SupervisoryTargets, t: float,

  111 |             if v is None:

  117 |             if abs(d) < c.eps:

  121 |             # back-off and return scores its net displacement, not twice its size;
  122 |             # a one-way staircase has nothing to undo and scores exactly as before
  123 |             up = max(0.0, d - c.s_neg * self.leak)
  124 |             down = max(0.0, -d - c.s_pos * self.leak)
  125 |             c.s_pos = max(0.0, c.s_pos * self.leak + (up if d > 0 else d) - c.k)
  126 |             c.s_neg = max(0.0, c.s_neg * self.leak + (down if d < 0 else -d) - c.k)
  127 |             sign = 1 if d > 0 else -1
  128 |             c.run_len = c.run_len + 1 if sign == c.run_sign else 1
  129 |             c.run_sign = sign
  130 | 
  131 |         for name, c in self.ch.items():
  132 |             s = max(c.s_pos, c.s_neg)
  133 |             if s > 0:
  134 |                 cands.append((min(1.0, s / c.h), "cusum",
  135 |                               f"{name}: {'upward' if c.s_pos >= c.s_neg else 'downward'} creep "
  136 |                               f"(CUSUM {s:.1f}/{c.h:.0f})"))
  137 |             if c.run_len >= self.min_run:
  138 |                 cands.append((min(1.0, (c.run_len - self.min_run + 1) / (self.run_alarm - self.min_run + 1)),
  139 |                               "run", f"{name}: {c.run_len:.0f} consecutive same-direction moves"))
  140 | 
  141 |         rs, why = self._rationale(targets.rationale)
  142 |         if rs > 0:
  143 |             cands.append((rs, "rationale", why))
  144 | 
  145 |         codes = set(keel_codes)
  146 |         if codes & {"rate_bound", "load_line"}:
  147 |             cands.append((0.8, "keel", "enforcer reports physical trend violation"))
  148 |         elif "divergence" in codes:
  149 |             cands.append((0.6, "keel", "enforcer reports measured/SIS divergence"))
  150 | 
  151 |         score, source, reason = max(cands, key=lambda x: x[0])
  152 |         sig = Suspicion(t, score, reason, source)
  153 |         self.history.append(sig)
  154 |         return sig
  155 | 
  156 |     def reset_channel(self, name: str) -> None:
  157 |         """Call after a human-approved setpoint change so legitimate intent doesn't linger."""
  158 |         c = self.ch[name]
  159 |         c.s_pos = c.s_neg = 0.0
  160 |         c.run_len, c.run_sign = 0, 0
  161 | 
  162 |     def reset_all(self, baseline: Optional[Dict[str, float]] = None) -> None:
  163 |         """Clear every channel's CUSUM and run state (e.g. after an operator re-arm).
  164 |         Also forget the last setpoint: with `baseline` (e.g. the design setpoints)
  165 |         the next setpoint is measured from it, otherwise it becomes a fresh
  166 |         baseline rather than a 'move' from the pre-trip value."""
  167 |         for name, c in self.ch.items():
  168 |             self.reset_channel(name)
  169 |             c.last = (baseline or {}).get(name)
  170 | 
  171 |     def _rationale(self, text: str) -> Tuple[float, str]:
  172 |         hits = [(w, p.pattern) for p, w in self._pat if text and p.search(text)]
  173 |         if not hits:
  174 |             return 0.0, ""
  175 |         return min(1.0, sum(w for w, _ in hits)), f"rationale matches {len(hits)} injection pattern(s)"

    1 | """Small advisory telemetry classifier; JSON trees, no sklearn runtime dependency.
    2 | 
    3 | Only measured fields and commanded positions are features. This classifier does
    4 | not control valves or contribute to governance authority.
    5 | """
    6 | from __future__ import annotations
    7 | 
    8 | import hashlib
    9 | import json
   10 | import math
   11 | from itertools import pairwise
   12 | from pathlib import Path
   13 | 
   14 | FEATURE_VERSION = 1
   15 | DEFAULT_MODEL = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "model/telemetry-classifier/model.json"
   16 | CHANNELS = {"pressure": 2700., "level": 45., "f1_flow": 200., "f2_flow": 40.,
   17 |             "purge_flow": 7., "product_flow": 100., "a_in_purge": .47,
   18 |             **{f"{v}_valve_{kind}": 100. for v in ("f1", "f2", "purge", "product") for kind in ("pos", "cmd")}}
   19 | 
   20 | 
   21 | def _stats(xs):
   22 |     n = len(xs)
   23 |     mean = sum(xs) / n
   24 |     delta = [b - a for a, b in pairwise(xs)]
   25 |     variance = sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in xs) / n
   26 |     return [xs[0], xs[-1], mean, min(xs), max(xs), max(xs) - min(xs), math.sqrt(variance),
   27 |             xs[-1] - xs[0], max(map(abs, delta), default=0.),
   28 |             sum(abs(x) for x in delta) / max(1, len(delta)),
   29 |             sum(x == 0 for x in xs) / n, sum(abs(x) < 1e-7 for x in delta) / max(1, len(delta))]
   30 | 
   31 | 
   32 | def features(window: dict) -> list[float]:
   33 |     if window.get("input") != "telemetry":
   34 |         raise ValueError("telemetry input required")
   35 |     n = len(window.get("pressure", []))
   36 |     if n < 4 or n > 128:
   37 |         raise ValueError("telemetry window must contain 4-128 samples")
   38 |     values = []
   39 |     sensor_stats = []
   40 |     for channel, scale in CHANNELS.items():
   41 |         xs = window.get(channel)
   42 |         if not isinstance(xs, list) or len(xs) != n or any(
   43 |             isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(x) for x in xs
   44 |         ):
   45 |             raise ValueError(f"invalid channel {channel}")
   46 |         stats = _stats([x / scale for x in xs])
   47 |         values.extend(stats)
   48 |         if channel in ("pressure", "level", "f1_flow", "f2_flow", "purge_flow", "product_flow", "a_in_purge"):
   49 |             sensor_stats.append(stats)
   50 |     # Shared statistics allow detecting abnormal shapes on channels absent from training faults.
   51 |     for i in (5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11):
   52 |         values.extend(sorted(abs(s[i]) for s in sensor_stats))
   53 |     for valve, cv, scale in (("f1", 6.4046, 200.), ("f2", .4246, 40.),
   54 |                               ("purge", .352, 7.), ("product", .0417, 100.)):
   55 |         pos, cmd = window[f"{valve}_valve_pos"], window[f"{valve}_valve_cmd"]
   56 |         values.extend(_stats([(a - c) / 100 for a, c in zip(pos, cmd)]))
   57 |         expected = [cv * a * (math.sqrt(max(0, p - 100)) if valve in ("purge", "product") else 1)
   58 |                     for a, p in zip(pos, window["pressure"])]
   59 |         residual = [(q - e) / scale for q, e in zip(window[f"{valve}_flow"], expected)]
   60 |         values.extend(_stats(residual))
   61 |     return values
   62 | 
   63 | 
   64 | class TelemetryClassifier:
   65 |     def __init__(self, path: Path = DEFAULT_MODEL):
   66 |         self.data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   67 |         if self.data.get("feature_version") not in (FEATURE_VERSION, 2):
   68 |             raise ValueError("telemetry classifier feature version mismatch")
   69 | 
   70 |     def predict(self, window: dict) -> dict:
   71 |         if self.data["feature_version"] == 2:
   72 |             from monitor.physics_features import physics_features
   73 |             xs = physics_features(window)
   74 |         else:
   75 |             xs = features(window)
   76 |         if len(xs) != self.data["n_features"]:
   77 |             raise ValueError("telemetry classifier input size mismatch")
   78 |         probabilities = [0.] * len(self.data["classes"])
   79 |         for tree in self.data["trees"]:
   80 |             node = 0
   81 |             while tree["left"][node] != -1:
   82 |                 node = tree["left"][node] if xs[tree["feature"][node]] <= tree["threshold"][node] else tree["right"][node]
   83 |             for i, value in enumerate(tree["probabilities"][node]):
   84 |                 probabilities[i] += value / len(self.data["trees"])
   85 |         index = max(range(len(probabilities)), key=probabilities.__getitem__)
   86 |         label = self.data["classes"][index]
   87 |         return {"label": label, "confidence": round(probabilities[index], 4),
   88 |                 "score": round(1 - probabilities[self.data["classes"].index("normal")], 4),
   89 |                 "reason": f"Measured telemetry classifier: {label.replace('_', ' ')}.",
   90 |                 "source": "telemetry-classifier", "advisory_only": True}
   91 | 
   92 |     def correct(self, window: dict, verdict: dict, threshold: float = .7) -> dict:
   93 |         """Only add a confident fault finding to an otherwise normal LLM verdict.
   94 | 
   95 |         Existing alarms are preserved. This never changes proposal evidence or authority.
   96 |         """
   97 |         if verdict.get("label") != "normal":
   98 |             return verdict
   99 |         candidate = self.predict(window)
  100 |         if candidate["label"] in ("sensor_fault", "actuator_fault") and candidate["confidence"] >= threshold:
  101 |             return {**candidate, "source": "llm+telemetry-specialist", "llm_label": "normal"}
  102 |         return verdict
  103 | 
  104 | 
  105 | def approved_specialist():
  106 |     from monitor.physics_detector import approved_physics_detector
  107 |     physics = approved_physics_detector()
  108 |     if physics is not None:
  109 |         return physics
  110 |     policy = DEFAULT_MODEL.parent / "policy.json"
  111 |     if not policy.exists():
  112 |         return None
  113 |     data = json.loads(policy.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
  114 |     if not data.get("enabled"):
  115 |         return None
  116 |     if hashlib.sha256(DEFAULT_MODEL.read_bytes()).hexdigest() != data.get("model_sha256"):
  117 |         raise ValueError("telemetry specialist changed since validation")
  118 |     if data.get("sensor_noise_calibration"):
  119 |         raise ValueError("sensor-noise suppression is not approved for deployment")
  120 |     return TelemetryClassifier()

    1 | #include "TE_process.h"
    2 | #include <iostream>
    3 | #include <cstdlib>
    4 | 
    5 | // sensor fault modes: one active mode per sensor at a time, plus a single
    6 | // severity value whose meaning depends on the mode (see apply_sensor_fault)
    7 | static const int SENSOR_FAULT_NONE = 0;
    8 | static const int SENSOR_FAULT_FROZEN = 1;
    9 | static const int SENSOR_FAULT_DRIFT = 2;
   10 | static const int SENSOR_FAULT_NOISE = 3;
   11 | static const int SENSOR_FAULT_DROPOUT = 4;
   12 | 
   13 | double tauvlv = 2.77e-3;
   14 | double VT = 122.0e0;
   15 | double VLmax=30.0e0;
   16 | double Rgas=8.314e0;
   17 | double Tgas=373.0e0;
   18 | double Lden = 8.3e0;
   19 | double cv[4] = {6.4046, 0.4246, 0.352, 0.0417};
   20 | uint64_t tpurge;
   21 | 
   22 | // slews pos toward sp, limited to rate*dt of travel per update; rate<=0 means no limit (healthy valve)
   23 | double slew_limit(double pos, double sp, double rate, double dt) {
   24 |     if (rate <= 0.0) {
   25 |         return sp;
   26 |     }
   27 |     double max_delta = rate * dt;
   28 |     double delta = sp - pos;
   29 |     if (delta > max_delta) {
   30 |         delta = max_delta;
   31 |     } else if (delta < -max_delta) {
   32 |         delta = -max_delta;
   33 |     }
   34 |     return pos + delta;
   35 | }
   36 | 
   37 | // uniform random value in [-amplitude, +amplitude]; amplitude<=0 means no noise
   38 | double uniform_noise(double amplitude) {
   39 |     if (amplitude <= 0.0) {
   40 |         return 0.0;
   41 |     }
   42 |     double r = (double(rand()) / RAND_MAX) * 2.0 - 1.0;
   43 |     return r * amplitude;
   44 | }
   45 | 
   46 | // deterministic duty-cycle dropout: within each fixed period, the sensor
   47 | // reports a dropout (loss-of-signal) reading for the first `duty` fraction of
   48 | // the period, then a healthy reading for the rest. duty<=0 means no dropout.
   49 | bool in_dropout_phase(double now_seconds, double duty) {
   50 |     if (duty <= 0.0) {
   51 |         return false;
   52 |     }
   53 |     const double period = 10.0; // seconds
   54 |     double phase = fmod(now_seconds, period) / period;
   55 |     return phase < duty;
   56 | }
   57 | 
   58 | // applies one sensor's fault mode: tracks true_value into *measured unless a
   59 | // fault mode says otherwise, and maintains *bias (drift's accumulated
   60 | // offset) across ticks. A NAMUR NE43-style "fails low to 0" convention is
   61 | // used for dropout, matching a real transmitter with a broken/open loop.
   62 | void apply_sensor_fault(double true_value, double *measured, double *bias,
   63 |                          int mode, double severity, double dt, double now_seconds) {
   64 |     switch (mode) {
   65 |         case SENSOR_FAULT_FROZEN:
   66 |             // hold *measured at whatever it last was; nothing to do
   67 |             *bias = 0.0;
   68 |             break;
   69 |         case SENSOR_FAULT_DRIFT:
   70 |             *bias += severity * dt;
   71 |             *measured = true_value + *bias;
   72 |             break;
   73 |         case SENSOR_FAULT_NOISE:
   74 |             *bias = 0.0;
   75 |             *measured = true_value + uniform_noise(severity);
   76 |             break;
   77 |         case SENSOR_FAULT_DROPOUT:
   78 |             *bias = 0.0;
   79 |             *measured = in_dropout_phase(now_seconds, severity) ? 0.0 : true_value;
   80 |             break;
   81 |         default: // SENSOR_FAULT_NONE
   82 |             *bias = 0.0;
   83 |             *measured = true_value;
   84 |             break;
   85 |     }
   86 | }

  156 | void TE::steady_state() {
  157 |     lapack_int n, nrhs, lda, ldb, info;
  158 |     int i, j;
  159 |     double *A, *b;
  160 |     lapack_int *ipiv;
  161 |     
  162 |     //matrix inits
  163 |     n = 3; nrhs = 1;
  164 |     lda=n, ldb=nrhs;
  165 | 
  166 |     double Pa = pressure*A_in_purge;
  167 |     double Pc = pow(product_flow/(kpar*(pow(Pa,1.2))),(1/ncpar));
  168 |     C_in_purge = Pc/pressure;
  169 |     double Pb = pressure - Pa - Pc;
  170 |     B_in_purge = Pb/pressure;
  171 |     yc1 = 1 - ya1 - yb1;
  172 |     
  173 |     
  174 |     //matrix inits
  175 |     A = (double *)malloc(n*n*sizeof(double)) ;
  176 |     if (A==NULL){ printf("error of memory allocation\n"); exit(0); }
  177 |     b = (double *)malloc(n*nrhs*sizeof(double)) ;
  178 |     if (b==NULL){ printf("error of memory allocation\n"); exit(0); }
  179 |     ipiv = (lapack_int *)malloc(n*sizeof(lapack_int)) ;
  180 |     if (ipiv==NULL){ printf("error of memory allocation\n"); exit(0); }
  181 |     
  182 |     //lapack wants the matrix in row major form
  183 |     A[0] = ya1;
  184 |     A[1] = 1;
  185 |     A[2] = -A_in_purge;
  186 |     A[3] = yb1;
  187 |     A[4] = 0;
  188 |     A[5] = -B_in_purge;
  189 |     A[6] = yc1;
  190 |     A[7] = 0;
  191 |     A[8] = -C_in_purge;
  192 |  
  193 |     b[0] = product_flow;
  194 |     b[1] = 0;
  195 |     b[2] = product_flow;
  196 |     
  197 |     
  198 |     /* Solve the equations A*X = B */
  199 |     info = LAPACKE_dgesv( LAPACK_ROW_MAJOR, n, nrhs, A, lda, ipiv,
  200 |                          b, ldb );
  201 |     /* Check for the exact singularity */
  202 |     if( info > 0 ) {
  203 |         printf( "The diagonal element of the triangular factor of A,\n" );
  204 |         printf( "U(%i,%i) is zero, so that A is singular;\n", info, info );
  205 |         printf( "the solution could not be computed.\n" );
  206 |         exit( 1 );
  207 |     }
  208 |     if (info <0) exit( 1 );
  209 |     
  210 |     f1_valve_pos = b[0]/cv[0];
  211 |     f2_valve_pos = b[1]/cv[1];
  212 |     purge_valve_pos = b[3]/(cv[2]*sqrt(pressure-100));
  213 |     product_valve_pos = product_flow/(cv[3]*sqrt(pressure-100));
  214 |     
  215 |     molar_D = 110;
  216 |     liquid_level = molar_D/8.3;
  217 |     double VV = VT-liquid_level;
  218 |     double NV = pressure*VV/(8.314*373);
  219 |     molar_A = NV*A_in_purge;
  220 |     molar_B = NV*B_in_purge;
  221 |     molar_C = NV*C_in_purge;
  222 | }

  352 |     }
  353 |     if (!f2_stuck) {
  354 |         f2_valve_pos = slew_limit(f2_valve_pos, f2_valve_sp, f2_slew_rate, dt);
  355 |     }
  356 |     if (!purge_stuck) {
  357 |         purge_valve_pos = slew_limit(purge_valve_pos, purge_valve_sp, purge_slew_rate, dt);
  358 |     }
  359 |     if (!product_stuck) {
  360 |         product_valve_pos = slew_limit(product_valve_pos, product_valve_sp, product_slew_rate, dt);
  361 |     }
  362 |     // TODO double check to make sure I didn't skip anything
  363 |     double NL = molar_D;                        // total liquid moles [kmol]
  364 |     double VL = NL/Lden;                        // liquid volume [m^3]
  365 |     double VV = VT-VL;                          // vapor volume [m^3]
  366 |     yc1 = 1.0 - ya1- yb1;                // mole fraction C in feed 1
  367 |     double NV = molar_A + molar_B + molar_C;    // total vapor moles [kmol]
  368 |     pressure = NV * Rgas * Tgas / VV;          // total pressure [kPa]
  369 |     liquid_level = VL * 100.0 / VLmax;          // liquid volume as percentage of capacity
  370 |     
  371 |     //flow rates
  372 |     f1_flow = cv[0] * f1_cv_scale * f1_valve_pos;
  373 |     f2_flow = cv[1] * f2_cv_scale * f2_valve_pos;
  374 |     if (pressure >= 100.0) {
  375 |         purge_flow = cv[2] * purge_cv_scale * purge_valve_pos * sqrt(pressure-100.0);
  376 |         product_flow = cv[3] * product_cv_scale * product_valve_pos * sqrt(pressure-100.0);
  377 |     } else {
  378 |         purge_flow = 0.0;
  379 |         product_flow = 0.0;
  380 |     }
  381 |     
  382 |     if (product_valve_pos <= 0.0) {
  383 |         product_flow = 0.0;
  384 |     }
  385 |     // if liquid level is 0 then product flow must be 0
  386 |     if (liquid_level <= 0.0) {
  387 |         product_flow = 0.0;
  388 |     }
  389 |     
  390 |     
  391 |     // vapor composition
  392 |     A_in_purge = molar_A / NV;
  393 |     B_in_purge = molar_B / NV;
  394 |     C_in_purge = molar_C / NV;
  395 |     
  396 |     // check for  delayed sampling
  397 |     if (current.tv_sec*1000000 +current.tv_usec > tpurge) {
  398 |         tpurge = tpurge + int(sampling_delay*60*60*1000000);
  399 |         printf("********************************************\n");
  400 |         for (int i=0; i++; i<3) {
  401 |             ymeas[i] = ylast[i];
  402 |         }
  403 |         ylast[0] = A_in_purge;
  404 |         ylast[1] = B_in_purge;
  405 |         ylast[2] = C_in_purge;
  406 |     }
  407 |     
  408 |     
  409 |     // reaction rate parameters
  410 |     // if 0 use defaults
  411 |     if (kpar <= 0.0) {
  412 |         kpar = 0.00117;
  413 |     }
  414 |     if (ncpar <= 0.0) {
  415 |         ncpar = 0.4;
  416 |     }
  417 |     
  418 |     double Pa = A_in_purge * pressure;
  419 |     double Pc = C_in_purge * pressure;
  420 |     double RR1 = kpar * pow(Pa,1.2)*pow(Pc,ncpar);
  421 |     
  422 | 
  423 |     dxdt_molar_A = ya1*f1_flow + f2_flow - A_in_purge*purge_flow - RR1;
  424 |     dxdt_molar_B = yb1*f1_flow - B_in_purge*purge_flow;
  425 |     dxdt_molar_C = yc1*f1_flow - C_in_purge*purge_flow - RR1;
  426 |     dxdt_molar_D = RR1 - product_flow;
  427 |     
  428 |     
  429 |     
  430 |     
  431 |     
  432 |     molar_A+= dxdt_molar_A * dt;
  433 |     molar_B+= dxdt_molar_B * dt;
  434 |     molar_C+= dxdt_molar_C * dt;
  435 |     molar_D+= dxdt_molar_D * dt;
  436 |         
  437 |     
  438 |     // check physical limits on all variables TODO move in better place
  439 |     f1_valve_pos = std::max(std::min(f1_valve_pos, 100.0), 0.0);
  440 |     f2_valve_pos = std::max(std::min(f2_valve_pos, 100.0), 0.0);
  441 |     purge_valve_pos = std::max(std::min(purge_valve_pos, 100.0), 0.0);
  442 |     product_valve_pos = std::max(std::min(product_valve_pos, 100.0), 0.0);
  443 |     liquid_level = std::max(std::min(liquid_level, 100.0), 0.0);
  444 |     pressure = std::max(std::min(pressure, 3200.0), 0.0);
  445 | 
  446 |     // fault parameters: rate must be non-negative, cv scale is a 0-1 fraction
  447 |     f1_slew_rate = std::max(f1_slew_rate, 0.0);
  448 |     f2_slew_rate = std::max(f2_slew_rate, 0.0);
  449 |     purge_slew_rate = std::max(purge_slew_rate, 0.0);
  450 |     product_slew_rate = std::max(product_slew_rate, 0.0);
  451 |     f1_cv_scale = std::max(std::min(f1_cv_scale, 1.0), 0.0);
  452 |     f2_cv_scale = std::max(std::min(f2_cv_scale, 1.0), 0.0);
  453 |     purge_cv_scale = std::max(std::min(purge_cv_scale, 1.0), 0.0);
  454 |     product_cv_scale = std::max(std::min(product_cv_scale, 1.0), 0.0);
  455 | 
  456 |     // sensor fault mode must be one of the 5 known modes; severity must be
  457 |     // non-negative (its unit/meaning depends on the mode - see apply_sensor_fault)
  458 |     tank_pressure_fault_mode = std::max(std::min(tank_pressure_fault_mode, 4), 0);
  459 |     tank_level_fault_mode = std::max(std::min(tank_level_fault_mode, 4), 0);
  460 |     f1_flow_fault_mode = std::max(std::min(f1_flow_fault_mode, 4), 0);
  461 |     f2_flow_fault_mode = std::max(std::min(f2_flow_fault_mode, 4), 0);
  462 |     purge_flow_fault_mode = std::max(std::min(purge_flow_fault_mode, 4), 0);
  463 |     product_flow_fault_mode = std::max(std::min(product_flow_fault_mode, 4), 0);
  464 |     analyzer_fault_mode = std::max(std::min(analyzer_fault_mode, 4), 0);
  465 |     tank_pressure_fault_severity = std::max(tank_pressure_fault_severity, 0.0);
  466 |     tank_level_fault_severity = std::max(tank_level_fault_severity, 0.0);
  467 |     f1_flow_fault_severity = std::max(f1_flow_fault_severity, 0.0);
  468 |     f2_flow_fault_severity = std::max(f2_flow_fault_severity, 0.0);
  469 |     purge_flow_fault_severity = std::max(purge_flow_fault_severity, 0.0);
  470 |     product_flow_fault_severity = std::max(product_flow_fault_severity, 0.0);
  471 |     analyzer_fault_severity = std::max(analyzer_fault_severity, 0.0);
  472 | 
  473 |     molar_A = std::max(molar_A, 0.0);
  474 |     molar_B = std::max(molar_B, 0.0);
  475 |     molar_C = std::max(molar_C, 0.0);
  476 |     molar_D = std::max(molar_D, 0.0);
  477 | 
  478 |     // measured (possibly faulted) sensor values: each tick, apply this
  479 |     // sensor's active fault mode (or just track the true value if healthy).
  480 |     // Modbus devices read only these measured_* fields, never the true
  481 |     // outputs above, so they stay unaware of whether a fault is active.
  482 |     double now_seconds = current.tv_sec + current.tv_usec / 1e6;
  483 |     apply_sensor_fault(pressure, &measured_pressure, &tank_pressure_bias,
  484 |                         tank_pressure_fault_mode, tank_pressure_fault_severity, dt, now_seconds);
  485 |     apply_sensor_fault(liquid_level, &measured_liquid_level, &tank_level_bias,
  486 |                         tank_level_fault_mode, tank_level_fault_severity, dt, now_seconds);
  487 |     apply_sensor_fault(f1_flow, &measured_f1_flow, &f1_flow_bias,
  488 |                         f1_flow_fault_mode, f1_flow_fault_severity, dt, now_seconds);
  489 |     apply_sensor_fault(f2_flow, &measured_f2_flow, &f2_flow_bias,
  490 |                         f2_flow_fault_mode, f2_flow_fault_severity, dt, now_seconds);
  491 |     apply_sensor_fault(purge_flow, &measured_purge_flow, &purge_flow_bias,
  492 |                         purge_flow_fault_mode, purge_flow_fault_severity, dt, now_seconds);
  493 |     apply_sensor_fault(product_flow, &measured_product_flow, &product_flow_bias,
  494 |                         product_flow_fault_mode, product_flow_fault_severity, dt, now_seconds);
  495 |     // analyzer is a single instrument: a real GC samples A/B/C together, so
  496 |     // they share one mode and one drift bias/dropout phase, not three
  497 |     // independent ones
  498 |     switch (analyzer_fault_mode) {
  499 |         case SENSOR_FAULT_FROZEN:
  500 |             analyzer_bias = 0.0;
  501 |             break;
  502 |         case SENSOR_FAULT_DRIFT:
  503 |             analyzer_bias += analyzer_fault_severity * dt;
  504 |             measured_A_in_purge = A_in_purge + analyzer_bias;
  505 |             measured_B_in_purge = B_in_purge + analyzer_bias;
  506 |             measured_C_in_purge = C_in_purge + analyzer_bias;
  507 |             break;
  508 |         case SENSOR_FAULT_NOISE:
  509 |             analyzer_bias = 0.0;
  510 |             measured_A_in_purge = A_in_purge + uniform_noise(analyzer_fault_severity);
  511 |             measured_B_in_purge = B_in_purge + uniform_noise(analyzer_fault_severity);
  512 |             measured_C_in_purge = C_in_purge + uniform_noise(analyzer_fault_severity);
  513 |             break;
  514 |         case SENSOR_FAULT_DROPOUT: {
  515 |             analyzer_bias = 0.0;
  516 |             bool dropped = in_dropout_phase(now_seconds, analyzer_fault_severity);
  517 |             measured_A_in_purge = dropped ? 0.0 : A_in_purge;
  518 |             measured_B_in_purge = dropped ? 0.0 : B_in_purge;
  519 |             measured_C_in_purge = dropped ? 0.0 : C_in_purge;
  520 |             break;
  521 |         }
  522 |         default: // SENSOR_FAULT_NONE
  523 |             analyzer_bias = 0.0;
  524 |             measured_A_in_purge = A_in_purge;
  525 |             measured_B_in_purge = B_in_purge;
  526 |             measured_C_in_purge = C_in_purge;
  527 |             break;
  528 |     }
  529 | 
  530 |     if (product_flow <= 0.0) {
  531 |         //hold at last cost
  532 |         cost = cost;
  533 |     } else {
  534 |         cost = purge_flow * (ymeas[0]*2.206 + ymeas[2]*6.177)/product_flow; // cost/mole product
  535 |     }
  536 | 
  537 | }

   14 | #include <jsoncpp/json/json.h>
   15 | #include "TE_process.h"
   16 | #define PORT 55555
   17 | #define TRUE 1
   18 | 
   19 | 
   20 | // compile with g++ example.cc TE_process.cc -ljsoncpp -llapacke -lpthread -o simulation
   21 | TE *my_te;
   22 | Json::Value inputs;
   23 | Json::Value outputs;
   24 | pthread_mutex_t simulation_lock;           // single lock used for any access to TE process, inputs, or outputs to ensure atomic operation
   25 | unsigned int process_rate = 100000;      // max of 1000000
   26 | 
   27 | void* simulation(void *ptr) {
   28 |     while (1) {
   29 |        
   30 |         /************** UPDATE PROCESS SIMULATION ***************/
   31 |         pthread_mutex_lock(&simulation_lock);
   32 |         my_te->update(inputs);
   33 |         outputs = my_te->get_state_json();
   34 |         my_te->print_outputs();
   35 |         pthread_mutex_unlock(&simulation_lock);       
   36 |         
   37 |         usleep(process_rate);
   38 |         
   39 |     }
   40 | 
   41 | 
   42 | }
   43 | 
   44 | int main(void) {
   45 |     Json::Reader reader;
   46 |     Json::FastWriter writer;
   47 |     Json::Value command;
   48 |     pthread_t process_thread;
   49 |     struct timeval timeout;
   50 |     timeout.tv_sec = 1;      // seconds
   51 |     timeout.tv_usec = 0;     // microseconds
   52 | 
   53 |     
   54 | 
   55 |     int opt = TRUE;  
   56 |     int master_socket , addrlen , new_socket , client_socket[30] , 
   57 |           max_clients = 30 , activity, i , valread , sd;  
   58 |     int max_sd;  
   59 |     struct sockaddr_in address;  
   60 |         
   61 |     char buffer[1025];  //data buffer of 1K 
   62 |         
   63 |     //set of socket descriptors 
   64 |     fd_set readfds;  
   65 |         
   66 | 
   67 |     
   68 |     //initialize TE process
   69 |     my_te = new TE();
   70 |     my_te->update(inputs);
   71 | 
   72 |     //initialise all client_socket[] to 0 so not checked 
   73 |     for (i = 0; i < max_clients; i++)  
   74 |     {  
   75 |         client_socket[i] = 0;  
   76 |     }  
   77 |         
   78 |     //create a master socket 
   79 |     if( (master_socket = socket(AF_INET , SOCK_STREAM , 0)) == 0)  
   80 |     {  
   81 |         perror("socket failed");  
   82 |         exit(EXIT_FAILURE);  
   83 |     }  
   84 |     
   85 |     //set master socket to allow multiple connections , 
   86 |     //this is just a good habit, it will work without this 
   87 |     if( setsockopt(master_socket, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, (char *)&opt, 
   88 |           sizeof(opt)) < 0 )  
   89 |     {  
   90 |         perror("setsockopt");  
   91 |         exit(EXIT_FAILURE);  
   92 |     }  
   93 |     
   94 |     //type of socket created 
   95 |     address.sin_family = AF_INET;  
   96 |     address.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY;  
   97 |     address.sin_port = htons( PORT );  
   98 |         
   99 |     //bind the socket to localhost port 55555 
  100 |     if (bind(master_socket, (struct sockaddr *)&address, sizeof(address))<0)  
  101 |     {  
  102 |         perror("bind failed");  
  103 |         exit(EXIT_FAILURE);  
  104 |     }  
  105 |     printf("Listener on port %d \n", PORT);  
  106 |         
  107 |     //try to specify maximum of 10 pending connections for the master socket 
  108 |     if (listen(master_socket, 10) < 0)  
  109 |     {  
  110 |         perror("listen");  
  111 |         exit(EXIT_FAILURE);  
  112 |     }  
  113 |         
  114 |     //accept the incoming connection 
  115 |     addrlen = sizeof(address);  
  116 |     puts("Waiting for connections ...");  
  117 |         
  118 |     while(TRUE)  
  119 |     {  
  120 |         my_te->update(inputs);
  121 |         //clear the socket set 
  122 |         FD_ZERO(&readfds);  
  123 |     
  124 |         //add master socket to set 
  125 |         FD_SET(master_socket, &readfds);  
  126 |         max_sd = master_socket;  
  127 |             
  128 |         //add child sockets to set 
  129 |         for ( i = 0 ; i < max_clients ; i++)  
  130 |         {  
  131 |             //socket descriptor 
  132 |             sd = client_socket[i];  
  133 |                 
  134 |             //if valid socket descriptor then add to read list 
  135 |             if(sd > 0)  
  136 |                 FD_SET( sd , &readfds);  
  137 |                 
  138 |             //highest file descriptor number, need it for the select function 
  139 |             if(sd > max_sd)  
  140 |                 max_sd = sd;  
  141 |         }  
  142 | 
  143 |         timeout.tv_sec = 1;
  144 |         timeout.tv_usec = 0;
  145 |     
  146 |         //wait for an activity on one of the sockets
  147 |         activity = select( max_sd + 1 , &readfds , NULL , NULL , &timeout);  
  148 |       
  149 |         if ((activity < 0) && (errno!=EINTR))  
  150 |         {  
  151 |             printf("select error");  
  152 |         }  
  153 |             
  154 |         //If something happened on the master socket , 
  155 |         //then its an incoming connection 
  156 |         if (FD_ISSET(master_socket, &readfds))  
  157 |         {  
  158 |             if ((new_socket = accept(master_socket, 
  159 |                     (struct sockaddr *)&address, (socklen_t*)&addrlen))<0)  
  160 |             {  
  161 |                 perror("accept");  
  162 |                 exit(EXIT_FAILURE);  
  163 |             }  
  164 |             
  165 |             //inform user of socket number - used in send and receive commands 
  166 |             printf("New connection , socket fd is %d , ip is : %s , port : %d \n" , new_socket , inet_ntoa(address.sin_addr) , ntohs
  167 |                   (address.sin_port));  
  168 |           
  169 |                 
  170 |             //add new socket to array of sockets 
  171 |             for (i = 0; i < max_clients; i++)  
  172 |             {  
  173 |                 //if position is empty 
  174 |                 if( client_socket[i] == 0 )  
  175 |                 {  
  176 |                     client_socket[i] = new_socket;  
  177 |                     printf("Adding to list of sockets as %d\n" , i);  
  178 |                         
  179 |                     break;  
  180 |                 }  
  181 |             }  
  182 |         }  
  183 |             
  184 |         //else its some IO operation on some other socket
  185 |         for (i = 0; i < max_clients; i++)  
  186 |         {  
  187 |             sd = client_socket[i];  
  188 |                 
  189 |             if (FD_ISSET( sd , &readfds))  
  190 |             {  
  191 |                 //Check if it was for closing , and also read the 
  192 |                 //incoming message 
  193 |                 if ((valread = read( sd , buffer, 1024)) == 0)  
  194 |                 {  
  195 |                     //Somebody disconnected , get his details and print 
  196 |                     getpeername(sd , (struct sockaddr*)&address , \
  197 |                         (socklen_t*)&addrlen);  
  198 |                     printf("Host disconnected , ip %s , port %d \n" , inet_ntoa(address.sin_addr) , ntohs(address.sin_port));  
  199 |                         
  200 |                     //Close the socket and mark as 0 in list for reuse 
  201 |                     close( sd );  
  202 |                     client_socket[i] = 0;  
  203 |                 }   
  204 |                     
  205 |                     // PROCESS INPUTS OR OUTPUTS
  206 |                 else
  207 |                 {  
  208 |                     bool reader_stat = reader.parse(buffer,command);
  209 |                     if (reader_stat) {
  210 |                         if (command.isMember("request")) {
  211 |                             if (command["request"] == "read") {
  212 |                                 outputs = my_te->get_state_json();
  213 |                                 std::string response = writer.write(outputs);

  223 |                             } else {
  224 |                                 //invalid json message
  225 |

  227 |                         }
  228 |                     } else {
  229 |                         //invalid json format
  230 |                     }
  231 |                 }  
  232 |             }  
  233 |         }  
  234 |     }
  235 | 
  236 |     return 0;
  237 | }

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | """
    2 | Reset the plant container to its designed operating point and confirm it has
    3 | settled before a run depends on it.
    4 | 
    5 | Why this exists: PlantService doesn't persist any state of its own, but the
    6 | simulator container does, in the running TE process - whatever valve
    7 | positions, e_stop, and sensor faults a previous run or test left behind carry
    8 | over into the next one. A run that assumes it's starting near the ~2700 kPa /
    9 | ~44% design point can instead inherit a mid-transient state (e.g. valves
   10 | pinned wide open from an aborted trip test), which silently turns a
   11 | "baseline holds in band" demo into a recovery-transient demo, or makes an
   12 | interlock trip test time out because truth is starting far from the limit.
   13 | 
   14 | What `docker compose restart simulation` does: it restarts the container's
   15 | PID 1 (supervisord), which respawns the simulation binary. The TE object
   16 | lives only in that process's memory (no volume persists it), so a fresh
   17 | process means a fresh TE() constructor - which calls steady_state() and
   18 | lands pressure at 2700 kPa, liquid_level at ~44.2%, and all four valves at
   19 | their physics-derived steady positions. Confirmed empirically: after a
   20 | restart, truth drifts <1 kPa over the first 12 reads with no valve commands
   21 | sent - it is already essentially settled, not just pointed at a target. This
   22 | script still polls for stability rather than assuming that, so it also works
   23 | if a future image version needs a real warmup.
   24 | 
   25 | Usage:
   26 |     python -m scripts.reset_plant                 # restart + wait, print the settled point
   27 |     python -m scripts.reset_plant --no-restart     # skip the restart, just wait/confirm settled
   28 | 
   29 | As a library:
   30 |     from scripts.reset_plant import reset_and_settle
   31 |     point = reset_and_settle()   # dict: pressure, level, valve positions, cycles_to_settle
   32 | """
   33 | 
   34 | from __future__ import annotations
   35 |

   45 |

   47 | HOST, PORT = "127.0.0.1", 55555
   48 | 
   49 | # GRFICS bug workaround. TE::steady_state() (simulation/simulation/TE_process.cc) solves
   50 | # the three design flows into b[0..2] but sets the purge valve from b[3], one past the
   51 | # end of the array, so a fresh simulator starts with the purge at memory garbage (~0)
   52 | # instead of its design opening. Feed 1 carries 0.5% inert B whose only exit is the
   53 | # purge, so with the purge shut B piles up and pressure creeps up ~3 kPa/min at the
   54 | # "design point", faster the more feed 1 is open. The value below is what the
   55 | # simulator's own steady-state equations give for the purge valve (purge flow
   56 | # 7.05 kmol/h at 2700 kPa); measured live it holds pressure flat (-0.2 kPa/min).
   57 | DESIGN_PURGE_VALVE_PCT = 0.3926

   82 | def wait_reachable(host: str = HOST, port: int = PORT, timeout_s: float = 60.0) -> None:
   83 |     """Block until the simulator accepts a TCP connection, or raise TimeoutError."""
   84 |     deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_s
   85 |     last_err: Optional[Exception] = None
   86 |     while time.monotonic() < deadline:

   88 |             with socket.create_connection((host, port), timeout=2):
