  459 |     fitView();
  460 |   });
  461 | 
  462 |   $("valveList").addEventListener("click", e => {
  463 |     const t = /** @type {HTMLElement} */ (e.target);
  464 |     const row = /** @type {HTMLElement | null} */ (t.closest(".valve"));
  465 |     if (!row) return;
  466 |     const k = /** @type {Valve} */ (row.dataset.valve);
  467 |     if (t.matches(".step")) move({variable: k, delta: Number(t.dataset.d)});
  468 |     if (t.matches("[data-apply]")) {
  469 |       const input = valveEls[k].input, v = parseFloat(input.value);
  470 |       if (!Number.isFinite(v)) { toast("Enter a value from 0 to 100", true); return; }
  471 |       input.value = "";
  472 |       move({variable: k, value: clamp(v, 0, 100)});
  473 |     }
  474 |   });
  475 |   $("valveList").addEventListener("keydown", e => {
  476 |     const t = /** @type {HTMLElement} */ (e.target);
  477 |     if (e.key === "Enter" && t.matches("[data-in]")) /** @type {HTMLElement} */ (t.closest(".valve")?.querySelector("[data-apply]")).click();
  478 |   });
  479 |   button("btnEstop").addEventListener("click", () => move({variable: "e_stop", value: plant?.e_stop ? 0 : 1}));
  480 | 
  481 |   button("btnReset").addEventListener("click", async () => {
  482 |     resettingHere = true; render();
  483 |     try {
  484 |       const r = await post("/api/reset");
  485 |       hist.length = 0;
  486 |       toast(`Plant reset: ${fmt(r.pressure, 0)} kPa`);
  487 |       /** @type {HTMLIFrameElement} */ ($("plant3d")).src = "http://localhost/";   // the rupture latch lives in the 3D client
  488 |     } catch (e) { toast(errText(e), true); }
  489 |     resettingHere = false; render();
  490 |   });
  491 |   button("btnSave").addEventListener("click", async () => {
  492 |     try { await post("/api/ai/rescue"); toast("AI is taking control"); } catch (e) { toast(errText(e), true); }
  493 |   });
  494 |   button("btnStop").addEventListener("click", async () => {
  495 |     try { await post("/api/ai/stop"); toast("AI stopped. Manual control."); } catch (e) { toast(errText(e), true); }
  496 |   });
  497 | 
  498 |   $("cmdForm").addEventListener("submit", e => {
  499 |     e.preventDefault();
  500 |     const input = /** @type {HTMLInputElement} */ ($("cmd"));
  501 |     const text = input.value.trim();
  502 |     if (!text) return;
  503 |     queue.push(text);
  504 |     input.value = "";
  505 |     sendLabel();
  506 |     runQueue();
  507 |   });
  508 |   window.addEventListener("resize", render);
  509 | }
  510 | 
  511 | // Commands queue, so the next one can be sent while the AI is still reading the last.
  512 | /** @type {string[]} */
  513 | const queue = [];
  514 | let busy = false;
  515 | function sendLabel() {
  516 |   button("btnSend").textContent = !busy ? "Send" : queue.length ? `Working (${queue.length} waiting)` : "Working…";
  517 | }
  518 | async function runQueue() {
  519 |   if (busy) return;
  520 |   busy = true;
  521 |   while (queue.length) {
  522 |     const text = /** @type {string} */ (queue.shift());
  523 |     sendLabel();
  524 |     try { toast((await post("/api/command", {text})).message); }
  525 |     catch (e) { toast(`“${text}”: ${errText(e)}`, true); }
  526 |   }
  527 |   busy = false;
  528 |   sendLabel();
  529 | }
  530 | 
  531 | // ---------- poll
  532 | 
  533 | async function poll() {
  534 |   let again = POLL_MS;
  535 |   try {
  536 |     const res = await fetchWithTimeout(`/api/state?since=${lastSeq}&since_ai=${lastAct}`, {cache: "no-store"});
  537 |     if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
  538 |     /** @type {PlantState} */
  539 |     const s = await res.json();
  540 |     if (plant && s.t < plant.t) {
  541 |       // the server restarted: its sequence numbers and activity ids start again from 1,
  542 |       // so start over and fetch everything it has
  543 |       lastSeq = lastAct = 0;
  544 |       hist.length = feed.length = 0;
  545 |       renderFeed();
  546 |       plant = null;
  547 |       again = 0;
  548 |       return;                                   // the finally block polls again straight away
  549 |     }
  550 |     for (const row of s.history ?? []) { hist.push(row); lastSeq = row[0]; }
  551 |     if (hist.length > KEEP * 2) hist.splice(0, hist.length - KEEP);
  552 |     const acts = s.ai?.activity ?? [];
  553 |     plant = s;
  554 |     serverUp = true;
  555 |     for (const a of acts) { lastAct = a.id; feed.unshift(toFeed(a)); }
  556 |     if (feed.length > FEED_MAX) feed.length = FEED_MAX;
  557 |     if (acts.length) renderFeed();
  558 |   } catch {
  559 |     serverUp = false;
  560 |   } finally {
  561 |     render();
  562 |     setTimeout(poll, again);
  563 |   }
  564 | }
  565 | 
  566 | buildGauge();
  567 | buildValves();
  568 | buildLegend();
  569 | renderFeed();
  570 | wireEvents();
  571 | fitView();
  572 | poll();

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | # GRFICS simulator in SCRAM
    2 | 
    3 | The normal SCRAM application uses the prebuilt `fortiphyd/grfics-simulation`
    4 | image configured in [docker-compose.yml](../docker-compose.yml). Run these
    5 | commands from the repository root with Docker running:
    6 | 
    7 | ```sh
    8 | docker compose up -d simulation
    9 | docker compose ps
   10 | docker compose logs simulation
   11 | ```
   12 | 
   13 | The plant TCP endpoint is `127.0.0.1:55555`; the image's web visualization is at
   14 | `http://127.0.0.1/`. The main SCRAM UI is launched separately with `python -m live`
   15 | at port 8765. See the [project README](../README.md) for Python setup.
   16 | 
   17 | Compose runs only the simulator service, using the simulator-only supervisor
   18 | configuration in `docker/`. It does not launch the original full GRFICS lab.
   19 | The plant ports are unauthenticated and published on loopback.
   20 | 
   21 | ## Compile and check the bundled C++ source
   22 | 
   23 | The source under `simulation/` contains the local solver, composition-delay and
   24 | TCP framing fixes. On Ubuntu or WSL, from the repository root:
   25 | 
   26 | ```sh
   27 | sudo apt-get update
   28 | sudo apt-get install build-essential libjsoncpp-dev liblapacke-dev
   29 | mkdir -p artifacts/simulator
   30 | g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -Werror simulation/simulation/main.cc simulation/simulation/TE_process.cc -ljsoncpp -llapacke -lpthread -o artifacts/simulator/simulation
   31 | python3 scripts/check_simulator.py artifacts/simulator/simulation
   32 | ```
   33 | 
   34 | The checker launches an isolated simulator on a temporary port. Compiling this
   35 | binary does not replace the prebuilt image or establish equivalence with its
   36 | extended fault-injection behavior. Compose has no local build configured.
   37 | 
   38 | The local source now uses `b[2]` for the design purge. The Python reset helper
   39 | still applies the design purge explicitly because normal startup uses the
   40 | prebuilt image. To reset the running demonstration, use its UI reset action or
   41 | restart `python -m live` without `--no-reset`; this changes plant state.
   42 | 
   43 | ## Visualization and provenance
   44 | 
   45 | The Unity build payloads are not included in this Git checkout. The runnable
   46 | visualization comes from the Docker image; local HTML/loader files alone are
   47 | not a complete Unity build. The older VirtualBox/GRFICSv2 installation steps do
   48 | not describe this repository's setup.
   49 | 
   50 | GRFICS attribution is recorded in [README_GRFICS.md](../README_GRFICS.md), with
   51 | the inherited license in [LICENSE](../LICENSE).

    1 | #!/bin/bash
    2 | set -euo pipefail
    3 | 
    4 | # Detect interface by IP
    5 | IF=$(ip -o -4 addr show | awk '$4 ~ /^192\.168\.95\./ {print $2}' | head -n1)
    6 | if [ -z "$IF" ]; then
    7 |     echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: no interface found with 192.168.95.x address" >&2
    8 |     exit 1
    9 | fi
   10 | 
   11 | echo "[entrypoint] Adding IP aliases to $IF manually..."
   12 | 
   13 | ip addr add 192.168.95.10/24 dev "$IF"
   14 | ip addr add 192.168.95.11/24 dev "$IF"
   15 | ip addr add 192.168.95.12/24 dev "$IF"
   16 | ip addr add 192.168.95.13/24 dev "$IF"
   17 | ip addr add 192.168.95.14/24 dev "$IF"
   18 | ip addr add 192.168.95.15/24 dev "$IF"
   19 | 
   20 | route add -net 192.168.90.0/24 gw 192.168.95.200
   21 | 
   22 | echo "[entrypoint] Starting nginx..."
   23 | # Give www-data access to the Docker socket so versions.php can query container labels.
   24 | # The socket GID varies by host, so we match it dynamically rather than hardcoding.
   25 | if [ -S /var/run/docker.sock ]; then
   26 |     DOCKER_GID=$(stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock)
   27 |     # A group with this GID may already exist (e.g. 'docker' on a fresh Ubuntu install).
   28 |     # If so, reuse it rather than trying to create 'dockersock', which would fail and
   29 |     # leave no group for the subsequent usermod call.
   30 |     DOCKER_GROUP=$(getent group "$DOCKER_GID" | cut -d: -f1 || true)
   31 |     if [ -z "$DOCKER_GROUP" ]; then
   32 |         groupadd -g "$DOCKER_GID" dockersock
   33 |         DOCKER_GROUP=dockersock
   34 |     fi
   35 |     usermod -aG "$DOCKER_GROUP" www-data
   36 | fi
   37 | php-fpm8.2 -D || { echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: php-fpm failed to start" >&2; exit 1; }
   38 | nginx || { echo "[entrypoint] ERROR: nginx failed to start" >&2; exit 1; }
   39 | 
   40 | echo "[entrypoint] Starting application..."
   41 | exec "$@"

simulation/simulation/TE_process.cc
Basic local reactor implementation: LAPACK steady-state solution, wall-clock Euler integration, species balances, pressure/flow equations, E-stop and JSON outputs. Does not supply the deployed measured/fault channel.
================================================================================================

Reading approach: follow declarations and setup first, then event handlers/loops, branch conditions and cleanup. The file role above and Study Guide describe the subsystem-specific semantics.

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | #include "TE_process.h"
    2 | #include <iostream>
    3 | double tauvlv = 2.77e-3;
    4 | double VT = 122.0e0;
    5 | double VLmax=30.0e0;
    6 | double Rgas=8.314e0;
    7 | double Tgas=373.0e0;
    8 | double Lden = 8.3e0;
    9 | double cv[4] = {6.4046, 0.4246, 0.352, 0.0417};
   10 | uint64_t tpurge;
   11 | TE::TE() {
   12 |     gettimeofday(&current, NULL);
   13 |     last_update = current;
   14 |     e_stop = 0;
   15 |     pressure = 2700;
   16 |     product_flow = 100;
   17 |     A_in_purge = 0.47;
   18 |     ya1 = 0.485;
   19 |     yb1 = 0.005;
   20 |     kpar = 0.00117;
   21 |     ncpar = 0.4;

   28 |     ylast[2] = C_in_purge;

   30 |     ymeas[1] = ylast[1];
   31 |     ymeas[2] = ylast[2];

   33 |

   35 | 
   36 | void TE::steady_state() {
   37 |     lapack_int n, nrhs, lda, ldb, info;
   38 |     double *A, *b;
   39 |     lapack_int *ipiv;
   40 |     
   41 |     //matrix inits
   42 |     n = 3; nrhs = 1;
   43 |     lda=n, ldb=nrhs;
   44 | 
   45 |     double Pa = pressure*A_in_purge;
   46 |     double Pc = pow(product_flow/(kpar*(pow(Pa,1.2))),(1/ncpar));
   47 |     C_in_purge = Pc/pressure;
   48 |     double Pb = pressure - Pa - Pc;
   49 |     B_in_purge = Pb/pressure;
   50 |     yc1 = 1 - ya1 - yb1;
   51 |     
   52 |     
   53 |     //matrix inits
   54 |     A = (double *)malloc(n*n*sizeof(double)) ;
   55 |     if (A==NULL){ printf("error of memory allocation\n"); exit(0); }
   56 |     b = (double *)malloc(n*nrhs*sizeof(double)) ;
   57 |     if (b==NULL){ printf("error of memory allocation\n"); exit(0); }
   58 |     ipiv = (lapack_int *)malloc(n*sizeof(lapack_int)) ;
   59 |     if (ipiv==NULL){ printf("error of memory allocation\n"); exit(0); }
   60 |     
   61 |     //lapack wants the matrix in row major form
   62 |     A[0] = ya1;
   63 |     A[1] = 1;
   64 |     A[2] = -A_in_purge;
   65 |     A[3] = yb1;
   66 |     A[4] = 0;
   67 |     A[5] = -B_in_purge;
   68 |     A[6] = yc1;
   69 |     A[7] = 0;
   70 |     A[8] = -C_in_purge;
   71 |  
   72 |     b[0] = product_flow;
   73 |     b[1] = 0;
   74 |     b[2] = product_flow;
   75 |     
   76 |     
   77 |     /* Solve the equations A*X = B */
   78 |     info = LAPACKE_dgesv( LAPACK_ROW_MAJOR, n, nrhs, A, lda, ipiv,
   79 |                          b, ldb );
   80 |     /* Check for the exact singularity */
   81 |     if( info > 0 ) {
   82 |         printf( "The diagonal element of the triangular factor of A,\n" );
   83 |         printf( "U(%i,%i) is zero, so that A is singular;\n", info, info );
   84 |         printf( "the solution could not be computed.\n" );
   85 |         exit( 1 );
   86 |     }
   87 |     if (info <0) exit( 1 );
   88 |     
   89 |     f1_valve_pos = b[0]/cv[0];
   90 |     f2_valve_pos = b[1]/cv[1];
   91 |     purge_valve_pos = b[2]/(cv[2]*sqrt(pressure-100));
   92 |     product_valve_pos = product_flow/(cv[3]*sqrt(pressure-100));
   93 |     
   94 |     molar_D = 110;
   95 |     liquid_level = molar_D/8.3;
   96 |     double VV = VT-liquid_level;
   97 |     double NV = pressure*VV/(8.314*373);
   98 |     molar_A = NV*A_in_purge;
   99 |     molar_B = NV*B_in_purge;
  100 |     molar_C = NV*C_in_purge;
  101 |     free(A);
  102 |     free(b);
  103 |     free(ipiv);
  104 | } 
  105 | 
  106 | 
  107 | void TE::update(Json::Value inputs) {
  108 |     //TODO limit valve positions, water level, and pressure 
  109 |     // TODO only modify given inputs
  110 |     double f1_valve_sp = f1_valve_pos;
  111 |     double f2_valve_sp = f2_valve_pos;
  112 |     double purge_valve_sp = purge_valve_pos;
  113 |     double product_valve_sp = product_valve_pos;
  114 |

  116 |     if (inputs["inputs"].isMember("e_stop")) {

  118 |                 e_stop = 1;
  119 |            } else {
  120 |                 e_stop = 0;
  121 |            }
  122 |     }
  123 |     if (e_stop) {
  124 |         f1_valve_sp = 0.0;
  125 |         f2_valve_sp = 0.0;
  126 |         purge_valve_sp = 100.0;
  127 |         product_valve_sp = 100.0;
  128 |     } else {
  129 | 
  130 |         if (inputs["inputs"].isMember("f1_valve_sp")) {
  131 |             f1_valve_sp = inputs["inputs"]["f1_valve_sp"].asDouble();
  132 |         }
  133 |         if (inputs["inputs"].isMember("f2_valve_sp")) {
  134 |             f2_valve_sp = inputs["inputs"]["f2_valve_sp"].asDouble();
  135 |         }
  136 |         if (inputs["inputs"].isMember("purge_valve_sp")) {
  137 |             purge_valve_sp = inputs["inputs"]["purge_valve_sp"].asDouble();
  138 |         }
  139 |         if (inputs["inputs"].isMember("product_valve_sp")) {
  140 |             product_valve_sp = inputs["inputs"]["product_valve_sp"].asDouble();
  141 |         }
  142 |     }
  143 | 
  144 |     last_update = current;
  145 |     gettimeofday(&current, NULL);
  146 |     double dt = ((current.tv_sec - last_update.tv_sec) + (current.tv_usec - last_update.tv_usec)/1000000.0)/60/60; //measurements are in hours
  147 |     dt = dt*time_scale;
  148 |     f1_valve_pos = f1_valve_sp;
  149 |     f2_valve_pos = f2_valve_sp;
  150 |     purge_valve_pos = purge_valve_sp;
  151 |     product_valve_pos = product_valve_sp;
  152 |     // TODO double check to make sure I didn't skip anything
  153 |     double NL = molar_D;                        // total liquid moles [kmol]
  154 |     double VL = NL/Lden;                        // liquid volume [m^3]
  155 |     double VV = VT-VL;                          // vapor volume [m^3]
  156 |     yc1 = 1.0 - ya1- yb1;                // mole fraction C in feed 1
  157 |     double NV = molar_A + molar_B + molar_C;    // total vapor moles [kmol]
  158 |     pressure = NV * Rgas * Tgas / VV;          // total pressure [kPa]
  159 |     liquid_level = VL * 100.0 / VLmax;          // liquid volume as percentage of capacity
  160 |     
  161 |     //flow rates
  162 |     f1_flow = cv[0] * f1_valve_pos;
  163 |     f2_flow = cv[1] * f2_valve_pos;
  164 |     if (pressure >= 100.0) {
  165 |         purge_flow = cv[2] * purge_valve_pos * sqrt(pressure-100.0);  
  166 |         product_flow = cv[3] * product_valve_pos * sqrt(pressure-100.0);
  167 |     } else {
  168 |         purge_flow = 0.0;
  169 |         product_flow = 0.0;
  170 |     }
  171 |     
  172 |     if (product_valve_pos <= 0.0) {
  173 |         product_flow = 0.0;
  174 |     }
  175 |     // if liquid level is 0 then product flow must be 0
  176 |     if (liquid_level <= 0.0) {
  177 |         product_flow = 0.0;
  178 |     }
  179 |     
  180 |     
  181 |     // vapor composition
  182 |     A_in_purge = molar_A / NV;
  183 |     B_in_purge = molar_B / NV;
  184 |     C_in_purge = molar_C / NV;
  185 |     
  186 |     // check for  delayed sampling
  187 |     if (static_cast<uint64_t>(current.tv_sec*1000000 +current.tv_usec) > tpurge) {
  188 |         tpurge = tpurge + int(sampling_delay*60*60*1000000);
  189 |         printf("********************************************\n");
  190 |         for (int i=0; i<3; i++) {
  191 |             ymeas[i] = ylast[i];
  192 |         }
  193 |         ylast[0] = A_in_purge;
  194 |         ylast[1] = B_in_purge;
  195 |         ylast[2] = C_in_purge;
  196 |     }
  197 |     
  198 |     
  199 |     // reaction rate parameters
  200 |     // if 0 use defaults
  201 |     if (kpar <= 0.0) {
  202 |         kpar = 0.00117;
  203 |     }
  204 |     if (ncpar <= 0.0) {
  205 |         ncpar = 0.4;
  206 |     }
  207 |     
  208 |     double Pa = A_in_purge * pressure;
  209 |     double Pc = C_in_purge * pressure;
  210 |     double RR1 = kpar * pow(Pa,1.2)*pow(Pc,ncpar);
  211 |     
  212 | 
  213 |     dxdt_molar_A = ya1*f1_flow + f2_flow - A_in_purge*purge_flow - RR1;
  214 |     dxdt_molar_B = yb1*f1_flow - B_in_purge*purge_flow;
  215 |     dxdt_molar_C = yc1*f1_flow - C_in_purge*purge_flow - RR1;
  216 |     dxdt_molar_D = RR1 - product_flow;
  217 |     
  218 |     
  219 |     
  220 |     
  221 |     
  222 |     molar_A+= dxdt_molar_A * dt;
  223 |     molar_B+= dxdt_molar_B * dt;
  224 |     molar_C+= dxdt_molar_C * dt;
  225 |     molar_D+= dxdt_molar_D * dt;
  226 |         
  227 |     
  228 |     // check physical limits on all variables TODO move in better place
  229 |     f1_valve_pos = std::max(std::min(f1_valve_pos, 100.0), 0.0);
  230 |     f2_valve_pos = std::max(std::min(f2_valve_pos, 100.0), 0.0);
  231 |     purge_valve_pos = std::max(std::min(purge_valve_pos, 100.0), 0.0);
  232 |     product_valve_pos = std::max(std::min(product_valve_pos, 100.0), 0.0);
  233 |     liquid_level = std::max(std::min(liquid_level, 100.0), 0.0);
  234 |     pressure = std::max(std::min(pressure, 3200.0), 0.0);
  235 |     
  236 |     molar_A = std::max(molar_A, 0.0);
  237 |     molar_B = std::max(molar_B, 0.0);
  238 |     molar_C = std::max(molar_C, 0.0);
  239 |     molar_D = std::max(molar_D, 0.0);
  240 | 
  241 |     
  242 |     
  243 |     
  244 |     if (product_flow <= 0.0) {
  245 |         //hold at last cost
  246 |         cost = cost;
  247 |     } else {
  248 |         cost = purge_flow * (ymeas[0]*2.206 + ymeas[2]*6.177)/product_flow; // cost/mole product
  249 |     }
  250 | 
  251 | }

   22 | static bool send_frame(int fd, const std::string &frame) {
   23 |     size_t sent = 0;
   24 |     while (sent < frame.size()) {
   25 |         ssize_t n = send(fd, frame.data() + sent, frame.size() - sent, MSG_NOSIGNAL);
   26 |         if (n < 0 && errno == EINTR) continue;
   27 |         if (n <= 0) return false;
   28 |         sent += static_cast<size_t>(n);
   29 |     }
   30 |     return true;
   31 | }

   70 | def setup_server(description=None, context=None, cmdline=None):
   71 |     """Run server setup."""
   72 |     args = helper.get_commandline(server=True, description=description, cmdline=cmdline)
   73 |     if context:
   74 |         args.context = context
   75 |     datablock: Callable[[], Any]
   76 |     if not args.context:
   77 |         _logger.info("### Create datastore")
   78 |         # The datastores only respond to the addresses that are initialized
   79 |         # If you initialize a DataBlock to addresses of 0x00 to 0xFF, a request to
   80 |         # 0x100 will respond with an invalid address exception.
   81 |         # This is because many devices exhibit this kind of behavior (but not all)
   82 |         if args.store == "sequential":
   83 |             # Continuing, use a sequential block without gaps.
   84 |             datablock = lambda : ModbusSequentialDataBlock(0x00, [17] * 100)  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment
   85 |         elif args.store == "sparse":
   86 |             # Continuing, or use a sparse DataBlock which can have gaps
   87 |             datablock = lambda : ModbusSparseDataBlock({0x00: 0, 0x05: 1})  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment
   88 |         elif args.store == "factory":
   89 |             # Alternately, use the factory methods to initialize the DataBlocks
   90 |             # or simply do not pass them to have them initialized to 0x00 on the
   91 |             # full address range::
   92 |             datablock = lambda : ModbusSequentialDataBlock.create()  # pylint: disable=unnecessary-lambda-assignment,unnecessary-lambda
   93 | 
   94 |         if args.slaves > 1:
   95 |             # The server then makes use of a server context that allows the server
   96 |             # to respond with different slave contexts for different slave ids.
   97 |             # By default it will return the same context for every slave id supplied
   98 |             # (broadcast mode).
   99 |             # However, this can be overloaded by setting the single flag to False and
  100 |             # then supplying a dictionary of slave id to context mapping::
  101 |             context = {}
  102 | 
  103 |             for slave in range(args.slaves):
  104 |                 context[slave] = ModbusSlaveContext(
  105 |                     di=datablock(),
  106 |                     co=datablock(),
  107 |                     hr=datablock(),
  108 |                     ir=datablock(),
  109 |                 )
  110 | 
  111 |             single = False
  112 |         else:
  113 |             context = ModbusSlaveContext(
  114 |                 di=datablock(), co=datablock(), hr=datablock(), ir=datablock()
  115 |             )
  116 |             single = True
  117 | 
  118 |         # Build data storage
  119 |         args.context = ModbusServerContext(slaves=context, single=single)
  120 | 
  121 |     # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- #
  122 |     # initialize the server information
  123 |     # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- #
  124 |     # If you don't set this or any fields, they are defaulted to empty strings.
  125 |     # ----------------------------------------------------------------------- #
  126 |     args.identity = ModbusDeviceIdentification(
  127 |         info_name={
  128 |             "VendorName": "Pymodbus",
  129 |             "ProductCode": "PM",
  130 |             "VendorUrl": "https://github.com/pymodbus-dev/pymodbus/",
  131 |             "ProductName": "Pymodbus Server",
  132 |             "ModelName": "Pymodbus Server",
  133 |             "MajorMinorRevision": pymodbus_version,
  134 |         }
  135 |     )
  136 |     return args
  137 | 
  138 | 
  139 | async def run_async_server(args) -> None:
  140 |     """Run server."""
  141 |     txt = f"### start ASYNC server, listening on {args.port} - {args.comm}"
  142 |     _logger.info(txt)
  143 |     if args.comm == "tcp":
  144 |         address = (args.host if args.host else "", args.port if args.port else None)
  145 |         await StartAsyncTcpServer(
  146 |             context=args.context,  # Data storage
  147 |             identity=args.identity,  # server identify
  148 |             address=address,  # listen address
  149 |             # custom_functions=[],  # allow custom handling
  150 |             framer=args.framer,  # The framer strategy to use
  151 |             # ignore_missing_slaves=True,  # ignore request to a missing slave
  152 |             # broadcast_enable=False,  # treat slave 0 as broadcast address,
  153 |             # timeout=1,  # waiting time for request to complete
  154 |         )
  155 |     elif args.comm == "udp":
  156 |         address = (
  157 |             args.host if args.host else "127.0.0.1",
  158 |             args.port if args.port else None,
  159 |         )
  160 |         await StartAsyncUdpServer(
  161 |             context=args.context,  # Data storage
  162 |             identity=args.identity,  # server identify
  163 |             address=address,  # listen address
  164 |             # custom_functions=[],  # allow custom handling
  165 |             framer=args.framer,  # The framer strategy to use
  166 |             # ignore_missing_slaves=True,  # ignore request to a missing slave
  167 |             # broadcast_enable=False,  # treat slave 0 as broadcast address,
  168 |             # timeout=1,  # waiting time for request to complete
  169 |         )
  170 |     elif args.comm == "serial":
  171 |         # socat -d -d PTY,link=/tmp/ptyp0,raw,echo=0,ispeed=9600
  172 |         #             PTY,link=/tmp/ttyp0,raw,echo=0,ospeed=9600
  173 |         await StartAsyncSerialServer(
  174 |             context=args.context,  # Data storage
  175 |             identity=args.identity,  # server identify
  176 |             # timeout=1,  # waiting time for request to complete
  177 |             port=args.port,  # serial port
  178 |             # custom_functions=[],  # allow custom handling
  179 |             framer=args.framer,  # The framer strategy to use
  180 |             # stopbits=1,  # The number of stop bits to use
  181 |             # bytesize=8,  # The bytesize of the serial messages
  182 |             # parity="N",  # Which kind of parity to use
  183 |             baudrate=args.baudrate,  # The baud rate to use for the serial device
  184 |             # handle_local_echo=False,  # Handle local echo of the USB-to-RS485 adaptor
  185 |             # ignore_missing_slaves=True,  # ignore request to a missing slave
  186 |             # broadcast_enable=False,  # treat slave 0 as broadcast address,
  187 |         )
  188 |     elif args.comm == "tls":
  189 |         address = (args.host if args.host else "", args.port if args.port else None)
  190 |         await StartAsyncTlsServer(
  191 |             context=args.context,  # Data storage
  192 |             # port=port,  # on which port
  193 |             identity=args.identity,  # server identify
  194 |             # custom_functions=[],  # allow custom handling
  195 |             address=address,  # listen address
  196 |             framer=args.framer,  # The framer strategy to use
  197 |             certfile=helper.get_certificate(
  198 |                 "crt"
  199 |             ),  # The cert file path for TLS (used if sslctx is None)
  200 |             # sslctx=sslctx,  # The SSLContext to use for TLS (default None and auto create)
  201 |             keyfile=helper.get_certificate(
  202 |                 "key"
  203 |             ),  # The key file path for TLS (used if sslctx is None)
  204 |             # password="none",  # The password for for decrypting the private key file
  205 |             # ignore_missing_slaves=True,  # ignore request to a missing slave
  206 |             # broadcast_enable=False,  # treat slave 0 as broadcast address,
  207 |             # timeout=1,  # waiting time for request to complete
  208 |         )

  336 |   function openTool(name) {
  337 |     const host = window.location.hostname;
  338 |     const endpoints = toolEndpoints[host] || toolEndpoints["localhost"];
  339 |     const url = endpoints[name];
  340 | 
  341 |     if (!url) {
  342 |       alert(`No URL configured for ${name} on host ${host}`);
  343 |       return;
  344 |     }
  345 | 
  346 |     window.open(url, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer");
  347 |   }
  348 | 
  349 |   function getToolUrl(name) {
  350 |     const host = window.location.hostname;
  351 |     const endpoints = toolEndpoints[host] || toolEndpoints["localhost"];
  352 |     return endpoints[name] || null;
  353 |   }
  354 | 
  355 |   function setStatus(text, color) {
  356 |     const label = document.getElementById("statusLabel");
  357 |     const dot = document.getElementById("statusDot");
  358 |     if (label) label.textContent = text;
  359 |     if (dot && color) dot.style.background = color;
  360 |   }
  361 | 
  362 |   // ---- Tool status polling (stable + no flicker) ----
  363 | 
  364 |   // Tuning knobs
  365 |   const POLL_MS_STABLE = 6000;   // when stable, check less often
  366 |   const POLL_MS_UNSTABLE = 1500; // when starting/flapping, check more often
  367 |   const STREAK_TO_CHANGE = 2;    // require 2 consecutive results to flip state
  368 | 
  369 |   const toolState = {
  370 |     attacker: { current: null, okStreak: 0, failStreak: 0 },
  371 |     defender: { current: null, okStreak: 0, failStreak: 0 },
  372 |     caldera:  { current: null, okStreak: 0, failStreak: 0 },
  373 |     wazuh:    { current: null, okStreak: 0, failStreak: 0 },
  374 |   };
  375 | 
  376 |   function setToolStatus(toolName, ok, detailText) {
  377 |     const dot = document.getElementById(`${toolName}Dot`);
  378 |     const text = document.getElementById(`${toolName}Text`);
  379 |     if (!dot || !text) return;
  380 | 
  381 |     if (ok === true) {
  382 |       dot.style.background = "#37d67a";
  383 |       dot.style.boxShadow = "0 0 0 3px rgba(55,214,122,0.12)";
  384 |       text.textContent = detailText || "Reachable";
  385 |     } else if (ok === false) {
  386 |       dot.style.background = "#ffd166"; // yellow for "Starting…"
  387 |       dot.style.boxShadow = "0 0 0 3px rgba(255,209,102,0.12)";
  388 |       text.textContent = detailText || "Starting…";
  389 |     } else {
  390 |       dot.style.background = "#6b7280"; // gray for unknown/checking
  391 |       dot.style.boxShadow = "0 0 0 3px rgba(107,114,128,0.12)";
  392 |       text.textContent = detailText || "Checking…";
  393 |     }
  394 |   }
  395 | 
  396 |   async function checkTool(name) {
  397 |     const url = getToolUrl(name);
  398 |     if (!url) {
  399 |       return false;
  400 |     }
  401 | 
  402 |     try {
  403 |       const ctrl = new AbortController();
  404 |       const t = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), 900);
  405 | 
  406 |       await fetch(url, {
  407 |         mode: "no-cors",
  408 |         cache: "no-store",
  409 |         signal: ctrl.signal
  410 |       });
  411 | 
  412 |       clearTimeout(t);
  413 |       return true;
  414 |     } catch {
  415 |       return false;
  416 |     }
  417 |   }
  418 | 
  419 |   function applyStabilizedResult(name, okNow) {
  420 |     const s = toolState[name];
  421 | 
  422 |     if (okNow) {
  423 |       s.okStreak += 1;
  424 |       s.failStreak = 0;
  425 |     } else {
  426 |       s.failStreak += 1;
  427 |       s.okStreak = 0;
  428 |     }
  429 | 
  430 |     // Only flip state after we see a streak
  431 |     if (okNow && s.current !== true && s.okStreak >= STREAK_TO_CHANGE) {
  432 |       s.current = true;
  433 |       setToolStatus(name, true, "Reachable");
  434 |     } else if (!okNow && s.current !== false && s.failStreak >= STREAK_TO_CHANGE) {
  435 |       s.current = false;
  436 |       setToolStatus(name, false, "Starting…");
  437 |     } else if (s.current === null) {
  438 |       // Only show "Checking…" while we don't have enough signal yet
  439 |       setToolStatus(name, null, "Checking…");
  440 |     }
  441 |   }
  442 | 
  443 |   function anyUnstable() {
  444 |     return Object.values(toolState).some(s => s.current !== true);
  445 |   }
  446 | 
  447 |   async function pollOnce() {
  448 |     const [attOk, defOk, calOk, wazOk] = await Promise.all([
  449 |       checkTool("attacker"),
  450 |       checkTool("defender"),
  451 |       checkTool("caldera"),
  452 |       checkTool("wazuh"),
  453 |     ]);
  454 | 
  455 |     applyStabilizedResult("attacker", attOk);
  456 |     applyStabilizedResult("defender", defOk);
  457 |     applyStabilizedResult("caldera",  calOk);
  458 |     applyStabilizedResult("wazuh",    wazOk);
  459 | 
  460 |     const next = anyUnstable() ? POLL_MS_UNSTABLE : POLL_MS_STABLE;
  461 |     setTimeout(pollOnce, next);
  462 |   }

  488 |     } catch { /* leave as-is */ }

  533 |   function copyVersionReport() {
  534 |     const d = _versionsData;
  535 |     const lines = ['GRFICSv3 Version Report', 'Generated: ' + new Date().toISOString(), ''];
  536 |     if (d && d.containers) {
  537 |       lines.push('Container'.padEnd(14) + 'Version'.padEnd(28) + 'Built'.padEnd(28) + 'Status');
  538 |       lines.push('-'.repeat(82));
  539 |       for (const c of d.containers) {
  540 |         lines.push(c.name.padEnd(14) + c.version.padEnd(28) + c.created.padEnd(28) + c.status);
  541 |       }
  542 |     } else {
  543 |       lines.push('(version data unavailable)');
  544 |     }
  545 |     navigator.clipboard.writeText(lines.join('\n')).then(() => {
  546 |       const btn = document.getElementById('copyReportBtn');
  547 |       if (!btn) return;
  548 |       btn.textContent = 'Copied!';
  549 |       setTimeout(() => { btn.textContent = 'Copy for bug report'; }, 2000);
  550 |     });
  551 |   }

  553 |   function isValidJson(text) {
  554 |     try {
  555 |       const obj = JSON.parse(text);
  556 |       // Basic sanity: must be a non-null object or array
  557 |       return obj !== null && (typeof obj === "object");
  558 |     } catch {
  559 |       return false;
  560 |     }
  561 |   }

  563 |   async function checkSimulationJson() {
  564 |     try {
  565 |       const res = await fetch("/data/index.php", { cache: "no-store" });
  566 |       if (!res.ok) return false;
  567 | 
  568 |       const text = await res.text();
  569 |       return isValidJson(text);
  570 |     } catch {
  571 |       return false;
  572 |     }
  573 |   }

  575 |   // Updates the main pill ONLY when it changes (prevents flicker)
  576 |   let simLastState = null; // null=unknown, true=running, false=not running
  577 |   async function refreshSimulationStatus() {
  578 |     const ok = await checkSimulationJson();
  579 | 
  580 |     if (ok === simLastState) return; // no change, don't touch UI
  581 | 
  582 |     simLastState = ok;
  583 |     if (ok) {
  584 |       setStatus("Simulation running", "#37d67a");
  585 |     } else {
  586 |       // Pick wording you like; this reads well during boot/restarts
  587 |       setStatus("Simulation starting…", "#ffd166");
  588 |     }
  589 |   }

NUMBERED ORIGINAL SOURCE

    1 | <?php
    2 | header('Content-Type: application/json');

    4 | 
    5 | $GRFICS = ['simulation', 'plc', 'EWS', 'HMI', 'kali', 'router', 'caldera', 'wazuh'];
    6 | 
    7 | function docker_get($path) {
    8 |     $sock = @stream_socket_client('unix:///var/run/docker.sock', $errno, $errstr, 3);
    9 |     if (!$sock) return null;
   10 |     stream_set_timeout($sock, 3);
   11 |     fwrite($sock, "GET $path HTTP/1.0\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n");
   12 |     $raw = '';
   13 |     while (!feof($sock)) $raw .= fread($sock, 8192);
   14 |     fclose($sock);
   15 |     $sep = strpos($raw, "\r\n\r\n");
   16 |     return $sep !== false ? json_decode(substr($raw, $sep + 4), true) : null;
   17 | }
   18 | 
   19 | $raw = docker_get('/containers/json?all=1');
   20 | $docker_available = $raw !== null;
   21 | $result = [];
   22 | 
   23 | if ($docker_available) {
   24 |     foreach ($raw as $c) {
   25 |         $name = ltrim($c['Names'][0] ?? '', '/');
   26 |         if (!in_array($name, $GRFICS)) continue;
   27 |         $labels = $c['Labels'] ?? [];
   28 |         $result[$name] = [
   29 |             'name'    => $name,
   30 |             'version' => $labels['org.opencontainers.image.version'] ?? 'unknown',
   31 |             'created' => $labels['org.opencontainers.image.created'] ?? 'unknown',
   32 |             'status'  => $c['State'] ?? 'unknown',
   33 |         ];
   34 |     }
   35 | }
   36 | 
   37 | // If Docker unavailable, at least show this container's own version from the baked-in file
   38 | if (!$docker_available) {
   39 |     $local = @file_get_contents('/etc/grfics-release');
   40 |     $data  = $local ? json_decode($local, true) : [];
   41 |     $result['simulation'] = [
   42 |         'name'    => 'simulation',
   43 |         'version' => $data['version'] ?? 'unknown',
   44 |         'created' => $data['created'] ?? 'unknown',
   45 |         'status'  => 'running',
   46 |     ];
   47 | }
   48 | 
   49 | foreach ($GRFICS as $name) {
   50 |     if (!isset($result[$name])) {
   51 |         $result[$name] = ['name' => $name, 'version' => '—', 'created' => '—', 'status' => 'not found'];
   52 |     }
   53 | }
   54 | ksort($result);
   55 | 
   56 | echo json_encode(['containers' => array_values($result), 'docker_available' => $docker_available]);

    6 | Requires the plant container to be running and reachable on 127.0.0.1:55555
    7 | (docker compose up -d simulation). Skipped automatically if it isn't.
    8 | 
    9 | Scenario:
   10 |   1. Freeze the pressure sensor (fault_injection.freeze) - its measured
   11 |      reading stops moving at a healthy, in-band value.
   12 |   2. Pin the feed valves open and the outflow valves shut via the normal L0
   13 |      control path (plant.apply) to drive TRUE pressure toward the hard limit,
   14 |      while confirming measured pressure never leaves its frozen band.
   15 |   3. Assert the interlock still trips (on truth), latches, forces the plant
   16 |      safe regardless of the commanded valves, and refuses reset_interlock()
   17 |      until truth is back inside the re-arm band - all while the frozen sensor
   18 |      is still reporting a healthy, in-band value throughout.
   19 | """
   20 | 
   21 | from __future__ import annotations
   22 | 
   23 | import socket
   24 | import time
   25 | 
   26 | import pytest
   27 | 
   28 | from contracts import ControlCommand
   29 | from l0_plant.plant_service import PlantService
   30 | from l0_plant import fault_injection as fi
   31 | from scripts.reset_plant import reset_and_settle
   32 | 
   33 | HOST, PORT = "127.0.0.1", 55555
   34 | 
   35 | 
   36 | def _plant_reachable() -> bool:
   37 |     try:
   38 |         with socket.create_connection((HOST, PORT), timeout=2):
   39 |             return True
   40 |     except OSError:
   41 |         return False
   42 | 
   43 | 
   44 | pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
   45 |     not _plant_reachable(),
   46 |     reason=f"plant not reachable on {HOST}:{PORT} (docker compose up -d simulation)",
   47 | )
   48 | 
   49 | 
   50 | @pytest.fixture
   51 | def plant():
   52 |     # A previous run can leave valves pinned open (or any other mid-transient
   53 |     # position) on the container, which silently changes how long this test's
   54 |     # drive-to-trip takes. Reset to the designed operating point first so the
   55 |     # test is reproducible regardless of what ran before it.
   56 |     reset_and_settle()
   57 |     svc = PlantService(HOST, PORT).start()
   58 |     fi.clear_all(svc.client)
   59 |     yield svc
   60 |     # best-effort cleanup so one test run doesn't poison the next
   61 |     try:
   62 |         fi.clear_all(svc.client)
   63 |         if svc.safety.tripped:
   64 |             svc.reset_interlock()
   65 |         svc.client.write_inputs({"e_stop": 0})
   66 |     finally:
   67 |         svc.stop()
   68 | 
   69 | 
   70 | DRIVE_OPEN = ControlCommand(f1_valve=100.0, f2_valve=100.0,
   71 |                              purge_valve=0.0, product_valve=0.0)
   72 | 
   73 | TRIP_TIMEOUT_S = 240
   74 | REARM_TIMEOUT_S = 180
   75 | POLL_S = 1.0
   76 | MEASURED_BAND_KPA = 5.0  # frozen sensor must not drift beyond this
   77 | 
   78 | 
   79 | def test_interlock_trips_on_truth_while_measured_stays_in_band(plant: PlantService):
   80 |     limits = plant.safety.limits
   81 | 
   82 |     baseline = plant.read()
   83 |     assert not baseline.scrammed, "interlock already tripped before the test started"
   84 | 
   85 |     # Freeze the pressure sensor: measured holds at its current (healthy) value.
   86 |     fi.freeze(plant.client, "tank_pressure")
   87 |     frozen_measured = plant.read().pressure
   88 | 
   89 |     # Drive truth toward the trip limit via the real control path (plant.apply),
   90 |     # polling until the interlock reports tripped - or we time out.
   91 |     state = plant.read()
   92 |     deadline = time.monotonic() + TRIP_TIMEOUT_S
   93 |     measured_samples = []
   94 |     while not state.scrammed:
   95 |         state = plant.apply(DRIVE_OPEN)
   96 |         measured_samples.append(state.pressure)
   97 |         assert abs(state.pressure - frozen_measured) <= MEASURED_BAND_KPA, (
   98 |             f"measured pressure drifted out of band while frozen: "
   99 |             f"{state.pressure:.1f} vs frozen {frozen_measured:.1f}"
  100 |         )
  101 |         if time.monotonic() > deadline:
  102 |             pytest.fail(
  103 |                 f"interlock never tripped within {TRIP_TIMEOUT_S}s; "
  104 |                 f"last truth pressure={state.truth['pressure']:.1f} kPa, "
  105 |                 f"measured stayed at ~{frozen_measured:.1f} kPa"
  106 |             )
  107 |         time.sleep(POLL_S)
  108 | 
  109 |     # It tripped - confirm it was truth that crossed the limit, not measured.
  110 |     assert state.truth["pressure"] >= limits.pressure_high
  111 |     assert state.pressure < limits.pressure_high, (
  112 |         "measured pressure also crossed the limit - the fault isn't masking anything, "
  113 |         "this run doesn't actually test the independent channel"
  114 |     )
  115 |     assert "pressure" in state.scram_reason.lower()
  116 |     assert plant.safety.tripped
  117 | 
  118 |     # Latching + override-proof: command the valves wide open again. The
  119 |     # interlock must force the plant safe regardless of what L1/L3 ask for.
  120 |     forced = plant.apply(DRIVE_OPEN)
  121 |     assert forced.scrammed
  122 |     assert forced.f1_valve_pos == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1.0)
  123 |     assert forced.f2_valve_pos == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1.0)
  124 |     assert forced.purge_valve_pos == pytest.approx(100.0, abs=1.0)
  125 |     assert forced.product_valve_pos == pytest.approx(100.0, abs=1.0)
  126 | 
  127 |     # Refuses to clear while truth is still outside the re-arm band.
  128 |     assert not plant.reset_interlock()
  129 |     assert plant.safety.tripped
  130 | 
  131 |     # Keep forcing safe (feeds shut, relief open) and wait for truth to fall
  132 |     # back inside the re-arm band.
  133 |     deadline = time.monotonic() + REARM_TIMEOUT_S
  134 |     rearmed_ok = False
  135 |     while time.monotonic() < deadline:
  136 |         s = plant.apply(DRIVE_OPEN)
  137 |         if plant.safety.can_reset(s.truth["pressure"], s.truth["liquid_level"]):
  138 |             rearmed_ok = True
  139 |             break
  140 |         time.sleep(POLL_S)
  141 |     assert rearmed_ok, f"truth pressure never fell back inside the re-arm band within {REARM_TIMEOUT_S}s"
  142 | 
  143 |     # Now the deliberate reset succeeds.
  144 |     assert plant.reset_interlock()
  145 |     assert not plant.safety.tripped
  146 | 
  147 |     # And measured pressure was in-band this whole time, including during the
  148 |     # trip and the force-safe window - the fault never had to "give up".
  149 |     assert max(measured_samples) - min(measured_samples) <= MEASURED_BAND_KPA
  150 | 
  151 | 
  152 | def test_reset_interlock_rejected_when_not_tripped_is_noop(plant: PlantService):
  153 |     # Sanity check on the untripped path: reset on a healthy plant is a no-op,
  154 |     # not an accidental trip-and-clear.
  155 |     assert not plant.safety.tripped
  156 |     assert not plant.reset_interlock()
  157 |     assert not plant.safety.tripped

    1 | """Fast tests for l1_regulator.L1Regulator against a toy TE-like plant (no container).
    2 | 
    3 | The toy plant only has the right SIGNS and rough magnitudes of the live plant
    4 | (pressure ~0.13 kPa/s per % purge and ~0.035 kPa/s per % of total feed, with a
    5 | 5 s lag; level integrates product inflow minus outflow; A responds to feed 2).
    6 | It exists to check loop structure - tracking, no sustained oscillation, no
    7 | windup, units, bumpless transfer - not to tune gains (that is done live).
    8 | """
    9 | from __future__ import annotations
   10 | 
   11 | from dataclasses import replace
   12 | 
   13 | from contracts import ControlCommand, PlantState, SupervisoryTargets
   14 | from l0_plant.provenance_gate import ProvenanceGate
   15 | from l1_regulator import (DESIGN_F1, DESIGN_F2, DESIGN_PRODUCT, DESIGN_PURGE, L1Regulator)
   16 | 
   17 | KEY = b"l1-test-key"
   18 | DESIGN = dict(pressure_sp=2700.6, level_sp=44.18, production_rate_sp=100.0, a_comp_sp=47.0)
   19 | DT = 0.1
   20 | 
   21 | 
   22 | class ToyPlant:
   23 |     def __init__(self):
   24 |         self.p, self.p_drive, self.l, self.q, self.a = 2700.6, 0.0, 44.18, 100.0, 0.47
   25 |         self.v = ControlCommand(DESIGN_F1, DESIGN_F2, DESIGN_PURGE, DESIGN_PRODUCT)
   26 | 
   27 |     def state(self) -> PlantState:
   28 |         return PlantState(pressure=self.p, level=self.l, f1_flow=0, f2_flow=0, purge_flow=0,
   29 |                           product_flow=self.q, a_in_purge=self.a, b_in_purge=0, c_in_purge=0,
   30 |                           f1_valve_pos=self.v.f1_valve, f2_valve_pos=self.v.f2_valve,
   31 |                           purge_valve_pos=self.v.purge_valve, product_valve_pos=self.v.product_valve, cost=0.0)
   32 | 
   33 |     def step(self, cmd: ControlCommand, dt: float = DT) -> None:
   34 |         self.v = cmd
   35 |         feed = (cmd.f1_valve + cmd.f2_valve) - (DESIGN_F1 + DESIGN_F2)
   36 |         drive = 0.035 * feed - 0.13 * (cmd.purge_valve - DESIGN_PURGE)
   37 |         self.p_drive += (drive - self.p_drive) * dt / 5.0                 # 5 s lag
   38 |         self.p += self.p_drive * dt
   39 |         inflow = 100.0 * cmd.f1_valve / DESIGN_F1
   40 |         outflow = 100.0 * cmd.product_valve / DESIGN_PRODUCT
   41 |         self.l += 0.004 * (inflow - outflow) * dt
   42 |         self.q += (outflow - self.q) * dt / 3.0
   43 |         self.a += 0.0004 * ((cmd.f2_valve - DESIGN_F2) - 20.0 * (self.a - 0.47)) * dt
   44 | 
   45 | 
   46 | def run(l1, plant, sp, seconds, trace=None):
   47 |     for _ in range(int(seconds / DT)):
   48 |         cmd = l1.regulate(SupervisoryTargets(**sp), plant.state(), DT)
   49 |         plant.step(cmd)
   50 |         if trace is not None:
   51 |             trace.append((plant.p, plant.l, plant.q, plant.a * 100, cmd))
   52 |     return plant
   53 | 
   54 | 
   55 | def fresh():
   56 |     plant = ToyPlant()
   57 |     l1 = L1Regulator(KEY)
   58 |     l1.bumpless(plant.state(), SupervisoryTargets(**DESIGN))
   59 |     return l1, plant
   60 | 
   61 | 
   62 | def test_holds_the_design_point():
   63 |     l1, plant = fresh()
   64 |     run(l1, plant, DESIGN, 300)
   65 |     assert abs(plant.p - 2700.6) < 1.0 and abs(plant.l - 44.18) < 0.05 and abs(plant.a - 0.47) < 0.001
   66 |     assert abs(plant.v.purge_valve - DESIGN_PURGE) < 1.0 and abs(plant.v.product_valve - DESIGN_PRODUCT) < 1.0
   67 | 
   68 | 
   69 | def _settles(xs, target, band, tail):
   70 |     """within band of target over the last `tail` samples, and no sustained oscillation
   71 |     (error sign changes over the tail are few)."""
   72 |     end = xs[-tail:]
   73 |     flips = sum((a - target) * (b - target) < 0 for a, b in zip(end, end[1:]))
   74 |     return all(abs(x - target) <= band for x in end) and flips <= 4
   75 |

================================================================================================
tests/test_safety_unit.py
Fast unit test for l0_plant/safety.py: pure logic, no container, no network. Feeds SafetyInterlock.evaluate()/reset() plain pressure/level numbers and checks trip, latch, override-while-tripped, and re-arm behavior. Should run in well under a second - if it doesn't, something is talking to the network. Regression specification; the test names and assertions below identify the behaviors protected. Fakes/mocks isolate dependencies unless the file explicitly requires the live simulator.

  264 | # ---- GRFICS steady_state() purge bug (b[3] out-of-bounds read) ------------------------
  265 | 
  266 | def test_design_purge_matches_te_steady_state_equations():
  267 |     """Re-derive the purge the simulator meant to set (TE_process.cc steady_state)."""
  268 |     import math
  269 |     import numpy as np
  270 |     from scripts.reset_plant import DESIGN_PURGE_VALVE_PCT
  271 |     P, xA, prod, kpar, nc, ya1, yb1 = 2700.0, 0.47, 100.0, 0.00117, 0.4, 0.485, 0.005
  272 |     Pa = P * xA
  273 |     Pc = (prod / (kpar * Pa ** 1.2)) ** (1 / nc)
  274 |     xC, xB = Pc / P, (P - Pa - Pc) / P
  275 |     f1, f2, purge = np.linalg.solve(np.array([[ya1, 1, -xA], [yb1, 0, -xB], [1 - ya1 - yb1, 0, -xC]]),
  276 |                                     np.array([prod, 0, prod]))
  277 |     assert purge / (0.352 * math.sqrt(P - 100)) == pytest.approx(DESIGN_PURGE_VALVE_PCT, abs=1e-4)
  278 |     assert f1 / 6.4046 == pytest.approx(ai.DESIGN_VALVES["f1"], abs=0.01)

    1 | """
    2 | Build the operator fine-tune dataset from REAL plant states.
    3 | 
    4 |   states.jsonl (collect_states.py)  --expert_policy-->  chat examples
    5 |       system    = operator role + the plant's real design targets and SIS limits
    6 |                   + the output JSON contract
    7 |       user      = the measured state as JSON (PlantState field names; never truth)
    8 |       assistant = setpoints + rationale JSON (the schema LLMOperator parses)
    9 | 
   10 | The prompt format (system text + state JSON) comes from l3_brain/prompt_format.py,
   11 | the same module LLMOperator serves with; the build asserts the system prompt is
   12 | byte-identical to the one served (train/serve match).
   13 | 
   14 | Split: exact-duplicate states are dropped, then each rollout is cut into
   15 | contiguous 10 s blocks and ~11% of every rollout's blocks go to val, so val
   16 | states are not interleaved 0.5 s neighbours of train states. If a rule ends up
   17 | with no val example, one train block containing it is moved to val.
   18 | 
   19 | Balance: within each split, every minority-rule example is kept and the
   20 | "hold design targets" rule is downsampled to at most --cap-design (default 40%)
   21 | of the split. Asserts no user-turn overlap between train and val.
   22 | 
   23 | Usage: python -m training.build_dataset [--cap-design 0.4] [--seed 0]
   24 | """

   49 |         return "hold:bad_reading"
   50 |     if rationale.startswith("In band"):
   51 |         return "design_targets"
   52 |     tags = []
   53 |     if "kPa from trip" in rationale:
   54 |         tags.append("pressure_backoff")
   55 |     if "low trip" in rationale:
   56 |         tags.append("level_low_backoff")
   57 |     if "high trip" in rationale:
   58 |         tags.append("level_high_backoff")

   62 | def histogram(name: str, values, lo: float, hi: float, bins: int, unit: str) -> None:

   64 |     counts = [0] * bins
   65 |     under = over = 0
   66 |     for v in values:

   69 |         elif v >= hi:

   80 |     if over:
   81 |         print(f"  {'>= ' + format(hi, 'g'):>15} | {'#' * max(1, round(40 * over / peak)):<40} {over}")

   90 |     design, lim, env = load_design_point(), TripLimits(), Envelope()
   91 |     sys_msg = system_prompt(design, lim)

   93 |                                       "the served prompt would not match training")
   94 | 
   95 |     # load, drop exact duplicate measured states, label each with the expert
   96 |     by_rollout, seen, raw_n = defaultdict(list), set(), 0
   97 |     with STATES.open() as f:

  109 |             r.update(user=user, assistant=out, rule=rule_of(why))

  111 | 
  112 |     # block split per rollout
  113 |     train_blocks, val_blocks = [], []
  114 |     for name, recs in by_rollout.items():
  115 |         blocks = [recs[i:i + BLOCK] for i in range(0, len(recs), BLOCK)]
  116 |         rng.shuffle(blocks)
  117 |         n_val = max(1, round(len(blocks) * VAL_FRAC))
  118 |         val_blocks += blocks[:n_val]
  119 |         train_blocks += blocks[n_val:]
  120 |     # every rule that exists at all gets at least one val block
  121 |     for rule in {r["rule"] for b in train_blocks for r in b}:
  122 |         if not any(r["rule"] == rule for b in val_blocks for r in b):
  123 |             b = next(b for b in train_blocks if any(r["rule"] == rule for r in b))
  124 |             train_blocks.remove(b)
  125 |             val_blocks.append(b)
  126 | 
  127 |     def balance(blocks):
  128 |         recs = [r for b in blocks for r in b]
  129 |         minority = [r for r in recs if r["rule"] != "design_targets"]
  130 |         design_recs = [r for r in recs if r["rule"] == "design_targets"]
  131 |         keep = int(len(minority) * a.cap_design / (1.0 - a.cap_design))
  132 |         rng.shuffle(design_recs)
  133 |         out = minority + design_recs[:keep]
  134 |         rng.shuffle(out)
  135 |         return out, len(design_recs)
  136 | 
  137 |     train, train_design_avail = balance(train_blocks)
  138 |     val, val_design_avail = balance(val_blocks)
  139 | 
  140 |     for split, recs in (("train", train), ("val", val)):
  141 |         with (HERE / f"{split}.jsonl").open("w") as f:
  142 |             for r in recs:
  143 |                 f.write(json.dumps({"messages": [
  144 |                     {"role": "system", "content": sys_msg},
  145 |                     {"role": "user", "content": r["user"]},
  146 |                     {"role": "assistant", "content": r["assistant"]}]}) + "\n")
  147 | 
  148 |     users = lambda p: {json.loads(l)["messages"][1]["content"] for l in p.open()}
  149 |     overlap = users(HERE / "train.jsonl") & users(HERE / "val.jsonl")
  150 |     assert not overlap, f"{len(overlap)} states in both train and val"
  151 | 
  152 |     m = [r["measured"] for r in train + val]
  153 |     print(f"real states collected: {raw_n} ({raw_n - len(seen)} exact duplicates dropped) "
  154 |           f"from {len(by_rollout)} rollouts")
  155 |     print(f"train.jsonl: {len(train)}   val.jsonl: {len(val)}   overlap: {len(overlap)}")
  156 |     print(f"'hold design targets' downsampled: train {train_design_avail} -> "
  157 |           f"{sum(r['rule'] == 'design_targets' for r in train)}, val {val_design_avail} -> "
  158 |           f"{sum(r['rule'] == 'design_targets' for r in val)} (cap {a.cap_design:.0%})")
  159 |     print("\nper-rollout (train / val):")
  160 |     rc = {s: Counter(r["rollout"] for r in recs) for s, recs in (("train", train), ("val", val))}
  161 |     for name in by_rollout:
  162 |         print(f"  {name:<32} {rc['train'][name]:5d} / {rc['val'][name]:4d}")
  163 |     print("\nexpert rule fired (train / val, % of train):")
  164 |     rules = {s: Counter(r["rule"] for r in recs) for s, recs in (("train", train), ("val", val))}
  165 |     all_rules = ["design_targets", "pressure_backoff", "level_high_backoff", "level_low_backoff",
  166 |                  "hold:tripped", "hold:bad_reading"]
  167 |     for rule in all_rules + sorted(set(rules["train"]) - set(all_rules)):
  168 |         print(f"  {rule:<36} {rules['train'][rule]:5d} / {rules['val'][rule]:4d}   "
  169 |               f"{100 * rules['train'][rule] / len(train):5.1f}%")
  170 | 
  171 |     print("\n--- coverage of the real measured states (train + val) ---")

  173 |     histogram("level", [x["level"] for x in m], 0, 100, 20, "%")
  174 |     histogram("product_flow", [x["product_flow"] for x in m], 0, 200, 20, "kmol/h")

  111 | def _cmd_of(rec) -> dict:

  113 |     actual positions, which is what L1 commanded in normal operation."""
  114 |     m = rec["measured"]

  118 | def _slope(xs, dt):

  120 |     tm = (n - 1) / 2.0
  121 |     return sum((i - tm) * (x - mean) for i, x in enumerate(xs)) / (sum((i - tm) ** 2 for i in range(n)) * dt)

  143 |     if mode == "frozen":

  145 |     if mode == "dropout":

  147 |     if mode == "noise":

  237 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------- synthesized faults
  238 | def _scale(ch: str, xs: List[float]) -> float:
  239 |     return {"pressure": 40.0, "level": 0.8, "a_in_purge": 0.01}.get(ch, 0.08 * max(sum(xs) / len(xs), 1.0))

  242 | def synth_sensor(base, ch: str, mode: str, mult: float, rng: random.Random) -> Optional[Example]:
  243 |     meas, cmd, ws = base
  244 |     xs = [m[ch] for m in meas]
  245 |     n, onset = len(xs), rng.randint(0, len(xs) // 2)
  246 |     s, sign = _scale(ch, xs), rng.choice((-1.0, 1.0))
  247 |     ys = list(xs)
  248 |     if mode == "frozen":
  249 |         if max(xs[onset:]) - min(xs[onset:]) < 0.25 * s:
  250 |             return None                                # a frozen value would be invisible here
  251 |         ys[onset:] = [xs[onset]] * (n - onset)
  252 |         score = 0.6
  253 |     elif mode == "drift":
  254 |         total = sign * mult * s
  255 |         ys = [x + (total * (i - onset) / max(1, n - 1 - onset) if i >= onset else 0.0) for i, x in enumerate(xs)]
  256 |         score = 0.35 + 0.12 * mult
  257 |     elif mode == "noise":
  258 |         ys = [x + (rng.gauss(0.0, 0.4 * mult * s) if i >= onset else 0.0) for i, x in enumerate(xs)]
  259 |         score = 0.35 + 0.12 * mult
  260 |     elif mode == "bias":
  261 |         ys = [x + (sign * mult * s if i >= onset else 0.0) for i, x in enumerate(xs)]
  262 |         score = 0.35 + 0.12 * mult
  263 |     else:                                              # dropout reads 0, like the sim's native mode
  264 |         frac = min(0.8, 0.1 + 0.1 * mult)
  265 |         for i in rng.sample(range(onset, n), max(1, int(frac * (n - onset)))):
  266 |             ys[i] = 0.0
  267 |         score = 0.5 + 0.5 * frac
  268 |     hi = 1.0 if ch == "a_in_purge" else float("inf")
  269 |     ys = [min(hi, max(0.0, y)) for y in ys]
  270 |     out = [{**m, ch: round(y, 4)} for m, y in zip(meas, ys)]
  271 |     return tel("sensor_fault", min(0.95, score), reason_sensor(ch, mode, ys, (n - onset) * F.SAMPLE_S), out, cmd, ws)
  272 | 
  273 | 
  274 | def synth_actuator(base, v: str, shape: str, rng: random.Random) -> Optional[Example]:
  275 |     meas, cmd0, ws = base
  276 |     act = [m[f"{v}_valve_pos"] for m in meas]
  277 |     n, onset = len(act), rng.randint(0, len(act) // 2)
  278 |     if shape == "stuck":                               # a still valve whose command walks away
  279 |         if max(act) - min(act) > 0.5:
  280 |             return None
  281 |         delta = rng.uniform(5.0, 30.0) * (1.0 if act[0] < 50.0 else -1.0)
  282 |         ramp = rng.randint(1, 5)
  283 |         cmd = [a + (delta * min(1.0, (i - onset + 1) / ramp) if i >= onset else 0.0) for i, a in enumerate(act)]
  284 |     elif shape == "gain":                              # opens only k x what it is told
  285 |         if sum(act) / n < 5.0:
  286 |             return None
  287 |         k = rng.uniform(0.5, 0.8)
  288 |         cmd = [min(100.0, a / k) if i >= onset else a for i, a in enumerate(act)]
  289 |     else:                                              # "offset" (unseen shape)
  290 |         c = rng.uniform(5.0, 20.0) * (1.0 if act[0] < 50.0 else -1.0)
  291 |         cmd = [min(100.0, max(0.0, a + c)) if i >= onset else a for i, a in enumerate(act)]
  292 |     gap = max(abs(a - c) for a, c in zip(act, cmd))
  293 |     if gap < 2.0:
  294 |         return None
  295 |     full = [{**c0, v: round(c, 4)} for c0, c in zip(cmd0, cmd)]
  296 |     return tel("actuator_fault", min(0.95, 0.4 + 0.015 * gap), reason_actuator(v, cmd, act), meas, full, ws)
  297 | 
  298 | 
  299 | def synthesized_telemetry(base, rng: random.Random, n_seen: int, n_unseen: int):
  300 |     pools = {"seen": defaultdict(list), "unseen": defaultdict(list)}
  301 |     plan = {"seen": (TRAIN_SENSOR_CH, (1.0, 3.0), TRAIN_VALVES, ("stuck", "gain"), n_seen),
  302 |             "unseen": (UNSEEN_SENSOR_CH, (4.0, 6.0), UNSEEN_VALVES + TRAIN_VALVES, ("offset",), n_unseen)}
  303 |     for split, (chans, mults, valves, shapes, n) in plan.items():
  304 |         src = base[split] or base["seen"]
  305 |         for _ in range(n * 6):
  306 |             if len(pools[split]["sensor_fault"]) >= n:
  307 |                 break
  308 |             ex = synth_sensor(rng.choice(src), rng.choice(chans), rng.choice(SENSOR_MODES), rng.uniform(*mults), rng)
  309 |             if ex:
  310 |                 pools[split]["sensor_fault"].append(ex)
  311 |         for _ in range(n * 10):
  312 |             if len(pools[split]["actuator_fault"]) >= n:
  313 |                 break
  314 |             v = rng.choice(valves)
  315 |             # unseen: f2 with any shape, the trained valves only with the held-out shape
  316 |             shape = rng.choice(("stuck", "gain", "offset")) if v in UNSEEN_VALVES else rng.choice(shapes)
  317 |             ex = synth_actuator(rng.choice(src), v, shape, rng)
  318 |             if ex:
  319 |                 pools[split]["actuator_fault"].append(ex)
  320 |     return pools
  321 | 
  322 | 
  323 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------- v2 proposals, verbatim
  324 | def v2_proposals(split: str, v2_dir: Path = V2_DIR) -> List[Example]:
  325 |     out = []
  326 |     for line in (v2_dir / f"observer_{split}.jsonl").open(encoding="utf-8"):
  327 |         m = json.loads(line)["messages"]
  328 |         if json.loads(m[1]["content"])["input"] == "proposals":
  329 |             out.append((json.loads(m[2]["content"])["label"], "proposals", m[1]["content"], m[2]["content"]))
  330 |     return out
  331 | 
  332 | 
  333 | # ---------------------------------------------------------------- assemble
  334 | def build(seed: int = 7, out_dir: Path = HERE, counts: dict = TELEMETRY_COUNTS, states: Path = STATES,
  335 |           obs_states: Path = OBS_STATES, v2_dir: Path = V2_DIR) -> dict:
  336 |     rng = random.Random(seed)
  337 |     tel_pools, base = recorded_telemetry(load_rollouts(states), load_rollouts(obs_states))
  338 |     need_seen = max(counts["train"].values()) + max(counts["val"].values())
  339 |     syn = synthesized_telemetry(base, rng, need_seen, max(counts["unseen"].values()))
  340 |     pools = {s: defaultdict(list) for s in ("seen", "unseen")}
  341 |     for src in (tel_pools, syn):
  342 |         for s in pools:
  343 |             for label, exs in src[s].items():
  344 |                 pools[s][label].extend(exs)
  345 | 
  346 |     splits = {"train": v2_proposals("train", v2_dir), "val": v2_proposals("val", v2_dir), "unseen": []}
  347 |     short = {}
  348 |     for label in ("normal", "excursion", "sensor_fault", "actuator_fault"):
  349 |         seen = list(pools["seen"][label])
  350 |         rng.shuffle(seen)
  351 |         nv, nt = counts["val"][label], counts["train"][label]
  352 |         val, rest = seen[:nv], seen[nv:]
  353 |         if len(rest) < nt:                             # short pool: resample (reported)
  354 |             short[label] = len(rest)
  355 |             rest = [rest[i % len(rest)] for i in range(nt)]
  356 |         splits["val"] += val
  357 |         splits["train"] += rest[:nt]
  358 |         uns = list(pools["unseen"][label])
  359 |         rng.shuffle(uns)
  360 |         splits["unseen"] += uns[:counts["unseen"][label]]
  361 |     train_users = {e[2] for e in splits["train"]}
  362 |     splits["unseen"] = [e for e in splits["unseen"] if e[2] not in train_users]
  363 |     out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  364 |     report = {}
  365 |     for name, exs in splits.items():
  366 |         rng.shuffle(exs)
  367 |         with (out_dir / f"observer_v3_{name}.jsonl").open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
  368 |             for label, kind, user, asst in exs:
  369 |                 f.write(json.dumps({"messages": F.messages(user, asst)}) + "\n")
  370 |         report[name] = {"n": len(exs), "by_label": dict(Counter(e[0] for e in exs)),
  371 |                         "by_input_label": {f"{k}/{lab}": n for (k, lab), n in
  372 |                                            sorted(Counter((e[1], e[0]) for e in exs).items())}}
  373 |     report["telemetry_train_pool_short"] = short
  374 |     report["_samples"] = [e for e in splits["train"] if e[1] == "telemetry"][:4]
  375 |     return report
  376 | 
  377 | 
  378 | def main() -> int:
  379 |     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
  380 |     ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=7)
  381 |     a = ap.parse_args()
  382 |     r = build(a.seed)
  383 |     samples = r.pop("_samples")
  384 |     print(json.dumps(r, indent=1))
  385 |     for label, _, user, asst in samples:
  386 |         print(f"\n[{label}] user ({len(user)} chars): {user[:500]}...\n  assistant: {asst}")
  387 |     return 0
  388 | 
  389 | 
  390 | if __name__ == "__main__":
  391 |     sys.exit(main())

    1 | """
    2 | Collect REAL telemetry for the L2 observer fine-tune: the simulator's NATIVE
    3 | sensor faults (fault_injection modes on several channels) and NATIVE actuator
    4 | faults (stuck valves, valve capacity degradation), with the commanded valve
    5 | positions recorded next to the measured state.
    6 | 
    7 | training/states.jsonl (collect_states.py) already covers normal operation,
    8 | excursions and a few sensor faults, but it never recorded what L1 commanded,
    9 | so an actuator fault (commanded != actual) cannot be seen in it. These rollouts
   10 | fill that gap and give the observer's unseen test set real, not synthesized,
   11 | fault windows.
   12 | 
   13 | Each rollout: reset to the operating point, run a fixed setpoint schedule (so
   14 | the valves have something to do), switch the fault on at FAULT_ON_S, record at
   15 | 2 Hz. Records stream to a temp file and are appended to
   16 | training/observer_states.jsonl only when the rollout completes; completed
   17 | rollouts are skipped on rerun.
   18 | 
   19 | Usage: python -m training.collect_observer_states [--only NAME] [--list]
   20 | """

    1 | """
    2 | Collect REAL plant states from the live GRFICS simulator for the operator
    3 | fine-tune. Nothing here is synthetic: every record is a read of the running
    4 | Tennessee-Eastman process.
    5 | 
    6 | Diversity comes from varying the CONDITIONS across rollouts - production /
    7 | pressure targets, setpoint steps, a pressure excursion, post-reset kicks, and
    8 | the simulator's native disturbances (sensor fault modes, valve capacity
    9 | degradation, a stuck valve). The plant is reset to its operating point before
   10 | every rollout; rollouts run one at a time.
   11 | 
   12 | Each rollout is regulated by the L1 stub, driven either by a fixed target
   13 | schedule or by the expert policy itself (on-policy states). The SIS interlock
   14 | (production limits) stays active throughout; if it trips, the trip is recorded
   15 | and the interlock is re-armed once the SIS channel allows.
   16 | 
   17 | Recording: the measured state at 2 Hz. Each line holds the measured PlantState
   18 | fields (what the operator sees) plus a `truth_eval_only` pressure/level pair
   19 | that is NOT used for training. Bounded memory: records stream to a temp file
   20 | and are appended to training/states.jsonl only when the rollout completes, so
   21 | an interrupted run never leaves a half rollout; completed rollouts are skipped
   22 | on rerun.
   23 | 
   24 | Also writes training/design_point.json: the settled operating point read from
   25 | the sim after the first reset (the expert's design targets).

  142 | def run_rollout(spec: dict, design: dict, scale: float) -> int:
  143 |     for attempt in (1, 2):           # first read after a restart can time out
  144 |         try:

  153 |     l1, brain = L1ControlStub(), _ExpertBrain(design)
  154 |     events = sorted(spec.get("events", []), key=lambda e: e[0])

   40 | def ask(model: str, user: str) -> str:

   50 | def score(model: str, cases: list) -> dict:
   51 |     """cases: list of (name, user_json, gold_dict)."""
   52 |     n_ok = hold_right = act_right = n_hold = n_act = 0
   53 |     errs, per = defaultdict(list), defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
   54 |     rows = []
   55 |     t0 = time.time()
   56 |     for name, user, gold in cases:
   57 |         text = ask(model, user)
   58 |         t, note = parse_llm_targets(text)
   59 |         try:
   60 |             raw = json.loads(text[text.find("{"):text.rfind("}") + 1])
   61 |             has_keys = isinstance(raw, dict) and all(k in raw for k in KEYS)
   62 |         except ValueError:
   63 |             has_keys = False
   64 |         ok = t is not None and has_keys
   65 |         gold_hold = all(gold[k] is None for k in KEYS)
   66 |         n_hold += gold_hold
   67 |         n_act += not gold_hold
   68 |         per[name]["n"] += 1
   69 |         row = {"case": name, "gold": gold, "raw": text[:300], "valid": ok}
   70 |         if ok:
   71 |             n_ok += 1
   72 |             pred = [getattr(t, k) for k in KEYS]
   73 |             pred_hold = all(v is None for v in pred)
   74 |             right = pred_hold == gold_hold
   75 |             hold_right += right and gold_hold
   76 |             act_right += right and not gold_hold
   77 |             per[name]["decision_right"] += right
   78 |             if not gold_hold and not pred_hold:
   79 |                 for k, v in zip(KEYS, pred):
   80 |                     if v is not None and gold[k] is not None:
   81 |                         e = abs(v - gold[k])
   82 |                         errs[k].append(e)
   83 |                         errs[(name, k)].append(e)
   84 |             row["pred"] = dict(zip(KEYS, pred))
   85 |         rows.append(row)
   86 |     mean = lambda v: round(sum(v) / len(v), 2) if v else None
   87 |     return {"model": model, "n": len(cases), "valid": n_ok,
   88 |             "hold_when_expert_holds": f"{hold_right}/{n_hold}",
   89 |             "act_when_expert_acts": f"{act_right}/{n_act}",
   90 |             "mae": {k: mean(errs[k]) for k in KEYS},
   91 |             "per_case": {c: {**v, "mae": {k: mean(errs[(c, k)]) for k in KEYS}} for c, v in per.items()},
   92 |             "secs_per_example": round((time.time() - t0) / max(1, len(cases)), 2), "rows": rows}
   93 |

    1 | """Validate conservative correction policy, then replay it on historical LLM outputs.
    2 | 
    3 | Validation determines activation. The historical test is a development comparison,
    4 | not a fresh blind test or a new inference run of the LLM weights.
    5 | """
    6 | import hashlib
    7 | import json

   13 | from training.train_telemetry_classifier import DEST, HISTORICAL, ROOT, load, metrics
   14 | 
   15 | 
   16 | def below_sensor_noise_floor(window: dict, reason: str) -> bool:
   17 |     """Reject small drift/noise claims, never dropouts, freezes or physical excursions.
   18 | 
   19 |     The fixed 0.5% window effect-size floor is validated on labeled held-out
   20 |     sensor examples before activation. This is not a safety permissive.
   21 |     """
   22 |     text = reason.lower()
   23 |     if any(word in text for word in ("frozen", "stuck", "drop", "zero", "constant", "flat")):
   24 |         return False
   25 |     if not any(word in text for word in ("drift", "nois", "jump")):
   26 |         return False
   27 |     channels = {"pressure": ("pressure",), "level": ("level",),
   28 |                 "f1_flow": ("feed 1", "feed1", "f1_flow"), "f2_flow": ("feed 2", "feed2", "f2_flow"),
   29 |                 "purge_flow": ("purge flow", "purge_flow"), "product_flow": ("product flow", "product_flow"),
   30 |                 "a_in_purge": ("a-in-purge", "analyzer", "composition")}
   31 |     matches = [(text.find(name), key) for key, names in channels.items() for name in names if name in text]
   32 |     if not matches:
   33 |         return False
   34 |     channel = min(matches)[1]
   35 |     xs = window.get(channel, [])
   36 |     if len(xs) < 4 or any(x is None or not math.isfinite(x) or x <= 0 for x in xs):
   37 |         return False
   38 |     # A high pressure or out-of-band level can never be dismissed by this check.
   39 |     if max(window.get("pressure", [float("inf")])) >= 2850 or not all(30 <= x <= 70 for x in window.get("level", [])):
   40 |         return False
   41 |     return max(xs) - min(xs) < .005 * (sum(xs) / len(xs))
   42 | 
   43 | 
   44 | def main():
   45 |     model = TelemetryClassifier()
   46 |     threshold = .7
   47 |     validation = load(OUT / "observer_v3_val.jsonl")
   48 |     accepted = []
   49 |     for window, gold, _ in validation:
   50 |         correction = model.correct(window, {"label": "normal"}, threshold)
   51 |         if correction["label"] != "normal":
   52 |             accepted.append((gold, correction["label"]))
   53 |     errors = sum(gold != predicted for gold, predicted in accepted)
   54 |     noise_rejections = []
   55 |     for line in (OUT / "observer_v3_val.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
   56 |         messages = json.loads(line)["messages"]
   57 |         gold = json.loads(messages[2]["content"])
   58 |         if gold["label"] == "sensor_fault":
   59 |             noise_rejections.append(below_sensor_noise_floor(json.loads(messages[1]["content"]), gold["reason"]))
   60 |     noise_errors = sum(noise_rejections)
   61 |     noise_passes = bool(noise_rejections) and noise_errors == 0
   62 |     enabled = len(accepted) >= 20 and errors == 0
   63 |     policy = {"enabled": enabled, "confidence_threshold": threshold, "validation_corrections": len(accepted),
   64 |               "sensor_noise_calibration": False, "noise_candidate_passed": noise_passes,
   65 |               "noise_validation_sensor_examples": len(noise_rejections), "noise_validation_missed_faults": noise_errors,
   66 |               "validation_correction_errors": errors, "validation_false_alarms": sum(gold == "normal" for gold, _ in accepted),
   67 |               "model_sha256": hashlib.sha256((DEST / "model.json").read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
   68 |               "scope": "telemetry only; correct normal LLM verdicts; never feeds authority"}
   69 |     baseline = json.loads((ROOT / "model/scram-observer-v3-gguf/eval_observer_test_unseen.json").read_text())
   70 |     rows = load(HISTORICAL)
   71 |     assert len(rows) == len(baseline["predictions"])
   72 |     assert all(gold == old["gold"] for (_, gold, _), old in zip(rows, baseline["predictions"]))
   73 |     changes = []
   74 |     predictions = {}

   81 |     replay_ms = 1000 * (time.perf_counter() - start) / len(rows)

   83 |     corrected_metrics.pop("mean_inference_ms")

    1 | """
    2 | Expert supervisory policy used to LABEL real plant states for the operator
    3 | fine-tune. expert(state) -> (setpoints, rationale).
    4 | 
    5 | Grounding (no invented numbers):
    6 |   * DESIGN targets are the plant's own settled operating point, read from the
    7 |     live simulator right after a reset (scripts/reset_plant.reset_and_settle)
    8 |     and saved to training/design_point.json by collect_states.py.
    9 |   * LIMITS are the SIS interlock's real trip / re-arm thresholds,
   10 |     l0_plant.safety.TripLimits() production defaults (pressure trips at
   11 |     3000 kPa and re-arms at 2800; level trips at 5% / 95% and re-arms inside
   12 |     15-85%).
   13 | 
   14 | The expert reads ONLY measured fields (what the operator sees through the basic
   15 | process instrumentation) - never `truth`. It emits setpoints, never valves, in
   16 | the same JSON schema LLMOperator parses (l3_brain/policy.parse_llm_targets).
   17 | `state` may be a PlantState or a plain dict with the same measured keys.
   18 | """
   19 | 
   20 | from __future__ import annotations
   21 | 
   22 | import json
   23 | import math
   24 | from pathlib import Path
   25 | from typing import Optional, Tuple
   26 |

   28 | 
   29 | HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
   30 | DESIGN_POINT_PATH = HERE / "design_point.json"
   31 | LIMITS = TripLimits()      # the production SIS thresholds, not a test override
   32 | 
   33 | # Back-off bands, in engineering units, placed relative to the real limits.
   34 | P_BACKOFF_START = LIMITS.pressure_rearm              # 2800 kPa: start easing at the re-arm line
   35 | P_BACKOFF_FULL = LIMITS.pressure_high - 50.0         # 2950 kPa: full back-off 50 kPa short of trip
   36 | L_LOW_BACKOFF_START = LIMITS.level_low_rearm + 10.0  # 25 %: start protecting inventory
   37 | L_LOW_BACKOFF_FULL = LIMITS.level_low_rearm - 5.0    # 10 %: full back-off 5 % above the 5 % trip
   38 | L_HIGH_BACKOFF_START = LIMITS.level_high_rearm - 10.0  # 75 %
   39 | L_HIGH_BACKOFF_FULL = LIMITS.level_high_rearm + 5.0    # 90 %: full back-off 5 % below the 95 % trip
   40 | P_SP_BACKOFF_KPA = 100.0      # how far the pressure setpoint drops at full back-off
   41 | PROD_BACKOFF_FRAC = 0.30      # fraction of design production shed at full back-off
   42 | L_SP_BACKOFF_PCT = 10.0       # how far the level setpoint moves at full back-off
   43 | 
   44 | 
   45 | def load_design_point(path: Path = DESIGN_POINT_PATH) -> dict:
