   47 |         raise FileNotFoundError(

   49 |             "the settled operating point from the live simulator and writes it there.")

   51 | 
   52 |

   54 |     return float(state[key] if isinstance(state, dict) else getattr(state, key))
   55 | 
   56 | 
   57 | def _ramp(x: float, start: float, full: float) -> float:
   58 |     """0 at `start`, 1 at `full` (either direction), clipped to [0, 1]."""
   59 |     if full == start:
   60 |         return 0.0
   61 |     return max(0.0, min(1.0, (x - start) / (full - start)))
   62 | 
   63 | 
   64 | def expert(state, design: Optional[dict] = None) -> Tuple[dict, str]:
   65 |     d = design or load_design_point()
   66 |     p0, l0, q0, a0 = d["pressure"], d["level"], d["production"], d["a_comp_pct"]
   67 |     hold = {"pressure_sp": None, "level_sp": None, "production_rate_sp": None, "a_comp_sp": None}
   68 | 
   69 |     scrammed = bool(state["scrammed"] if isinstance(state, dict) else state.scrammed)
   70 |     p, lv = _get(state, "pressure"), _get(state, "level")
   71 | 
   72 |     # Rule 1 - interlock tripped: the SIS owns the plant; ask for nothing until it re-arms.
   73 |     if scrammed:
   74 |         return hold, "Interlock tripped; holding all setpoints until the SIS re-arms."
   75 | 
   76 |     # Rule 2 - implausible reading (non-finite, or pressure/level reading <= 0 while the SIS
   77 |     # has not tripped, i.e. a dropped-out transmitter): do not steer on bad data, hold.
   78 |     if not (math.isfinite(p) and math.isfinite(lv)) or p <= 0.0 or lv <= 0.0:
   79 |         return hold, "Pressure or level reading implausible (sensor dropout); holding setpoints."
   80 | 
   81 |     sp = {"pressure_sp": p0, "level_sp": l0, "production_rate_sp": q0, "a_comp_sp": a0}
   82 |     notes = []
   83 | 
   84 |     # Rule 3 - pressure nearing the 3000 kPa trip: from the 2800 kPa re-arm line to 2950 kPa,
   85 |     # lower the pressure setpoint (vent more) and shed production (less feed) proportionally.
   86 |     wp = _ramp(p, P_BACKOFF_START, P_BACKOFF_FULL)
   87 |     if wp > 0:
   88 |         sp["pressure_sp"] = p0 - P_SP_BACKOFF_KPA * wp
   89 |         sp["production_rate_sp"] = q0 * (1.0 - PROD_BACKOFF_FRAC * wp)
   90 |         notes.append(f"pressure {p:.0f} kPa is {LIMITS.pressure_high - p:.0f} kPa from trip, "
   91 |                      f"backing off {wp:.0%}")
   92 | 
   93 |     # Rule 4 - level nearing the 5 % low trip: raise the level setpoint above design so the
   94 |     # level loop closes the product valve and inventory recovers.
   95 |     wl = _ramp(lv, L_LOW_BACKOFF_START, L_LOW_BACKOFF_FULL)
   96 |     if wl > 0:
   97 |         sp["level_sp"] = l0 + L_SP_BACKOFF_PCT * wl
   98 |         notes.append(f"level {lv:.1f}% is near the low trip, raising level setpoint")
   99 | 
  100 |     # Rule 5 - level nearing the 95 % high trip: lower the level setpoint (drain via product)
  101 |     # and shed production (less inflow); the larger of the pressure / level cut wins.
  102 |     wh = _ramp(lv, L_HIGH_BACKOFF_START, L_HIGH_BACKOFF_FULL)
  103 |     if wh > 0:
  104 |         sp["level_sp"] = l0 - L_SP_BACKOFF_PCT * wh
  105 |         sp["production_rate_sp"] = min(sp["production_rate_sp"], q0 * (1.0 - PROD_BACKOFF_FRAC * wh))
  106 |         notes.append(f"level {lv:.1f}% is near the high trip, lowering level setpoint and production")
  107 | 
  108 |     # Rule 6 - composition: always hold the design A-in-purge target; it has no SIS limit,
  109 |     # so it is never used as a back-off lever.
  110 |     sp = {k: round(v, 1) for k, v in sp.items()}
  111 | 
  112 |     # Rule 7 - otherwise: hold the design operating point.
  113 |     if not notes:
  114 |         return sp, (f"In band (P {p:.0f} kPa, L {lv:.1f}%); holding design targets.")
  115 |     text = "; ".join(notes)
  116 |     return sp, text[0].upper() + text[1:] + "."

    5 |   base     Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, 4-bit (Unsloth bnb-4bit), LoRA r=16

    7 |   format   every example is checked against l3_brain/prompt_format (the same

   23 |   python -m training.train_local                  # train, eval, export

    1 | """Train a CPU telemetry specialist and compare against unchanged recorded LLM results.
    2 | 
    3 | No test-set fitting or hyperparameter search. Exports plain JSON for Python-only inference.
    4 | Run: python -m training.train_telemetry_classifier

    6 | from __future__ import annotations
    7 | 
    8 | import hashlib
    9 | import json
   10 | import time
   11 | from collections import Counter
   12 | from pathlib import Path
   13 | 
   14 | import numpy as np
   15 | from sklearn.ensemble import ExtraTreesClassifier
   16 | 
   17 | from monitor.telemetry_classifier import FEATURE_VERSION, TelemetryClassifier, features

   24 | 
   25 | def load(path):
   26 |     rows = []
   27 |     for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
   28 |         turns = json.loads(line)["messages"]
   29 |         window, gold = json.loads(turns[1]["content"]), json.loads(turns[2]["content"])
   30 |         if window["input"] == "telemetry":
   31 |             rows.append((window, gold["label"], canonical(turns[1]["content"])))
   32 |     return rows
   33 | 
   34 | 
   35 | def metrics(rows, predict):
   36 |     confusion = {label: Counter() for label in ("normal", "excursion", "sensor_fault", "actuator_fault")}
   37 |     start = time.perf_counter()
   38 |     for window, gold, _ in rows:
   39 |         confusion[gold][predict(window)] += 1
   40 |     recalls = {label: confusion[label][label] / sum(confusion[label].values()) if confusion[label] else None
   41 |                for label in confusion}
   42 |     normals = sum(confusion["normal"].values())
   43 |     attacks = len(rows) - normals
   44 |     return {"n": len(rows), "accuracy": sum(confusion[k][k] for k in confusion) / len(rows),
   45 |             "per_class_recall": recalls,
   46 |             "false_alarm_rate": 1 - recalls["normal"] if normals else None,
   47 |             "detection_rate": 1 - sum(confusion[k]["normal"] for k in confusion if k != "normal") / attacks if attacks else None,
   48 |             "mean_inference_ms": 1000 * (time.perf_counter() - start) / len(rows),
   49 |             "confusion": confusion}
   50 | 
   51 | 
   52 | def main():
   53 |     splits = {s: load(OUT / f"observer_v3_{s}.jsonl") for s in ("train", "val", "unseen")}
   54 |     historical = load(HISTORICAL)
   55 |     # Defense in depth: reserve exact benchmark turns even when rebuilding future source pools.
   56 |     excluded = {row[2] for row in historical + splits["val"] + splits["unseen"]}
   57 |     train = [row for row in splits["train"] if row[2] not in excluded]
   58 |     if len(train) < 100:
   59 |         raise ValueError("not enough independent training telemetry")
   60 |     xs = np.array([features(row[0]) for row in train], dtype=np.float32)
   61 |     labels = [row[1] for row in train]
   62 |     model = ExtraTreesClassifier(n_estimators=64, max_depth=14, min_samples_leaf=2,
   63 |                                  class_weight="balanced", random_state=19, n_jobs=2)
   64 |     model.fit(xs, labels)
   65 |     trees = []
   66 |     for estimator in model.estimators_:
   67 |         tree = estimator.tree_
   68 |         probabilities = tree.value[:, 0, :]
   69 |         probabilities = probabilities / probabilities.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
   70 |         trees.append({"left": tree.children_left.tolist(), "right": tree.children_right.tolist(),
   71 |                       "feature": tree.feature.tolist(), "threshold": tree.threshold.tolist(),
   72 |                       "probabilities": probabilities.tolist()})
   73 |     DEST.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   74 |     output = {"feature_version": FEATURE_VERSION, "n_features": xs.shape[1], "classes": model.classes_.tolist(),
   75 |               "trees": trees, "training_manifest_sha256": hashlib.sha256((OUT / "manifest.json").read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
   76 |     path = DEST / "model.json"
   77 |     path.write_text(json.dumps(output, separators=(",", ":")), encoding="utf-8")
   78 |     runtime = TelemetryClassifier(path)
   79 |     # Verify that the dependency-free runtime matches the training library before evaluating it.
   80 |     assert [runtime.predict(row[0])["label"] for row in splits["val"]] == model.predict(
   81 |         np.array([features(row[0]) for row in splits["val"]], dtype=np.float32)).tolist()
   82 |     report = {"algorithm": "ExtraTrees", "seed": 19, "train_n": len(train), "model_bytes": path.stat().st_size,
   83 |               "extra_gpu_bytes": 0, "benchmark_fit_overlap": 0,
   84 |               "validation": metrics(splits["val"], lambda w: runtime.predict(w)["label"]),
   85 |               "clean_unseen": metrics(splits["unseen"], lambda w: runtime.predict(w)["label"]),
   86 |               "historical_unseen": metrics(historical, lambda w: runtime.predict(w)["label"])}
   87 |     baseline = json.loads((ROOT / "model/scram-observer-v3-gguf/eval_observer_test_unseen.json").read_text())
   88 |     report["historical_llm_baseline"] = {k: baseline[k] for k in ("n", "accuracy", "per_class_recall", "false_alarm_rate", "detection_rate")}
   89 |     report["comparison_note"] = "Same unchanged 480-example benchmark; historical LLM results, not a new LLM run. No model selection on this benchmark."
   90 |     (DEST / "evaluation.json").write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
   91 |     print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
   92 |

================================================================================================
training/scram_observer_finetune.ipynb
================================================================================================
Cell 1: markdown
# SCRAM - L2 observer v3 fine-tune (QLoRA on Qwen2.5-1.5B) - local, WSL2, RTX 3050 6 GB

Trains the **v3 L2 observer** (guardian): a 7-label classifier that reads either
the operator's last 6 **proposals** or a 15 s **telemetry window** and answers
`{"label", "score", "reason"}`.

v3 = v2 with the TELEMETRY side rebuilt: 16 samples over ~15 s (v2: 6 samples,
~2.6 s), every flow, and each valve's commanded vs actual position. The proposal
examples are v2's, verbatim.

Labels: `normal`, `excursion`, `sensor_fault`, `actuator_fault`,
`provenance_violation`, `rationale_mismatch`, `setpoint_drift`.

Data: `training/observer_v3_{train,val,unseen}.jsonl` (built by
`python -m training.build_observer_dataset`), formatted by
`monitor/observer_v3_format.py`, the module that will also serve the model.
`unseen` is telemetry only: held-out fault runs, channels, valve and fault shape.

Run from the repo root (or set `SCRAM_REPO`). Outputs go to `model/scram-observer-v3-gguf/`.

Cell 2: markdown
## 0. Setup (once) - WSL2 + CUDA + venv

**Windows side**
1. WSL2 with Ubuntu: `wsl --install -d Ubuntu-24.04` in an admin PowerShell, reboot;
   `wsl -l -v` must show VERSION 2.
2. NVIDIA driver with CUDA on WSL: the normal Windows Game Ready / Studio driver
   (R535 or newer). Do **not** install a Linux GPU driver inside WSL. Inside WSL,
   `nvidia-smi` must list the RTX 3050.
3. Optional, more RAM for WSL: `%UserProfile%/.wslconfig` with `[wsl2]`,
   `memory=10GB`, `swap=8GB`, then `wsl --shutdown`.

**Inside WSL (Ubuntu)**
```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3-venv python3-dev build-essential cmake git curl libcurl4-openssl-dev
python3 -m venv ~/scram-observer-venv && source ~/scram-observer-venv/bin/activate
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install unsloth
pip install --no-deps "xformers<0.0.27" "trl<0.12.0" peft accelerate bitsandbytes
pip install jupyter nbconvert ipykernel
```
`cmake` / `build-essential` / `libcurl` are for the llama.cpp build Unsloth runs in
section 6 to produce the GGUF.

**Launch** (inside WSL, repo on the Windows drive):
```bash
source ~/scram-observer-venv/bin/activate
cd /mnt/c/Users/<you>/Downloads/SCRAM-Project
jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute training/scram_observer_finetune.ipynb --output scram_observer_finetune.run.ipynb --ExecutePreprocessor.timeout=-1
```
or `jupyter lab` and run the cells.

**Before launching:** close GPU-using Windows apps (browsers with hardware
acceleration, games, video players, Ollama). Expected peak VRAM at these settings
is ~4-4.5 GB of the 6 GB (4-bit base ~1.3 GB; LoRA weights + paged 8-bit Adam
~0.3 GB; activations for a 2,560-token sequence with Unsloth gradient
checkpointing and chunked cross-entropy ~2-2.5 GB), leaving ~1.5 GB headroom. The
Windows desktop alone can hold 0.5-1.5 GB, so that headroom is real but thin.

Cell 4: markdown
## 1. Load the base model (4-bit)
Same base as the operator. 4-bit weights are what make a 6 GB GPU possible (v2 was
trained in fp16 and peaked at ~10 GB). The longest examples (telemetry) are ~2,450
tokens with the system prompt, so MAX_SEQ is 2560; section 3 asserts nothing is
truncated.

Cell 5: code
from unsloth import FastLanguageModel

MODEL = "unsloth/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-bnb-4bit"
MAX_SEQ = 2560

model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    model_name     = MODEL,
    max_seq_length = MAX_SEQ,
    load_in_4bit   = True,
    dtype          = None,   # auto: bf16 on an RTX 30xx
)

## 3. Load and format the data
Each line is `{"messages":[system, user, assistant]}`.

from datasets import load_dataset
from unsloth.chat_templates import get_chat_template

tokenizer = get_chat_template(tokenizer, chat_template="qwen-2.5")

def to_text(ex):
    return {"text": tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
        ex["messages"], tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=False)}

train_ds  = load_dataset("json", data_files=str(FILES["train"]),  split="train").map(to_text)
val_ds    = load_dataset("json", data_files=str(FILES["val"]),    split="train").map(to_text)
unseen_ds = load_dataset("json", data_files=str(FILES["unseen"]), split="train")
print(train_ds, val_ds, unseen_ds)
lens = [len(tokenizer(t)["input_ids"]) for t in train_ds["text"]]
print("token length: max", max(lens), "mean", sum(lens) // len(lens))
assert max(lens) < MAX_SEQ, "raise MAX_SEQ: an example would be truncated"
print("\n--- one formatted example ---\n")
print(train_ds[0]["text"][:1500])

Cell 10: markdown
## 4. Train (1 epoch, responses only)
One epoch like v2: the classes are templated, so more passes mostly memorise.
`train_on_responses_only` puts the loss on the assistant JSON only.
6 GB settings: batch 1 x grad-accum 8 (the same effective batch 8 as the Colab
version) and paged 8-bit AdamW (optimizer state can page to CPU instead of OOM).

Cell 11: code
from trl import SFTTrainer, SFTConfig
from unsloth.chat_templates import train_on_responses_only

trainer = SFTTrainer(
    model         = model,
    tokenizer     = tokenizer,
    train_dataset = train_ds,
    eval_dataset  = val_ds,
    args = SFTConfig(
        dataset_text_field          = "text",
        max_seq_length              = MAX_SEQ,
        per_device_train_batch_size = 1,
        gradient_accumulation_steps = 8,
        warmup_steps                = 10,
        num_train_epochs            = 1,
        learning_rate               = 2e-4,
        fp16                        = not torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),
        bf16                        = torch.cuda.is_bf16_supported(),
        logging_steps               = 10,
        eval_strategy               = "steps",
        eval_steps                  = 150,
        optim                       = "paged_adamw_8bit",
        weight_decay                = 0.01,
        lr_scheduler_type           = "linear",
        seed                        = 3407,
        output_dir                  = str(REPO / "training" / "_observer_v3_outputs"),
        report_to                   = "none",
        save_strategy               = "steps",   # checkpoint so a stopped run resumes, not restarts
        save_steps                  = 50,
        save_total_limit            = 2,
    ),
)

trainer = train_on_responses_only(
    trainer,
    instruction_part = "<|im_start|>user\n",
    response_part    = "<|im_start|>assistant\n",
)

import glob
ckpts = sorted(glob.glob(str(REPO / "training" / "_observer_v3_outputs" / "checkpoint-*")),
               key=lambda p: int(p.rsplit("-", 1)[1]))
print("resuming from", ckpts[-1] if ckpts else "scratch")
stats = trainer.train(resume_from_checkpoint=ckpts[-1] if ckpts else None)
print(stats)
print("peak VRAM reserved", round(torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved() / 2**30, 2), "GB")
model.save_pretrained(str(OUT / "lora")); tokenizer.save_pretrained(str(OUT / "lora"))

Cell 12: markdown
## 5. Evaluate on val AND unseen
Same report shape as v2's `eval_observer_val.json` so the numbers compare:
accuracy, valid-JSON rate, per-class recall, detection rate (attack classes
flagged as any attack), false-alarm rate (normal flagged), confusion, and the
same metrics split by input type. `EVAL_N = None` runs every example (val + unseen
~1-1.5 h on a 3050); set e.g. 300 for a quick look. Reports go to `OUT`.

Cell 13: code
import random
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
FastLanguageModel.for_inference(model)

LABELS = ["normal","excursion","sensor_fault","actuator_fault",
          "provenance_violation","rationale_mismatch","setpoint_drift"]
EVAL_N = None

def ask(messages_wo_answer):
    prompt = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(messages_wo_answer, tokenize=False, add_generation_prompt=True)
    ids = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda")
    out = model.generate(**ids, max_new_tokens=96, do_sample=False, pad_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id)
    return tokenizer.decode(out[0][ids["input_ids"].shape[1]:], skip_special_tokens=True)

def parse(text):   # same rules as monitor/observer_v2_format.parse
    s, e = text.find("{"), text.rfind("}")
    if s < 0 or e <= s: return None
    try: obj = json.loads(text[s:e+1])
    except ValueError: return None
    return obj.get("label") if isinstance(obj, dict) and obj.get("label") in LABELS else None

def metrics(rows):
    if not rows: return None
    n = len(rows); valid = sum(r["pred"] is not None for r in rows)
    gold = Counter(r["gold"] for r in rows)
    recall = {c: (sum(r["gold"] == c and r["pred"] == c for r in rows) / gold[c]) if gold[c] else None
              for c in LABELS}
    att = [r for r in rows if r["gold"] != "normal"]; nor = [r for r in rows if r["gold"] == "normal"]
    conf = defaultdict(Counter)
    for r in rows: conf[r["gold"]][r["pred"] or "invalid"] += 1
    return {"n": n, "valid_json": valid / n, "accuracy": sum(r["gold"] == r["pred"] for r in rows) / n,
            "per_class_recall": recall,
            "detection_rate": (sum(r["pred"] not in (None, "normal") for r in att) / len(att)) if att else None,
            "false_alarm_rate": (sum(r["pred"] not in (None, "normal") for r in nor) / len(nor)) if nor else None,
            "n_normal": len(nor), "confusion": {g: dict(c) for g, c in conf.items()}}

def evaluate(ds, split):
    idx = list(range(len(ds)))
    if EVAL_N:
        random.Random(0).shuffle(idx); idx = idx[:EVAL_N]
    rows = []
    for i in idx:
        msgs = ds[i]["messages"]
        raw = ask(msgs[:2])
        rows.append({"gold": json.loads(msgs[2]["content"])["label"], "pred": parse(raw), "raw": raw,
                     "kind": json.loads(msgs[1]["content"])["input"]})
    rep = {"split": split, **metrics(rows),
           "by_kind": {"proposals": metrics([r for r in rows if r["kind"] == "proposals"]),
                       "telemetry": metrics([r for r in rows if r["kind"] == "telemetry"])},
           "predictions": [{"gold": r["gold"], "pred": r["pred"], "raw": r["raw"]} for r in rows]}
    json.dump(rep, open(OUT / f"eval_{split}.json", "w"), indent=1)
    fa = rep["false_alarm_rate"]
    print(f"== {split}: n={rep['n']} acc={rep['accuracy']:.3f} valid={rep['valid_json']:.3f} "
          f"detect={rep['detection_rate']:.3f} false_alarm={fa if fa is None else round(fa, 3)}")
    for c in LABELS: print(f"   {c:20s} recall={rep['per_class_recall'][c]}")
    for k, m in rep["by_kind"].items():
        if m: print(f"   by input {k:10s} n={m['n']} acc={m['accuracy']:.3f}")
    return rep

rep_val = evaluate(val_ds, "observer_val")
rep_unseen = evaluate(unseen_ds, "observer_test_unseen")

Cell 14: markdown
## 6. Export GGUF for Ollama
Merges the LoRA adapter into the base and quantises to `q4_k_m` (Unsloth builds
llama.cpp the first time - needs cmake / build-essential from section 0), then
writes a Modelfile with the observer system prompt taken from a training example,
so Ollama serves exactly what was trained. `num_ctx 3072`: v3 telemetry prompts
are ~2,450 tokens.

Cell 15: code
import glob, shutil
GGUF_DIR = str(OUT)
model.save_pretrained_gguf(GGUF_DIR, tokenizer, quantization_method="q4_k_m")
gguf = os.path.basename(sorted(glob.glob(GGUF_DIR + "/*.gguf"), key=os.path.getsize)[0])   # the q4_k_m one
sys_prompt = json.loads(open(FILES["train"]).readline())["messages"][0]["content"]
Q3 = chr(34) * 3
modelfile = ("FROM ./" + gguf + "\n"
             "PARAMETER temperature 0\n"
             "PARAMETER num_ctx 3072\n"
             "SYSTEM " + Q3 + sys_prompt + Q3 + "\n")
open(GGUF_DIR + "/Modelfile", "w").write(modelfile)
json.dump(stats.metrics, open(GGUF_DIR + "/train_metrics.json", "w"), indent=1)
zip_path = shutil.make_archive(str(OUT.parent / "scram-observer-v3"), "zip", GGUF_DIR)
print("wrote", zip_path, "and", GGUF_DIR)

Cell 16: markdown
## 7. Register with Ollama (Windows)
```powershell
cd model/scram-observer-v3-gguf
ollama create scram-observer-v3 -f Modelfile
```
Compare with v2 by input type: v2 telemetry accuracy was 71.3% val / 41.6% unseen
(sensor_fault 27.9% / 0%, actuator_fault 14.3%); the proposal side should stay
~100% / ~98%. v3 is wired in as its own step afterwards (own format module +
parity gate).
